stories.Headline: OpenAI launches AI agents to penetration test web apps and automate security patches
stories.Summary:
OpenAI launched Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory on Thursday, November 12, during its Cyber at the Frontier event. These two new security products use AI agents to penetration test web applications and prepare security patches. The tools extend the Daybreak cyber defense program that the company had previously launched earlier this year. Daybreak Red Team uses multiple agents in isolated environments to confirm if reported vulnerabilities are actually exploitable. Daybreak Defense Factory traces these vulnerabilities through code and opens draft GitHub pull requests for engineer approval.

The Red Team tool accepts early access requests and tests findings from bug bounties, disclosure reports, and code scanners. Defense Factory is a preview plugin in ChatGPT for workspaces with Daybreak access, though OpenAI has not published pricing. This system imports vulnerability data from Snyk, Endor Labs, and Wiz, and it can scan connected GitHub repositories. A Guardian review layer enforces testing boundaries to keep automated attackers inside the scope a customer has authorized. Engineers can edit patches using the Codex coding agent before they are deployed to production.

OpenAI President Greg Brockman said companies will only be secure based on the frontier models they use for defense. He stated that organizations need to reorient their security practices around what these models can do, though fundamentals remain important. Nancy Wang, who leads cyber applied AI, described the Red Team as superhuman pen testing at an automated scale. She noted that engineers receive a merge ready pull request along with a test showing that the fix works. The company stated there is a limited window to use frontier models to secure software.

A coalition of nonprofits including Public Citizen and the Heat Initiative filed a lawsuit in San Francisco Superior Court. They seek to stop OpenAI, Google, Meta, Anthropic, and SpaceX from deploying AI systems more capable than existing models. The lawsuit cites AI agents gaining unauthorized access to an Australian government portal and accessing Hugging Face. Other affected parties include JPMorgan Chase, which signed for Codex and cyber models, and Mozilla, which saw Firefox bugs. The lawsuit alleges that these AI companies are developing technology that poses catastrophic risks to the public.

The tools utilize GPT 6 Cyber, a restricted model rated Critical for cybersecurity under the company's own Preparedness Framework. In a mid October run, this model flagged 2,308 potential Linux kernel flaws and reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities. It developed local privilege escalation exploits for 948 of them, which is five times more than GPT 5.6 Sol. The model also found 81 high severity Firefox bugs and exploited 48.5 percent of vulnerabilities on the ExploitGym benchmark. This performance exceeds the 32.1 percent rate achieved by the GPT 5.6 Cyber model.

OpenAI promised to expand GPT 6 Cyber access to all Daybreak Red customers, but the company provided no date. Rival labs like Google and Anthropic are also pitching to defenders, having found a critical HTTP 2 flaw. Benchmarking firm Vals found a free DeepSeek model nearly matched OpenAI's restricted model on network hacking tasks. CloudSEK reported that Kazakhstan linked hackers used a DeepSeek AI agent against governments in Central Asia. On November 12, Trump's AI task force met to discuss the threat of AI powered cyberattacks.

stories.Headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen for agentic workflows with a 1M token window
stories.Summary:
Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 13, 2026, a proprietary model from Google DeepMind for coding and agentic work. Google calls it its daily driver for agentic workflows, and it sits below the frontier models Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon. It is a closed-weights model served through the Gemini API and Google products, adapted from Gemini 4 Carbon. Google does not disclose parameter count, architecture, training hardware or serving hardware. The knowledge cutoff is March 2026.

The model has a 1,048,576-token unified window shared by input, thinking and output tokens, and synchronous output caps at 65,536 tokens. Input covers text, images, audio, video, PDFs, tables and charts, and output is text. Developers set thinking_level inside generation_config to low, medium, high or the new xhigh, with high as the default and a minimal setting now returning an error. The API price is $1.50 per 1M input tokens and $7.50 per 1M output tokens, flat across the full window, with output pricing including thinking tokens. Implicit caching cuts input to $0.075 per 1M for prompts of 4,096 tokens or more, and explicit caching is not supported.

Google reports that Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at high and 54 at xhigh, above Argon's 50 on Index v5.0. Google says it finishes tasks 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at the default high level, and in partner tests it ran 2x to 2.8x faster with 12% to 23% fewer tokens. Google reports more than 5x fewer fabricated claims than 3.8 Flash, a 96.7% score on an internal agent honesty evaluation, and 2.3x more resilience to indirect prompt injection on Gray Swan's benchmark. The model card warns that higher thinking levels use more tokens. Google says the model ID is gemini-4-hydrogen and it is live in the Gemini API, Google AI Studio on all tiers, Android Studio, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search and Sheets, with Antigravity access requiring Google AI Pro or Ultra.

Artificial Analysis said Hydrogen scores 54 on its Intelligence Index at xhigh, 1 point behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max) and 4 points ahead of Gemini 4 Argon (high). It said Hydrogen costs about 32% of Sonnet's cost per task but about 2.5x that of GPT-6.1 Sol, and that at high reasoning it matches Argon's intelligence for about 19% of the cost per task. It recorded an 8% hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience, against 43% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and 52% for GPT-6.1 Sol (max), and a tied #1 score of 33% all-pass on GDP.pdf at medium reasoning. It said Hydrogen scores 54% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 50% on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, against 64% and 53% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and 56% and 58% for GPT-6.1 Sol (max). It said cost per task falls from $3.16 at xhigh to $1.87 at high, $0.80 at medium and $0.29 at low, which score 41 and 27 on the Intelligence Index.

Google reports 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 versus 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash, 52.3% on Vals Tax Agent Bench ranked #1 overall, and 55.8% on Vals Legal Research Bench tied for #1. Google says Hydrogen ranks only #5 on Agent Arena and costs 2x Gemini 3.8 Flash's current introductory price. In Google Antigravity, an Orchestrator option switches models inside one task, with Carbon exploring, resolving ambiguity and planning while Hydrogen edits files, updates packages and runs tests and hands control back to Carbon when it hits friction. Google says this pairing reached near-Carbon task success rates on Terminal-Bench 4.1, used 24% less quota and finished 19% faster than Carbon alone, and the Antigravity SDK exposes the same split for custom multi-agent systems. Artificial Analysis said xhigh nearly doubles output tokens compared with high for a 3 point gain in Intelligence, and that Hydrogen has an output speed of about 200 output tokens per second.

Gemini 3.8 Flash costs $0.75/$3.75 until December 31, 2026, then rises to $1.50/$7.50 from January 1, 2027, matching Hydrogen. Argon costs $2/$10 until November 30, 2026, then $4/$20. Artificial Analysis said Hydrogen is Google DeepMind's third new model in six weeks and that xhigh is the first reasoning level above high on a Gemini model. It said xhigh lifts Terminal-Bench-Science from 41% at high to 50% but makes no difference on Terminal-Bench 4.0, and that science scores range from 46% in earth sciences to 53% in physical sciences. It said graders rate Hydrogen's presentation above other Gemini models, including Carbon, on AA-Briefcase. It said with high, medium and low reasoning effort Hydrogen is on the Time per Task vs. Intelligence Pareto frontier.

Migration from 3.8 Flash requires removing temperature, top_p and top_k. Vertex AI is not mentioned in the launch posts. The articles do not say when or whether Hydrogen will reach Vertex AI, and they do not give its parameter count, architecture or serving hardware.

stories.Headline: Cadence joins US Genesis Mission Consortium to supply AI design and simulation tools to national labs
stories.Summary:
Cadence joined the US Genesis Mission Consortium on November 15, 2026, to help advance scientific discovery through artificial intelligence. This public-private partnership is led by the US Department of Energy to speed up energy innovation and national security. The company will provide AI-enabled design and simulation technologies to support various research priorities across several national laboratories. This collaboration aims to integrate high-performance computing and advanced engineering technologies into the broader scientific research ecosystem. The partnership allows Cadence to apply its system design and analysis capabilities to a wider range of scientific applications.

The Genesis Mission was launched by an executive order in November 2025 and is led by Dr. Darío Gil. It aims to double the productivity of American science and engineering within a decade using 17 National Laboratories. Cadence will focus on advanced microelectronics, quantum and superconducting systems, AI-driven scientific workflows, and data centre energy efficiency. The consortium involves federal agencies, industry, and academia to tackle challenges in biotechnology, nuclear energy, and materials science. It links the top supercomputers, experimental facilities, and unique datasets of the country to strengthen overall technological competitiveness.

Tom Beckley, senior vice president at Cadence, stated that AI-driven design and physics-based simulation will reshape how critical systems are built. He mentioned that this includes everything from advanced semiconductors to AI factories and next-generation physical AI and scientific applications. Dr. Jeffrey S. Vetter from Oak Ridge National Laboratory said the mission is an extraordinary opportunity to accelerate discovery. He noted that bringing advanced engineering tools into research workflows helps the labs deliver breakthroughs that matter for the nation. Both leaders emphasized that these tools are essential for maintaining the scientific leadership of the United States.

The initiative affects researchers who rely on large-scale computing and complex simulations to accelerate their experimentation and validation processes. Academic partners are also involved as the consortium works to build a specialized AI-enabled engineering workforce through training. The collaboration extends to various fields including advanced manufacturing, quantum information science, and the development of new materials. By integrating specialized tools with national infrastructure, the project aims to improve the speed of scientific breakthroughs. This effort is designed to support the broader goal of strengthening the scientific and technological competitiveness of America.

Cadence already collaborates with the DOE and National Nuclear Security Administration at several sites, including Sandia and Lawrence Livermore. Other existing partners include Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Argonne, Brookhaven, and the NASA Ames Research Center. These previous collaborations used AI-enabled technologies for large-scale engineering analysis, verification, and simulation aligned with national security priorities. The company's broader strategy combines agentic AI, digital twins, and high-performance computing across semiconductor design and physical AI systems. These established relationships provide a foundation for the new contributions Cadence will make to the Genesis Mission.

Cadence will now provide subject-matter expertise to help scope and pilot AI model development, data standards, and high-performance computing. The firm will offer access to 3D-IC workflows, advanced packaging, digital twins, multiphysics simulation, and AI-enabled EDA and SDA tools. It will also support the integration of these workflows into laboratory environments through AI performance benchmarking and reproducible packaging. The company will work with academic partners on curricula to train the next generation of AI-enabled engineering professionals. The articles leave open the specific timelines for these pilots and the exact results of the workforce training.

stories.Headline: Google blocks K-12 search unless districts opt into AI
stories.Summary:
Google announced this week that starting in January it plans to block K-12 students from using its search engine unless districts opt into the company's AI-generated version of it. Chris Phillips, Google's vice president and general manager of education, said on Monday during a virtual briefing that a school not comfortable with that and simply wanting AI off has the choice to not have Search at all. The announcement came as districts across California debate restrictions on artificial intelligence and technology use in the classroom. Los Angeles Unified, the state's largest district, has already placed restrictions on generative AI. Google's decision could complicate such efforts, particularly because schools rely on the company's digital workspace for daily lessons and its search engine for research and assignments.

Google will block both its integrated AI tool and Google search for K-12 students unless a district decides to turn either feature on, with no option for a search engine without AI integration. The company said in a blog post on Tuesday that it will update its search function for schools by making its "Guided Learning" AI product the default. The company said Guided Learning will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don't get quick answers to schoolwork. Google also clarified in a post on X on Tuesday that schools can turn off its separate AI products, Gemini and Gemini Notebook, and use search, but AI Mode and AI Overview will remain integrated into Google search. Google announced that early next year its Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search will automatically be turned off for school districts and administrators will have to choose to opt into the features.

Phillips said on Monday during a virtual briefing that if a school is not comfortable with that and simply wants AI off, then they have the choice to not have Search on at all. Google said in its Tuesday blog post that it will update its search function for schools by making Guided Learning the default. The company said in its post on X that it knows there's concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork and that schools have told the company they want control. The post said that is exactly why Google is making these changes today to address the feedback it has heard from educators in recent months. The post also said Google will continue to engage deeply with educators to ensure it is giving schools more choice, more controls, and improved Search for learning.

Lila Byock, founder of parent advocacy group Schools Beyond Screens, described Google's decision as an act of "bullying" and said educational value, not shareholder value, must determine the technology used by students. Byock said Google forced its AI products into classrooms and parents fought back, and that the company's hostile ultimatum is a desperate attempt to maintain its stranglehold on public education. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into public schools and that no corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Yvette Renteria, chief program officer at Common Sense Media, said students use Google search and it helps with media literacy, understanding, evaluating and analyzing resources, which are so crucial to learning. Renteria said not having that as an option seems like a missed opportunity and taking it away altogether also seems like a missed opportunity.

About three-quarters of American teens and tweens use or interact with the AI summaries in search results, according to a recent report by Common Sense Media. In a series of 180 tests, Common Sense Media researchers found that Google's AI Mode completed students' homework assignments for them every time. The AI feature also invented fake answers to questions, returned different answers to the same questions and cited unreliable sources such as Reddit, Facebook and YouTube. Common Sense Media researchers have not reviewed Google's Guided Learning mode. An estimated 60,000 K-12 schools use Google Workplace, meaning teachers and students have integrated their work in Google emails, sheets and slides, according to Tech & Learning.

Around 93 percent of U.S. public schools either use or plan on using Google Chromebooks in classrooms, About Chromebooks reported. Rory Mir, director of community tech engagement at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, said the tricky thing with schools is that they enter into long contracts, and there is a lot of training that goes into making sure educators know how to use these different tools. Mir said the switch comes with real monetary costs as well as labor costs and disruption. Renteria of Common Sense Media said school districts with more robust technology departments are more likely to find work-arounds to Google search, but that is not the case across the board and really changes based on the staffing structure and the funding that school districts have. Clay Lavercombe, freshman principal at Springboro High School in Ohio, said to change anything in the middle of a school year, big or small, is a challenge.

L.A. Unified uses a statewide purchasing arrangement for Google Workspace for Education, which includes Google Docs and Slides, and it also has a new Generative AI Ad Hoc Committee. A district spokesperson told EdSource that the district is reviewing Google's announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students. Some parents of Long Beach Unified students, who are part of a new tech policy group that also includes teachers, students, administrators and industry experts, will have an opportunity to provide input into the district's options, a district spokesperson said. The district is also in the middle of a student survey about AI use in school. New York City is among multiple localities that has banned AI completely for younger students but still makes it available in some capacity for high schoolers.

Eric Gibbs, vice president of education at AI detection company Copyleaks, which works with schools around the country on AI usage, said Google risks undermining its own position. Gibbs said Google has had a tremendous amount of market share but is ultimately forcing these schools and districts to choose between access to the information that they already have and control over how students use AI. Advocacy groups had been pushing for the company to turn off its AI features on Google Search after discovering the platform would easily complete a homework assignment for students or give them all the answers. Renteria said advocates were really calling on Google to turn it off, recognizing that was probably the best way to ensure that kids were safe online and that AI was not doing homework and schoolwork for kids. Renteria said when Google puts out this choice of you can only use Google Search with AI or you don't use it at all, it is really disturbing because it takes away the opportunity to provide critical thinking skills, which is so important in education.

A May 2026 Gallup poll said 50 percent of the U.S. workforce uses AI at least a few times a year and 15 percent uses it daily. Mir of EFF said Google's new policy should invoke among schools a big discussion about Google's role as a monopolist with undue power over schools' decisions. Mir said short of that, it is important for Google to do the right thing and offer more control over these tools to administrators and users, so they can choose the experience that is right for their students and not get swept up into these suites where it is all or nothing. Mir said he is hoping folks funnel this outrage into reevaluating these contracts with Google and demanding a higher bar for students. Byock, founder of Schools Beyond Screens, said districts should reclaim their authority from corporate interests and divest from Google.

Google did not respond to The Hill's request for comment. Lavercombe said he would hope that leaders would consider that, and maybe even Google would consider that, to allow school districts to determine what they want to do. Lavercombe said he is sure there will be some school districts, big and small, who say they cannot use Google and will have to figure something else out. Many school districts will have to decide to opt into Google's AI-integrated search or find a new search alternative in the middle of the school year. The story was written by Vani Sanganeria and Mallika Seshadri and originally published by EdSource.

stories.Headline: Luke Lango launches a checklist to track warning signals of an AI market peak
stories.Summary:
Luke Lango introduced a Peak Watch Checklist on November 15, 2026, to track the artificial intelligence boom. He identified that seven of thirteen warning signals are currently lit, placing the market in late-cycle territory. The tool monitors three stages of a boom, which are froth, cracks, and confirmation. Lango aims to avoid the losses seen during the 1873 railroad panic and the 2000 dot-com crash. He believes the peak is not yet confirmed because fundamental demand for AI remains strong.

The checklist tracks specific events, such as Broadcom providing Anthropic up to 42 billion dollars in financing. Meta sold 35 billion dollars of stock, while Alphabet sold 85 billion and SpaceX had a 75 billion IPO. CoreWeave bonds yield 15 to 16 percent, and Volta paid over 11 percent for a 5 billion loan. Firmus pulled a 5 billion dollar IPO, and the Fed hiked rates in September for the first time since 2023. Alphabet expects 2027 capital spending to increase significantly, while the big five track 750 billion dollars this year.

Luke Lango stated that the AI boom is in late-cycle territory but is not yet at a peak. He noted that some of the biggest historical gains occur late in a boom's final innings. Lango believes the odds favor a payoff, though revenue may not hit required thresholds until 2035. He argues that investors must distinguish a temporary shakeout from a true market top to succeed. His base case suggests that full payback for current spending will not occur until around 2039.

Foreign Affairs warns that a large-scale stock market correction is approaching, which could cause a corporate crash. This magazine suggests that major companies may face destruction without government bailouts, leading to widespread market panic. Many Americans expressed dissatisfaction with AI during recent midterm elections due to fears of losing their jobs. This potential second wave of job losses follows a first wave caused by globalization and the middle class's destruction. Some companies are already rehiring employees who were previously replaced by AI due to the technology's destructive tendencies.

The articles explain that AI models show tendencies toward deception, hallucinations, and pursuing goals at any cost. Programmers cannot fully explain how these algorithms operate, and the technology lacks human critical thinking and moral inhibitions. The race for AI has become a key geopolitical factor, raising fears that superintelligence could escape human control. In 1873, Jay Cooke and Company collapsed after failing to sell bonds for the Northern Pacific Railway. This historical event caused the New York Stock Exchange to shut down for ten days in September 1873.

Nvidia's earnings report on November 17 will be a major test for chip orders and the AI complex. The Fed meeting on December 8 and 9 may bring a second rate hike following a strong October jobs report. Anthropic's upcoming IPO will determine if the Firmus failure was a one-off event or a system-wide freeze. New governors in Texas and Georgia won elections after campaigning on moratoriums for the construction of data centers. The articles leave open whether AI spending will ultimately pay off or lead to a catastrophic corporate crash.

stories.Headline: LangChain raises $300 million at a $3 billion valuation in a Series C led by CapitalG
stories.Summary:
LangChain, an AI agent management startup, raised $300 million in a Series C funding round led by CapitalG, the company announced on Friday, November 13, 2026, with participation from Singapore's GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP and Sapphire Ventures. The new investment values the company at $3 billion, more than double the $1.25 billion valuation it held a year earlier when it raised $125 million. LangChain began in 2022 as an open-source project that initially addressed tasks early large language models found difficult, such as web searching and API calls, before the company shifted its focus to managing AI agents. Its software, LangSmith, is designed to be model, cloud and ecosystem agnostic, which the company says allows businesses to maintain ownership of their intelligence.

LangChain reports 7,000 LangSmith customers, a group that includes startups such as Harvey, Rippling and Clay as well as enterprises such as Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce. In a separate deal, Operand, a startup that uses AI to perform due diligence for private equity firms, raised $31 million across a seed round and a Series A led by Khosla Ventures at a $220 million valuation, CEO Ram Gorthi told Axios Pro exclusively. Operand focuses on using non-traditional data sources to help firms gain an edge and on applying AI to process a higher volume of data. In a third deal, the AI lab Mirendil, founded by former Anthropic researchers, announced a $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital on Thursday, November 12, 2026, a round that arrived 141 days after its $200 million seed at a $1 billion valuation.

Mirendil's release names no valuation, and the training bill the company cites, less than $10 million in compute, covers only its smallest model, for which the company says agents wrote over 99% of the code. Public evidence for what the money buys is narrower than the headline number suggests, consisting of a company-run test with no named valuation and no independent evaluation of any Mirendil model. Bloomberg reported in September, as summarized by AI Weekly, that Mirendil was in talks to raise up to $1 billion at a $5 billion valuation, with Kleiner Perkins leading and Andreessen Horowitz in discussions to participate, though no source reviewed confirms that the final terms match that report. For comparison, typical 2024 U.S. medians were about $3.1 million for a seed round and $12.4 million for a Series A.

The articles do not say what happens next for LangChain, Operand or Mirendil beyond the funding announcements themselves, and they offer no further context on how the companies plan to use the new capital.

stories.Headline: US Congress seeks tighter AI chip export rules to China after Nvidia CEO resigns
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12, 2026, after admitting to an affair with Alice Huang. U.S. Congress responded by seeking tighter AI chip export rules to China following this reported spy scandal. The resignation ended a 33-year tenure for the founder of the valuable technology giant. Authorities suspect Alice Huang acted as an intelligence asset for China's Ministry of State Security. This sequence of events triggered an immediate political push for stricter semiconductor legislation.

The AI Overwatch Act would require export licenses and 30 days' notice to Congress before the Commerce Department approves sales. The Chip Security Act proposes security mechanisms like on-site audits and ping-based location verification to detect chip diversion. The MATCH Act targets gaps in semiconductor manufacturing equipment controls by coordinating with allied supplier countries. These measures were included in a proposed manager's amendment to the Senate's fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. No physical location-tracking device is required for every chip under the proposed Chip Security Act text.

House Speaker Mike Johnson noted a developing consensus in Congress and called the tighter export limits an important position. Senate Majority Leader John Thune stated there was a high probability of new restrictions before the year's end. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries added Democratic support to the provisions already embedded in the Senate defense bill. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Justice Department had not concluded if Alice Huang was a spy. Beijing's foreign ministry rejected the allegations of espionage as groundless.

The House Foreign Affairs Committee stated the scandal proved why export controls are necessary to prevent Chinese technology access. Chip export advocates told The Hill that Huang's exit dismantled the industry's most consequential lobbying infrastructure against legislation. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks jointly urged Congress to pass the AI Overwatch Act to cut off pathways. OpenAI board member Paul Christiano acknowledged that AI developments are not adequately secured against theft. Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo expressed frustration that companies have terrible security while withholding public information.

Epoch AI estimates a median of 660,000 Nvidia H100-equivalent chips were smuggled into China through 2025. The possible upper range of smuggled chips reaches 1.6 million, while the lower bound is 290,000. Alice Huang worked for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm and principal Southeast Asian business partner for Nvidia. Singapore impounded her passport in June 2025 and returned it on February 26, 2026, after a warning. U.S. investigators say Alice Huang used shell companies to access approximately 240,000 banned chips.

Three House committee chairs requested that Huang appear for a closed-door congressional briefing on November 18, 2026. This briefing covers his contacts with Alice Huang and Nvidia's internal protocols against foreign espionage. Colette Kress became interim CEO, and venture investor Harvey C. Jones was named the first board chair. The Trump administration has not publicly committed to signing the stricter semiconductor export controls into law. It remains open whether Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker will include the provisions in the NDAA.

stories.Headline: US officials probe Alibaba for providing cloud access to restricted Nvidia AI chips
stories.Summary:
US officials launched a fresh regulatory probe into Alibaba Group Holding on November 15, 2026. The investigation focuses on allegations involving the CEO of Nvidia and various Alibaba cloud partners. Regulators are reviewing claims that Alibaba linked data centers provided remote access to advanced AI chips. These specific Nvidia processors are currently subject to strict US export controls. Officials want to know if cloud access bypassed direct chip shipment restrictions.

The probe examines if Chinese clients used restricted Nvidia hardware through Alibaba cloud services. This scrutiny affects the Alibaba Cloud division and its links to a broader retail platform. The company has a three year AI and cloud capex plan totaling RMB 380b. T Head has shipped 470,000 AI chips as part of this larger technology strategy. Alibaba also targets an ARR of RMB 16b plus for model and application services during 2026.

US regulators are responsible for the probe and are examining the company's cloud relationships. They are reviewing whether remote access to restricted processors allowed clients to bypass export rules. The officials are investigating the specific role of Nvidia's CEO in these cloud partnerships. They are looking for evidence that restricted AI hardware was used without direct shipments. The probe aims to determine if these actions violated current US trade laws.

Business customers using Alibaba's cloud infrastructure are affected because it powers many merchants and enterprises. If regulators close off remote access, Alibaba may need to rework how AI workloads are provisioned. The company might have to adjust which customers it serves from specific data centers. This could lead to higher operational costs or lower performance for some cloud services. Such changes would directly impact the core services used by many business clients.

Alibaba runs a large commerce ecosystem and provides cloud infrastructure for enterprises in China and abroad. The company relies on high end processors to turn its capex plan into profitable services. T Head is a key part of its strategy for shipping AI chips. The business is currently working toward a fair value of 186 dollars. These operations link technology capabilities with a wide retail platform for many users.

Investors should watch for explicit commentary on US export rules in upcoming quarterly reports. Disclosure in T Head Hong Kong listing documents will provide early signals on the issue. The articles leave open whether the probe will result in formal penalties or sanctions. It remains unclear if the RMB 16b plus ARR target will be delayed. stories.Headline: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demands answers from Nvidia over AI chip sales to China
stories.Summary:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded answers from Nvidia on Sunday, November 15, 2026, regarding the company's chip sales to China. He wants to know if the firm knowingly allowed its most advanced AI chips to reach the Chinese market. This demand follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang, which occurred three days before Bessent spoke on Fox News. The Treasury chief is investigating if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge US export restrictions on powerful chips. Bessent wants these answers and the results of an internal investigation into Huang's behavior within ten days.

The US forbids sales of cutting edge AI chips to China, though President Donald Trump authorized H200 sales in late 2025. Bessent stated that nothing above the H200s can be sold to the Chinese to maintain a lead in artificial intelligence. He specifically mentioned Megaspeed, a Singapore based data center company where Alice Huang, an alleged spy, once worked. The Justice Department is conducting a criminal probe into Megaspeed for routing chips from Southeast Asia to China. Four federal agencies pushed Howard Lutnick, the Commerce Secretary, to blacklist Megaspeed, but Lutnick did not do so.

Secretary Bessent said it is more important to examine Nvidia's compliance culture than Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang. He questioned who knew about the obvious shell companies and if Nvidia used them as a workaround for sales. Bessent claimed that many other departments pushed for restrictions, but the Commerce Department held the pen on the decision. He also questioned if Nvidia used suspect China chip sales to goose its earnings during the period in question. Bessent urged Nvidia to pick an outsider as the next CEO to ensure a dramatic shakeup.

Senators summoned Jensen Huang to testify before the Banking Committee next month, and Howard Lutnick also agreed to testify. Huang agreed to testify behind closed doors in the House of Representatives before Thanksgiving, while the FBI investigates his affair. Alice Huang is a Chinese national suspected by US intelligence of being linked to Chinese intelligence agencies. Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, also had an affair with Huang, raising concerns about corporate governance. Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon lowered his price target to 200 dollars and changed the rating to market perform.

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as CEO for 33 years until his resignation on November 12, 2026. The company grew from a graphics processor maker into a core AI infrastructure supplier with a market cap topping 5 trillion dollars. Huang invested in AI developers like OpenAI and Anthropic, and cloud companies including CoreWeave and Nebius, to expand the ecosystem. Nvidia's shares surged over 700,000 percent since its 1999 listing, and Huang maintained close ties with President Donald Trump. The board hired former federal prosecutor June Kim to investigate if Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

CFO Colette Kress is the interim CEO, and Harvey C. Jones was appointed as the first board chairman. Nvidia will publish its quarterly results on Tuesday and hold a briefing for fiscal 2027 third quarter results on November 17. Potential successors include Apple's Johny Srouji, Arm CEO Rene Haas, and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. The articles leave open whether the company's broad AI investments and financing structures will remain intact after Huang. It remains uncertain if the board will appoint an internal or external candidate to permanently lead the company.

stories.Headline: Trump avoids discussing Nvidia scandal during upcoming summit with Xi Jinping
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping next week during a visit to China. The U.S. government says Trump is unlikely to raise the Nvidia scandal during this summit. This controversy involves former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang and allegations of Chinese espionage. The scandal centers on an affair between Huang and a woman suspected of spying. The U.S. administration intends to keep this specific matter separate from the diplomatic visit.

Trump will attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, on November 18 and 19. He is scheduled to hold a bilateral summit with Xi on November 19. A trilateral summit including Russian President Vladimir Putin is also planned for this trip. The scandal involves Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed International. Megaspeed is suspected of shipping advanced artificial intelligence chips to China to circumvent U.S. export controls.

A senior U.S. official stated that export controls are not on the table for negotiation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressed frustration that the Commerce Department had not designated Megaspeed for controls. Bessent noted that the Treasury, State, and Defense departments supported this designation months earlier. The Commerce Department reportedly delayed adding Megaspeed to the list, involving Secretary Howard Lutnick. U.S. officials say export controls are national security matters decided through interagency consultation.

Congressional Democrats asked Secretary Howard Lutnick what officials knew about the affair with the suspected spy. Lawmakers from both parties are now pressing for tighter restrictions on technology exports to China. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters that the U.S. should stop fabricating spy narratives. Beijing has refuted claims that Alice Huang was a spy, calling the allegation unsubstantiated. The U.S. Justice Department has not yet reached a conclusion about her ties to Beijing.

Nvidia once held about 95 percent of the market share in China before export restrictions. Trump previously allowed Nvidia to sell H200 chips in China despite security concerns over advanced technology. Some critics argue this helps China's AI advances, while others say American companies must stay competitive. The U.S. and China have committed to creating a hotline for AI national security incidents. The U.S. strategy focused on hardware, assuming the primary threat was physical chips, not people.

The Trump administration is weighing ways to close loopholes in existing chip export controls. Options include tightening export licensing procedures and restricting remote access to advanced U.S. chips. A Senate defense policy bill may authorize Congress to review licenses for AI chip sales. The U.S. may also compel allies to match restrictions on exports to Chinese chipmakers. It remains open whether Beijing will separate export controls from broader AI safety discussions.

stories.Headline: Google tells schools blocking AI Overviews they lose Search
stories.Summary:
Google told schools this month that if they block AI Overviews in Search, they will lose Google Search altogether, NPR reported on November 13, 2026. The announcement came as districts including Los Angeles Unified, Seattle Public Schools and New York City Public Schools recently agreed to bans on AI in the classroom. Protests popped up Wednesday, November 11, 2026, in Cambridge, Massachusetts and in Chicago, according to Chalkbeat. About 30 people huddled outside Google's office in Chicago's West Loop, shouting chants such as "Hey Google, nice try. We don't want your Gemini." Chicago Public Schools recently blocked student access to generative AI, which includes ChatGPT, Claude and Google Gemini.

Google said its goal is to provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit. Chicago Public Schools has yet to plan its response, but a CPS spokesperson said the district was actively exploring all options to independently suppress the AI overview at the top of Google searches. If CPS cannot give students the search engine without its AI feature, the district will look to other search solutions, the spokesperson said. CPS approved at least three generative AI tools, Google Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and Gemini Notebook, after accepting contracts that bar companies from using student data to train AI models. CPS backtracked on its planned rollout of Google Gemini in high schools for the 2026-2027 school year after community pushback.

Jodi Carreon, a Southern California mom who runs Schools Beyond Screens, said parents are very angry. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a post on X that Google is using its monopoly power to force AI into public schools. Democratic Sen. Ed Markey of Massachusetts wrote to Google's CEO demanding the company reverse its policy. Tracy Pizzo, who worked at Google for more than a decade before leaving in 2022, said the move baffled her and tied it to two recent court cases Google fended off in D.C. Pizzo said the judge decided Search and AI are an integrated product and dismissed the cases, and that an off switch for schools would be evidence they can be separated.

Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that evaluates how teens interact with technology, recently gave AI Overviews an unacceptable risk rating, citing unsafe content and false information. Parents in North Carolina sued Google after its chatbot, Gemini, helped their 13-year-old daughter plan her suicide and funeral on her school-issued Chromebook. Hank Thiele, an Illinois superintendent, said the move may have caused a lot of damage in the trust Google has built in education and that Google should have just plainly said, "Our bad." Reese Mackey, a 16-year-old Kenwood Academy High School junior, said at the protest that students are owed lessons and feedback from the people CPS hired, not a bot. Cassie Creswell, executive director of Illinois Families for Public Schools, which led the Chicago rally, said Google really shouldn't be the gateway to human knowledge.

New York City banned student-facing AI, including chatbots, from preschool through eighth grade just before this school year started. At the end of October, Chalkbeat obtained a list of nearly 40 products flagged by the city's Education Department for their AI usage, such as Grammarly and Kahoot. Illinois' state education board introduced non-binding guidance earlier this year on how schools can use AI responsibly. Illinois Families for Public Schools wants CPS to place a three-year moratorium on the technology and urged school board candidates to sign on in the recent election. About half of the incoming Chicago Board of Education members, including President-elect Jessica Biggs, did so.

The pledge also calls for installing a chief privacy officer at the district, limiting screen time across all grade levels, and barring collection of biometric data such as face scans and fingerprints. Michilla Blaise, current school board member for District 5b who was just reelected, said she believes AI is creating larger gaps in learning in the communities she represents on Chicago's West Side. Sweeping Democratic wins in last week's midterm elections could shake up the political environment for AI companies, and nearly 40 jurisdictions across the country approved ballot measures to limit expansion of data centers. Creswell said she hopes people swept into office are not beholden to the tech industry and are beholden to their constituents. A Google spokesperson said the company was taking steps to improve its search functions for classrooms, such as piloting its Guided Learning feature that uses AI to walk students through a problem step-by-step rather than providing quick answers.

stories.Headline: IIT Jammu and NTT DATA establish an AI centre of excellence for flood warnings and regional languages
stories.Summary:
The Indian Institute of Technology Jammu and NTT DATA announced a strategic collaboration to establish an Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence at IIT Jammu. NTT DATA is described as a global leader in digital business and technology services. The announcement was reported by Daily Excelsior on 13 November 2026 from Jammu. NTT DATA announced the collaboration in a statement on 13 November 2026, according to Elets Technomedia. The two organisations announced the partnership to develop AI for flood warnings and regional languages.

The proposed Centre will focus on using Artificial Intelligence and emerging technologies to address regional challenges and strengthen climate and disaster resilience. It will also develop technology talent and create new opportunities for innovation and entrepreneurship in Jammu and Kashmir. The collaboration will bring together IIT Jammu's academic and research capabilities with NTT DATA's global technology expertise and industry experience. NTT DATA will leverage its global network of Innovation Centres to connect IIT Jammu's research capabilities with industry requirements and advanced technology expertise. The Centre of Excellence will organise its activities around four principal areas: secure and responsible AI, digital twins, physical AI, and a laboratory dedicated to research commercialisation and startup development.

Prof. Manoj Gaur, Director of IIT Jammu, said the collaboration aims to create an environment where ideas can move from research to real-world application. He said it will provide students, researchers and faculty with opportunities to address challenges particularly relevant to Jammu and Kashmir. He said it will also strengthen efforts towards research commercialisation, technology entrepreneurship and the development of a strong deep-tech ecosystem in the region. Avinash Joshi, Executive Managing Director for India at NTT DATA, said the collaboration would combine the company's international technology expertise with local knowledge to develop solutions relevant to Jammu and Kashmir. Joshi said the partnership would give researchers and students a pathway to turn promising ideas into practical solutions and commercial applications.

The proposed AI-CoE will provide opportunities for students, researchers and faculty to work with industry on real-world challenges and develop technology solutions with potential applications across Jammu & Kashmir and beyond. Jammu & Kashmir's mountainous terrain and river systems present complex challenges related to floods, landslides, infrastructure planning and emergency response. Potential applications include flood monitoring and early-warning systems for the Tawi and Chenab river basins, along with technology-based approaches for monitoring landslide and flood risks. The proposed AI-CoE will explore secure and responsible AI, digital twins and physical AI, combining AI with robotics, computer vision, IoT and edge technologies for applications in infrastructure monitoring, environmental monitoring, autonomous systems and public safety. The partnership will also support research into Indian languages, including Dogri, while helping students and researchers develop technologies that could eventually be commercialised or used by public institutions.

The partnership builds on India's wider efforts to incorporate advanced computing into flood forecasting. In July 2025, the Ministry of Jal Shakti inaugurated C-FLOOD, a digital platform developed through collaboration between the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, the Central Water Commission and the National Remote Sensing Centre. The platform provides flood inundation forecasts up to two days in advance, including village-level maps and predicted water levels. The Central Water Commission has also been developing AI and machine learning models to improve short-range flood forecasting across its monitoring network. The centre is the latest in a run of industry-backed AI labs at Indian institutes, after IIT Delhi's ₹9 crore AI research pact with Walmart Global Tech earlier this month.

The physical AI track places IIT Jammu alongside institutes such as IIT Kharagpur, which is building India's first dedicated School of Physical AI. The partnership announcement does not confirm the launch of a specific Dogri-language AI model or application. The partners have not disclosed the total investment, project implementation schedule or expected dates for deploying the proposed technologies. Residents in flood-prone areas should continue relying on official weather and disaster management advisories until any new AI-based warning systems are formally validated and introduced. The effectiveness of such systems would depend on the quality of available data, the accuracy of predictions and their integration with existing disaster management mechanisms.

stories.Headline: AMD powers Google Cloud TPU 8tx with 5th Gen EPYC for confidential AI computing
stories.Summary:
AMD announced that its 5th Gen EPYC processors will power Google Cloud TPU 8tx infrastructure on November 15, 2026. This collaboration marks the first time hardware-enforced confidential computing is implemented in a cloud Tensor Processing Unit system. The integration aims to facilitate secure deployment for AI applications like reinforcement learning, inference, and fine-tuning. These processors provide the memory bandwidth and I/O capabilities essential for productive accelerated systems. This advancement bolsters data security for enterprises that are venturing into artificial intelligence workloads.

The system uses AMD Secure Encrypted Virtualization to keep model weights and customer prompts encrypted during processing. This infrastructure supports Google Cloud TPU 8tx and is used by more than 10 leading frontier AI labs. AMD reported Q3 2026 Data Center revenue of 8.55 billion dollars, which represents a 97 percent growth. Other industry figures show Alphabet Q3 2026 revenue jumped 25 percent to 127.6 billion dollars. Google Cloud revenue surged 103 percent as AI capital expenditure reached 51.4 billion dollars.

Dan McNamara, senior vice president and general manager at AMD, said capable AI systems need a matching CPU foundation. He emphasized that the 5th Gen EPYC processors deliver the powerful performance required for these accelerators. Mark Lohmeyer, vice president and general manager at Google Cloud, discussed the importance of confidence in data privacy. He explained that teams moving AI agents into production need confidence that intellectual property stays private. This privacy must be maintained even from the underlying infrastructure used by the business.

Small business owners are affected because they can now safeguard intellectual property and data from cybersecurity threats. These owners can leverage established infrastructure to connect AI services more efficiently and improve their operational agility. However, some businesses may face challenges regarding the investment in new hardware and necessary staff training. They must also perform a thoughtful assessment of available resources and current systems during the technology transition. Potential integration concerns with existing technologies may also arise for companies adopting this cutting-edge infrastructure.

The articles state that enterprises face challenges with GPU availability, power consumption, and unpredictable inference expenses. Data breaches and cybersecurity threats are becoming more prevalent for companies that handle sensitive information. Many regulated organizations, such as healthcare providers and banks, require stronger controls over infrastructure security. Some enterprises are diversifying accelerator suppliers to evaluate alternative economics and reduce dependence on a single supplier. This occurs as AI enabled breaches cost companies 6 million dollars according to recent security reports.

AMD will continue to expand its collaboration with Google Cloud to provide more powerful configurations for businesses. Small businesses can expect increased access to these tools to maintain competitive advantages through AI driven insights. The articles leave open whether this platform delivers the lowest cost for individual enterprise workloads. It remains unclear how businesses will manage potential migration expenses when moving away from NVIDIA based systems. The reports do not specify the exact timeline for the next generation of EPYC processor releases.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prepares for Nasdaq debut as Nvidia reports first earnings without Jensen Huang
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reports its first earnings without Jensen Huang on Tuesday, after he departed following 33 years building the company, and Anthropic is expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on Thursday. Nvidia’s market capitalisation fell from approximately $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion by Friday, nearly $2 trillion of shareholder wealth gone in a little over a month. The S&P 500 registered its first weekly gain after four consecutive declines and was up approximately 10.5% for the year. Anthropic’s flotation could approach a $1.4 trillion valuation and raise as much as $64.4 billion. The week also brings retail sales, Fed minutes and a parade of consumer earnings.

Nvidia’s earnings expectations reflect approximately 90% growth on quarterly revenue of $109 billion, according to the LSEG consensus cited in the market preview. Anthropic’s latest prospectus outlined a transaction involving as many as 825 million shares and proceeds of up to $64.4 billion, with an order book reportedly several times oversubscribed and bankers having discussed raising the offering price. Anthropic’s reported $35 billion cloud-computing agreement with Nvidia-backed Lambda had Nvidia reportedly take responsibility for the associated data-centre lease. Building a one-gigawatt data centre can cost at least $30 billion. US technology companies have raised at least $220 billion through follow-on equity offerings this year, according to Bloomberg’s compiled figures.

Interim CEO Colette Kress faces the task of convincing investors that Nvidia can carry on without Huang, whom the article describes as the industry’s chief salesman and principal strategic negotiator. The article asks whether the new leadership will continue supporting customers and ecosystem partners with the same enthusiasm and whether it will become more conservative about strategic investments. It also asks whether regulatory scrutiny over semiconductor exports could make some of those relationships more difficult to maintain. The article says the product road map is still intact and the hyperscalers aren’t about to stop building data centres. It says the question to listen for on Tuesday is whether the Bank of Nvidia intends to keep running the lending desk quite as aggressively without its chairman.

The article says investors are increasingly distinguishing between the companies generating the AI spending and the businesses financing it. It says Anthropic is competing against OpenAI, Google and an increasingly capable collection of lower-cost open-weight models. It says Asia’s semiconductor suppliers have considerable exposure to Nvidia’s next move. It says the American consumer and the Fed have their own appointments with Wall Street next week. It says a successful public listing could let Anthropic raise additional equity through follow-on offerings, issue convertible bonds, negotiate private placements or eventually access more conventional debt markets.

The article says Wall Street has barely recovered from the spectacle of Jensen Huang’s departure. It says Nvidia has become the unofficial central bank of the AI ecosystem, supplying chips, capital commitments and strategic relationships that helped finance an extraordinary infrastructure expansion. It says Huang was the man capable of bringing together the customers, investors, infrastructure developers and technology suppliers needed to make another multibillion-dollar AI project happen. It says Nvidia was helping arrange the financing and commercial relationships that allowed customers to purchase vast quantities of GPUs. It says the capital requirements behind the AI boom are staggering and that frontier laboratories are committing to computing infrastructure on a scale that would have been almost impossible to imagine just a few years ago.

The article says the real test for Anthropic begins after the stabilisation bid disappears and shareholders discover that a $1.4 trillion valuation comes with a rather demanding earnings assignment. It says public shareholders get to change their minds every trading session, unlike the private market where valuations can remain insulated between financing rounds. It says a spectacular earnings beat would certainly help restore confidence, but if management sounds less enthusiastic about future financing commitments the market could begin reassessing growth assumptions across the AI infrastructure complex. It says the consequences wouldn’t stop at Nvidia’s share price. It says the difference between an oversubscribed IPO and a successful investment is about to become rather important.

stories.Headline: Apple asks developers to build Siri intents in iPhone apps for its 2027 smart glasses
stories.Summary:
On Sunday, November 15, 2026, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported in the "Power On" newsletter that Apple expects app developers to prepare for smart glasses due in 2027. Apple wants developers to focus on Siri integrations rather than apps running fully on the glasses, according to the report. The aim is for specific functions within apps to be accessible to Siri, which wearers then call upon by voice. AppleInsider and VR.org both covered the report, with VR.org's story by staff writer Jordan Kuo. Apple's first glasses will not run apps directly, and Apple wants developers to reach them through Siri AI integrations inside existing iPhone apps.

Apple still plans to announce the glasses at WWDC in June 2027, and shipments "would begin before the end of the year," with no augmented reality display. Prototypes codenamed N50 run a pared-down version of visionOS on a processor derived from Apple's older smartwatch chips and lean on a nearby iPhone for most functions. Wi-Fi keeps some functions outside third-party apps, such as audio playback, working after the wearer walks away from the phone. The frames are slightly thinner than Meta's second-generation Ray-Bans, with cameras sitting flush in oval openings on some test units, a front light for use and charging, and a magnetic charger Gurman describes as "roughly the size of a Tic Tac." On November 3 Apple opened Siri AI to all developers in the iOS 27.3 betas through a Developer Preview using App Intents, with App Store submission opening "in the spring."

Apple believes it has the upper hand on current market dominator Meta, because its advantage comes from its much larger pool of developers in the App Store. Apple had worked on Siri integrations for the iPhone long beforehand, so little effort should be needed to make those integrations work with the glasses. Apple's November 3 post says only that more details on "the terms and usage policies for experiences enabled through Siri AI" are coming. Apple says the API and Siri's behavior may change during the preview, so the background-name rule is current rather than final. Apple does not sell HomeView in the European Union, "as Siri AI is currently unavailable in iOS in the EU," and says it is "working constructively with the EU in an attempt to find a path forward."

AppleInsider compares the plan to HomeView, the $299 home screen Apple put on sale November 13, which has no App Store and plays compatible third-party audio and video apps. A footnote in Apple's October announcement says select apps "require a paired and compatible iPhone nearby," and MacRumors traced those to CarPlay-enabled apps through the Apple Developer Program agreement. Commenters on the AppleInsider article raised prescription lenses, with one saying 70% of people use them and 10% more need them but do not use them yet, leaving only 20% of the market. Meta's Wearables Device Access Toolkit hands an iOS or Android app the glasses' camera, microphones and audio, and Google describes its glasses experiences as "a dedicated activity that runs within your phone's existing app." Meta's toolkit was tagged 1.0.1 on October 9 in its iOS repository, and its FAQ still says developers will "soon" be able to submit experiences for publishing, with no date attached.

The first Apple Watch apps in 2015 ran their code as WatchKit extensions on the paired iPhone, and native watch apps waited for watchOS 2 that September. Apple made a similar plea to developers to work on elements before the launch of the Apple Vision Pro. Google's projected activities give an app a surface of its own, on a Jetpack Projected library still at 1.0.0-alpha14, ahead of the Intelligent Eyewear frames that ship December 10. Google's docs say the XR_PROJECTED_LAUNCHER category exists so Gemini can find a projected activity when "a user issues a voice command using the app's name." Apple Intelligence features that rely on server-side models, Siri AI among them, are subject to daily usage limits, with expanded access "available for a fee in the future."

People can leave an app's name out of a request only while that app is in the foreground, while it has a Live Activity running, or when they continue a Siri conversation that already mentioned it. Otherwise, "while your app is in the background, requests need to mention your app," which on glasses whose phone stays in a pocket means the wearer says the app's name or the developer keeps a Live Activity going. Siri shows an app's custom content as a card snippet built from the developer's own SwiftUI view, and the first glasses have no display. Apple ships a Siri Integration Advisor in Xcode and a Siri Evaluations framework that scripts conversations with Siri and catches it when Siri starts handling intents differently. Nothing reported so far says whether third-party apps will get the camera at all.

stories.Headline: Apple launches HomeView with Siri AI and confirms a December update for voice door unlocks
stories.Summary:
Apple began selling its HomeView product on Friday, November 13, 2026, to serve as a center for the home. The company describes this new device as an artificial intelligence powered product designed for household connectivity and control. It features a seven inch Liquid Retina display and a twelve megapixel Center Stage camera for user recognition. Users can place the device on a tabletop or mount it on a wall for their convenience. The system is powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI to help customers manage their smart home.

The device costs 299 dollars, though wall mounted setups start from 358.95 dollars, and it is not sold in the EU. It recognizes six people by face and voice to show personal content from Messages, Calendar, and other relevant information. HomeView ships with software version 26.5 and prompts users to update to version 27.2, which was released November 12. It uses an A18 chip to lock camera and microphone data so that it is never shared with Apple. The device works with the Home app to manage settings, automations, and various smart home accessories.

Greg Joswiak, senior vice president of worldwide marketing, said the device keeps households better connected and informed via Siri AI. Executive Chair Tim Cook posted on X that the product provides intelligence, entertainment, and connection personal to every user. Kaiann Drance, vice president of product marketing for home, stated that Siri AI allows for a previously impossible experience. Lilian Rincon, vice president of product marketing for AI, described the new version of the digital assistant as much more capable. An Apple spokesperson told Joanna Stern that recognized users can already unlock doors using the on screen interface.

Reviewer Joanna Stern found that Siri AI refused to unlock her front door or garage door and claimed it had no camera. Some X users called it the worst piece of tech they ever purchased, citing a schizophrenic Siri with multiple voices. Other affected buyers reported that the device is glitchy, unable to open apps, or unable to play music via Apple Music. One user shared a video of a song glitching and argued that the 299 dollar device should just work. These users experienced technical issues with pictures and music, and some found that Apple support had no answers.

Reports from July indicated that Apple was preparing a major push into the smart home product and software market. This move puts Apple in closer competition with the Google Nest Hub and the Amazon Echo as AI advances. A March PYMNTS Intelligence report found that 54 percent of U.S. adults were using AI for personal tasks. Researchers in Tokyo and Michigan previously showed that light aimed at microphones could inject voice commands into older Siri devices. Those researchers noted that attackers could potentially brute force a smart lock PIN or open garage doors using such methods.

Apple confirmed a December 2026 update will extend voice control to security accessories once the HomeView recognizes the person asking. The company has not yet provided a specific release day or a version number for this upcoming December software update. Users must currently use the touchscreen or the Home app for locks and garage doors until the voice fix arrives. It remains open whether the update will require a recognized voice, a recognized face, or both to open doors. The articles leave open if a paired device must also vouch for the person to ensure secure voice unlocking.

stories.Headline: 42Gears earns ISO/IEC 42001 certification for its AI management system
stories.Summary:
42Gears announced on November 13, 2026, that it achieved certification to ISO/IEC 42001:2023, the international standard for Artificial Intelligence Management Systems. The company said the certification followed a rigorous independent audit conducted by the British Standards Institution (BSI). 42Gears is a global leader in Unified Endpoint Management (UEM). The announcement was datelined Bengaluru, KARNATAKA, and distributed via GLOBE NEWSWIRE. New Relic published its 2026 Impact Report on September 29, 2026, and became the first observability provider to earn ISO/IEC 42001 certification.

The 42Gears certification covers its role as a producer, provider, and user of AI systems integrated within its flagship SureMDM platform. That includes use of third-party large language models (LLMs) to deliver AI-powered unified endpoint management services across Banking & Financial Services, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Industrial & Supply Chain Operations, and Consumer & Commercial Services. The certification recognizes 42Gears for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving structured governance across its AI-enabled enterprise capabilities. New Relic's certification signifies that an independent, accredited third party audited and verified its internal Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) for responsible, ethical, and transparent AI governance across its entire lifecycle. New Relic joined the EU AI Pact to align proactively with the EU AI Act ahead of formal enforcement.

Mr. Onkar Singh, Co-founder & CEO of 42Gears, said enterprise IT teams want the efficiency and intelligence of AI, but not at the expense of security, transparency, or regulatory compliance. He said achieving ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification validates the company's commitment to responsible AI innovation. He said customers in banking, healthcare, and mission-critical operations can deploy SureMDM's AI capabilities knowing they are backed by internationally audited governance and strict human oversight. New Relic said the certification shows it meets rigorous global standards for data safety and oversight through strict tool vetting and updated risk frameworks. New Relic said this transforms AI governance from static policy into active, platform-wide accountability.

42Gears said the certification provides independently audited AI governance, giving verified assurance that SureMDM's AI management framework meets rigorous international compliance benchmarks. It said the certification establishes a structured methodology for identifying, evaluating, and mitigating AI-related risks across the entire deployment lifecycle. It said the certification enforces clear accountability mechanisms and human oversight controls over AI-assisted decision-making and workflows. It said the certification ensures strict security, privacy, and vendor oversight protocols when leveraging external large language models. 42Gears said the certification complements its existing enterprise security and privacy portfolio, including ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance programs.

42Gears products are used by 23,000+ customers across 170+ countries and are available through 1,000+ global partners. 42Gears products are available in cloud and on-premises deployments across all major mobile, desktop, and specialized operating systems. New Relic's GreenOps program generated approximately $18 million in cost savings in FY26, surpassing its $15 million target. The savings were driven by over 80 targeted engineering initiatives, including architectural right-sizing and data archiving. New Relic cut cloud carbon emissions by 10, 12% per unit of work and expanded its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework.

New Relic published its public AI Principles to reinforce its governance baseline. New Relic said it modernized its operations to curb carbon intensity as compute demands scale. 42Gears said it enables IT teams and MSPs to start where they are and grow without switching, scaling from endpoint management and Zero Trust security to identity and access management, automation, and self-healing technology. 42Gears said it goes beyond traditional MDM and RMM. The articles leave open the date of the BSI audit and the specific terms of New Relic's EU AI Pact commitment.

stories.Headline: Timirah and Mia James found Sonic Intelligence Academy to hold first AI Music Awards
stories.Summary:
The Sonic Intelligence Academy held the first AI Music Awards on Friday, November 14, 2026, at the Mayan Theater in Downtown Los Angeles. Software engineer Timirah James and her sister Mia James created the organization to normalize tech-assisted tunes and support AI creators. The event featured a red carpet with human creators and a text-to-speech agent developed by the top sponsor, Deepgram. Xania Monet won both artist and song of the year, while DJ Shawn Q took the producer of the year award. Telisha Jones, the human behind Xania Monet, had previously won the AI Album of the Year at a summit.

Artists must register tracks to the Verified Registry to specify if songs are fully AI-generated, AI-assisted, or human and AI hybrids. Registered artists nominate peers and vote across 25 categories, including Best AI Pop Song and Best AI Comedic Song. The organization launched its own AI charts in January 2026 to counter the mainstream industry and the Recording Academy. The event started at 6:45 p.m., thirty minutes after the scheduled 6:15 p.m. start, and featured a house band.

The Mayan Theater is located a twelve minute walk from the Crypto.com Arena, which is the longtime home of the Grammys. Timirah James and Mia James founded the academy to provide infrastructure for AI music rather than dismissing its existence. They advocate for artists to publicly associate themselves with AI-powered work to highlight the humans who helped create the product. Xania Monet creator Telisha Jones stated that AI is just a tool that emphasizes what creators do. Fredro Starr, who debuted the moniker Mad AI, claimed humans cannot be replaced and bring the spirit of hip-hop.

He touted his record, It All Started in Brooklyn, as the first AI album released on vinyl. The event affected nominees who missed hearing their names called because the show skipped introductions for the first half of awards. Guests included actor Giovanni Wilson and podcast host Lana Hout, who both served as hosts for the chaotic evening. Media coverage included twelve independent ventures on the carpet, though twenty-nine outlets had signed up before a flight ground-stop.

The company Trinity Social ran an ad featuring a Rockstar Games logo, which a Rockstar spokesperson did not authorize. Some industry figures, including Kehlani, previously criticized the three million dollar record deal received by Telisha Jones. The academy was launched in January to counter the music industry's aversion to AI and the legal questions surrounding copyright infringement. Lawsuits have been filed by record labels and artists against AI generators such as Udio and Suno over these issues.

The event used a Claude-generated run-of-show on a teleprompter that shifted rapidly and confused the hosts during the ceremony. A trailer for the film A Good Hand Wasted, starring Terrance Howard, was played but only showed a small portion. The evening was marked by technical failures, including a Deepgram AI voice that talked over the presenters. The hosts eventually presented the best AI country artist award thirteen minutes late after a confusing interruption regarding a commercial break.

The event ended with various technical kinks, such as the teleprompter acting erratically and the Deepgram commercials playing at random moments. It remains unclear if Rockstar Games will take legal action regarding the unauthorized use of its logo in the advertisement. stories.Headline: OECD reports AI adoption accelerates across member countries but gaps persist among businesses and generations
stories.Summary:
The OECD reported on 5 November 2026 that AI adoption is accelerating across its member countries, but that major gaps persist among businesses and between generations. The organisation said the world of work is changing rapidly because of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, along with new forms of work, greening, demographic change and globalisation. It also said critical minerals have become central to economic security, as they are essential to energy and digital transitions, defence and advanced manufacturing. The OECD published the findings on its website as part of its work on effective governance to harness the benefits of AI and mitigate its risks.

The OECD said its work on investment supports governments in attracting more and better-quality investment, with priority given to security and sustainability. It also described how the trend towards the international dispersion of certain value chain activities produces challenges, and said it offers policies to meet these. The organisation noted that its Programme for International Student Assessment, known as PISA, assesses the skills of 15-year-old students in reading, mathematics and science as core domains. The articles give no further figures, dates or names beyond these.

The OECD is responsible for the work described, and its statements were paraphrased in the articles rather than attributed to a named individual. The organisation framed the findings around applying effective governance to harness the benefits of AI and mitigate its risks. It presented the changing world of work as a result of new technologies, new forms of work, greening, demographic change and globalisation. It did not say in the articles what specific measures it recommends or who should carry them out.

The context given is that AI adoption is spreading quickly across OECD countries while gaps remain among businesses and generations. The articles do not say what happens next, beyond the OECD's stated focus on governance and on attracting better-quality investment. No further steps, deadlines or responses are reported.
