stories.Headline: Anthropic launches Nasdaq IPO to fund frontier models amid AI industry backlash
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is launching an initial public offering on the Nasdaq this Thursday, November 19, 2026, to raise money for its frontier models. The company is going public during a difficult period for the technology industry, which is currently facing a nationwide artificial intelligence backlash. This event follows a major political shift in Washington, D.C., and the sudden ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang early Thursday. The IPO arrives as investors seek a bright spot after the Nasdaq dropped 5.3 percent in October, its worst month since March 2025. This offering is considered a defining event for the young artificial intelligence market and the most important tech IPO in several years.

The IPO price is expected between 70 and 78 dollars a share, with a valuation of 1.4 trillion dollars and six times oversubscription. Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, Micron, Broadcom, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, and Advanced Micro Devices are collectively investing 26 billion dollars at this price. Anthropic has 900 billion dollars in spending commitments, including 110 billion dollars over ten years with Amazon and 400 billion dollars for cloud capacity. The lab committed 300 billion dollars to chip and data center partners and 125 billion to 150 billion dollars for Google chips. Google will own 13 percent of the company and backstop 19 billion dollars in lease commitments to Terawulf for Kentucky data centers.

Anthropic stated in its prospectus that it previously underestimated compute requirements, which constrained its capacity and impacted both product development and deployment. The company recorded a net loss of 104 billion dollars through the first nine months of 2026 before this public offering. Joe Fath of Eclipse called the staggering numbers hard to wrap one's head around, while David Tollen called it smart investing. Subhadeep Chatterjee, a former Google cloud partnerships leader, stated that everyone knows Anthropic is going to be the future of Google. Eli Mansoor of OskaQ Consulting said companies must rush to get infrastructure or they will be out of business.

The IPO affects major tech giants who need Anthropic's massive spending to continue for many years to come to drive the AI buildout. Corey Quinn of Duckbill said it is almost certain that the ten year Amazon contract will be renegotiated before it culminates. Investors are currently strained by rising interest rates, which have pushed them out of debt heavy neoclouds that are critical for infrastructure. Democratic victories in midterm elections and new ballot measures may potentially limit the development of new data centers across the country. Nvidia shareholders are affected as shares tumbled 13 percent this week to their lowest levels since July 2025 following the scandal.

Anthropic is a five year old company that has never lived through a technology downturn but is now burning historic amounts of money. The company has 132 billion dollars in existing cash and short term investments and could yield over 90 billion dollars in proceeds. Amazon previously built a custom chip data center in Indiana specifically for Anthropic, while cloud partners account for 31 percent of obligations. Bank of America, Blackstone, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley offered 63 billion dollars to buy Broadcom AI chip racks for Anthropic to rent. Broadcom has provided a backstop for these rentals with a maximum liability of 43 billion dollars to support the lab.

Nvidia interim CEO Colette Cress faces a major test on Tuesday when the company reports quarterly results two days before the Anthropic debut. stories.Headline: Anthropic ports AI model to AMD hardware in three days to reduce reliance on Nvidia software
stories.Summary:
Anthropic recently announced that its AI model could be ported to different hardware in just three days. This development occurred around November 15, 2026, and provides a major advantage to Advanced Micro Devices. The move potentially weakens the market dominance of Nvidia by reducing the reliance on its software. This shift allows AI labs to switch chip vendors much faster than was previously possible.

The process involved the Claude Mythos Preview model porting 100 percent of its kernels to AMD MI355 GPUs. This replaces a traditional process requiring twelve engineers and between six and twelve months of work. Anthropic aims to create a fungible compute pool using AMD, Nvidia, Amazon Trainium, and Alphabet Tensor Processing Units. AMD's Helios system costs roughly 20 billion dollars per gigawatt, while Nvidia's Vera Rubin costs 40 billion.

Anthropic stated that its goal was to bring any AI chip up to speed within a few days. The company wants to buy chips based on the best price performance regardless of the specific vendor. This strategy allows the lab to use different chips for model training or inference based on efficiency. By reducing the complexity of switching hardware, the company levels the playing field for semiconductor manufacturers.

Investors in AMD may benefit, while Nvidia faces potential losses in sales, gross margins, and overall profitability. The shift affects the semiconductor space by challenging the moat created by the Nvidia CUDA software platform. Some analysts suggest that AMD is now the top AI semiconductor stock to buy following this news. Others note that Nvidia still possesses the premier AI infrastructure solution and the best overall ecosystem.

Nvidia built its dominance by seeding the CUDA platform into universities and research labs for early AI work. This created a generation of developers who wrote original AI code optimized specifically for Nvidia chips. The company later expanded this ecosystem with CUDA-X to help scale high-performance computing workloads. Recently, Nvidia suffered reputational damage because its former CEO was linked to an alleged Chinese spy.

AMD will now roll out its new Helios system to compete for a larger market share. Nvidia still holds a lead by locking up supply-constrained high-bandwidth memory needed for chip performance. The articles leave open whether Nvidia will be forced to lower its prices to remain competitive. It remains unclear if AMD can overcome the performance lead of the Vera Rubin platform.

stories.Headline: Young South Koreans use AI to create fake funeral portraits as a prank
stories.Summary:
Young South Koreans are using generative artificial intelligence to create fake funeral portraits of themselves or their friends as a joke. This social media trend was reported on November 15, 2026, as a growing practice among the youth in Seoul. The prank involves posting these AI images on Instagram accompanied by memorial messages to trick people into thinking they died. Many of these posts are designed to look like genuine death announcements to confuse the people who see them. This trend has prompted various news reports to call for tighter regulation of the online platforms where they appear.

The posts feature black and white images styled as funeral portraits with phrases like Rest in peace or You will always be remembered. Some images include fabricated dates of death and dates of birth, along with white chrysanthemums and black ribbons for added realism. This specific practice has recently gained popularity among teenagers and people in their 20s as a prank among close friends. The images are shared on Instagram, which is the primary platform where this surge of AI generated content is occurring. These visual elements make the fake portraits very difficult to distinguish from real announcements of a person's passing.

Kim Si-deok is a professor in the department of funeral services at Eulji University who spoke to the South Korean media. He stated that younger generations are increasingly taking the significance of death and funeral traditions lightly through this specific social trend. The professor warned that this behavior trivialises death and urged online platforms to take steps to prevent such content from spreading. Meta, the parent company of Instagram, responded by saying it removes or restricts content that violates its community standards. The company told a local news outlet that it will continue working with outside organisations to maintain a safe environment.

Some people who are aware of the prank ask what food they should prepare for the fake memorial service in comments. Others are unaware that the posts are fake and offer sincere condolences, saying it is heartbreaking to see someone die young. Experts are affected by this trend and have called for stronger action from social media platforms to stop the practice. Meta noted that users can report manipulated images of private individuals, including minors, that are shared without their own consent. The company claims it promptly removes such content following a review to protect the users on its social platform.

The articles provide background on how generative AI is being used to create these deceptive images for social media entertainment. This trend is part of a broader context of AI use in South Korea, including fake chats and exam cheating. One mentioned case involved a man making over 100 prank calls to police to be sent to a jail. Another instance involved an actor named Lee Yi kyung whose lewd chats were created by an accuser using AI tools. These examples show a pattern of using artificial intelligence for deception or pranks within the South Korean society.

Meta will continue to review and remove manipulated images of private individuals that are reported by users on the Instagram platform. The company intends to keep working with relevant outside organisations to ensure that the social media environment remains safe. The articles leave open whether the calls for tighter regulation of online platforms will lead to new laws or rules. It is unclear if the trend among teenagers and people in their 20s will decrease after these expert warnings. The reports do not state if any specific legal actions will be taken against those posting the fake portraits.

stories.Headline: EU leaders postpone AI discussions to focus on Ukraine negotiations at Dublin summit
stories.Summary:
EU leaders gathered in Dublin on November 13 and 14 for a summit focused on artificial intelligence and regional security. The meetings were derailed when the Ukraine issue became the main focus after US envoys met with President Zelensky. European leaders shifted their attention to forming a negotiating team to speak with one voice to the outside world. The ninth European Political Community summit occurred Thursday, followed by an informal European Union leaders meeting on Friday. These high-level gatherings took place at the Convention Centre Dublin, which overlooks the River Liffey in Ireland.

The summit required a negotiating team consisting of EU institutions and five Coalition of the Willing countries, Britain, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland. Ursula von der Leyen proposed spending 30 billion euros, or 33.07 billion US dollars, to build seven AI gigafactories. She estimated that Europe actually needs at least 500 billion euros, or 551.10 billion dollars, to advance its broader technological ambitions. The 2023 Chips Act aimed for 20 percent of the global market, but the industry now declares this goal unattainable. Ireland held the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU during the second half of 2026.

European Council President Antonio Costa announced the formation of the negotiating team and said leaders would revisit AI in February 2027. Ursula von der Leyen outlined the gigafactory plans, while President Emmanuel Macron called for faster decisions and much greater investment. Macron and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten will convene a meeting of European technology leaders in Paris on December 2. President Zelensky described recent talks in Abu Dhabi as serious and urged Europe to secure a regular place in negotiations. These leaders sought a greater say in decisions affecting the future of Europe and the security of the region.

Around 1,000 pro-Palestinian demonstrators marched toward the National Gallery of Ireland to protest military spending and the neutrality of Ireland. More than 5,000 Irish police officers managed security, causing road closures and transport restrictions that disrupted daily life in Dublin. The Irish Times noted that these security operations caused public disruption and raised questions about the costs of hosting gatherings. The Centre for European Policy Studies warned that relying on foreign chip suppliers could create new and dangerous technological dependencies. The Financial Times reported that productivity gains from AI in Europe have remained modest despite some new industrial activity.

The 2000 Lisbon Strategy aimed to build a competitive knowledge economy by 2010, but it failed and became the Europe 2020 Strategy. This second strategy also failed because subsidizing farmers and saving factories wins more votes than spending on long-term competitiveness. Europe now faces funding gaps for Ukraine and a 22nd round of sanctions, with more financial discussions coming soon. The region struggles with strategic anxiety and a lack of hard power in computing, chips, and advanced AI models. This pattern shows a tendency to retreat to coordination rather than committing real money to achieve clear strategic objectives.

EU leaders will return to discuss Ukraine financing needs at their next meeting on November 26 and 27. Territorial disputes and security guarantees for Ukraine remain unresolved, and the appointment of a single European envoy is still open. The future of the AI gigafactory plan remains stalled and tied to negotiations over the next long-term EU budget. The articles leave open whether Europe can maintain strategic autonomy without depending on any third party for its international role. It remains unclear if the 27 member states will agree to pay the funds needed for technological competitiveness.

stories.Headline: Japanese manufacturers report higher profits as AI demand lifts earnings
stories.Summary:
Many publicly traded Japanese companies reported higher profits for the first half of the current business year ending in March. These financial gains occurred during the period from April to September and were driven by the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. Firms within the manufacturing sector performed particularly well as they capitalized on the robust demand for new technology. Several of these organizations have already revised their full-year earnings forecasts upward to reflect this growth.

The current economic shift requires these companies to adapt their production and financial planning to meet the surging demand for AI. This trend changes the outlook for the manufacturing sector by increasing the expected revenue for the remainder of the fiscal year. Every firm that closes its books in March must now account for these unexpected gains in their official reports. The surge in profits indicates a broader transition toward integrating artificial intelligence across various industrial applications.

Yoshimitsu Goto, who serves as the Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of SoftBank Group, spoke about these developments. He addressed the current business climate during an online news conference held on Tuesday to discuss the financial landscape. While the specific details of his remarks were not fully detailed, his presence highlighted the importance of the AI boom. He represents a major player in the technology sector that is closely monitoring these market shifts.

The broader context involves a period of significant growth for Japanese firms despite growing uncertainty in the global market. These companies are leveraging the AI boom to strengthen their positions against international competitors in the tech space. Future reports will likely determine if this profit trend continues through the end of the business year. Analysts are watching to see if other sectors beyond manufacturing will experience similar financial boosts.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Google agrees to pay $10 million for Spirit Airlines corporate data
stories.Summary:
Google agreed to pay $10 million for bankrupt Spirit Airlines’ corporate data, covering some 31 years of internal workflows, Cedar News reported on 2026-11-15. Cedar News said a new market is taking shape around one of businesses’ most overlooked assets, their internal data. The Cedar News item appeared under the headline that frontier labs are buying up internal company data to train AI. Cedar News said the marketplace is booming, despite privacy concerns. The potential payouts are substantial, Cedar News said.

Bain & Company estimated spending of up to US$6.5tn to build nearly 150GW of new compute capacity by 2030. Bain expected 20, 30% growth in data centre critical capacity over the next five years. Hyperscalers’ data centre CapEx could top US$1tn by 2028, Bain said. The number of semiconductor companies manufacturing the most advanced logic node fell 84%, from 25 companies in 2002, 2003 to 4 companies from 2020-2026. Global data centre electricity demand is estimated to more than double from an estimated 589TWh in 2026 to 1,228TWh in 2030, and North America’s virtual power plant market is 37.5GW.

Adam Mayer, Technical Product Marketing Director at Qlik, wrote in TechRadar on 13 November 2026 that data privacy is becoming harder to manage as businesses give AI applications and agents access to more internal systems. Mayer said much of the focus has been on the risk of AI models surfacing sensitive or confidential information in their responses, but the privacy challenge starts earlier. He said organizations also need to understand what data AI systems can access in the first place, where that data comes from and how it is being used. Mayer said 95% of enterprises have delayed or cancelled AI projects because of infrastructure and data governance challenges. He said businesses need to get the foundations right before privacy risks become impossible to contain.

Mayer said data privacy is not just a legal or compliance concern and should matter to everyone who touches data within an organization. He said the consequences of getting it wrong are growing, from exposing sensitive information to damaging customer trust and brand reputation. Mayer said poorly classified, duplicated or outdated data can carry existing privacy problems into AI applications, turning weaknesses previously contained within individual systems into much wider risks. He said agentic AI raises the stakes further because agents can increasingly surface and act on information across multiple parts of the business. Mayer said personally identifiable information such as names, addresses or financial details should be clearly labelled so it can be spotted before it is moved.

Mayer said identifying sensitive data is only the first step in managing the privacy challenge. He said businesses also need to track where it moves, particularly when information is copied from live systems into testing or development environments which may not have the same security controls in place. He said sensitive information should remain within the live systems where it is needed wherever possible. Mayer said removing or masking identifying details can reduce the risk of unnecessary exposure if data does need to be used elsewhere. Bain said building AI-ready data centres is proving as much a test of supply chains and power infrastructure as it is of capital.

Bain’s figures were drawn from the December Week 1 edition of Data Centre Magazine, which sets out the scale of the challenge from the spending required to deliver nearly 150GW of new compute capacity by 2030 to the shrinking number of manufacturers able to produce the most advanced chips. Bain’s figures also point to sharply rising electricity demand and a growing virtual power plant market in North America. Cedar News said the potential payouts are substantial, evidenced by Google’s agreement to pay $10 million for Spirit Airlines’ corporate data. TechRadar published Mayer’s opinion piece on 13 November 2026 under the title that AI privacy starts with your data. Data Centre Magazine published its Bain statistics article on November 15, 2026.

stories.Headline: Huawei Horinger data center has 7 percent of the compute of SpaceX Colossus 2
stories.Summary:
Ben Cottier and Lynette Bye analyzed Huawei's Horinger data center using satellite imagery on November 12, 2026. They found that this Chinese facility lags far behind the American Colossus 2. The researchers determined that Horinger has only seven percent of the compute of Colossus 2. This gap is expected to persist until at least 2028. Huawei is the biggest AI chip developer in China.

The Horinger campus in Inner Mongolia has three zones called West, South, and North. It requires up to 286 megawatts of IT power capacity across four buildings. The facility uses 105,000 Ascend 910C chips and 8,000 Ascend 910B chips. Colossus 2 is located in Tennessee and is the largest AI data center. The Horinger site demolished villages to make room for these buildings.

Epoch AI researchers are responsible for these findings and the cooling equipment model. They said that heat rejection capacity reveals the buildings' IT power capacity. The authors noted that moving fans create colored ghosts in satellite images. They stated that Horinger is likely one of the largest centers in China. They explained that US facilities extract 2.5 times more compute per unit of power.

The report affects China's AI capabilities and deployment capacity compared to the United States. Other Chinese centers like Huawei Wuhu and VNET Bayin Ulanqab may match Horinger. The analysis suggests that China's compute constraints will not ease for two years. A model like GPT-6 Astra would take one year to train at Horinger. This is possible if all current compute was combined for one run.

Huawei uses abundant energy in China to build these large AI data centers. US export controls cause Huawei to lag behind Nvidia in performance and efficiency. Nvidia's B200 and B300 chips perform at about 2.5 H100-equivalents each. Huawei's 910C chip performs at around 0.76 H100-equivalents. By March 2026, Huawei had sold 907,000 Ascend 910C and 600,000 Ascend 910B chips.

One building in the West zone should become operational by December 2026. A new building in the South zone may be operational by February 2028. This growth could increase Horinger's total AI compute by over 70 percent. Colossus 2 is expected to reach 1.8 million H100-equivalents by 2028. The articles leave open whether other Chinese data centers will fall further behind.

stories.Headline: Downing Street aide reads ChatGPT feedback on Burnham speech draft on train
stories.Summary:
An unnamed Downing Street speechwriter was photographed on Friday reading ChatGPT’s suggestions for making the prime minister’s speech more emotive, according to the Mail on Sunday. The aide to Andy Burnham was seen on the 5.03pm train from London Euston to Holyhead as Burnham and his team headed to the Welsh Labour conference with a bottle of bubbly. The pictures were taken while the aide sipped prosecco and read the AI chatbot’s feedback on a passage criticising the legacy of Margaret Thatcher. An image of the aide’s phone screen showed ChatGPT commenting on lines about Thatcher’s impact on working men’s clubs, choirs and other social infrastructure in the 1980s. Burnham later delivered the speech at the Welsh Labour Conference in Llandudno, in northern Wales, and did not use the specific passage seen in the pictures.

The chatbot said it preferred the second passage because it moves from the miners to their families to the wider community, showing how industrial work created bonds beyond the workplace. In the speech, Burnham said Thatcher shattered the way of life for communities up and down Britain with mines closed, factories closed and steelworks silenced. He also said cost of living is the top issue in Wales, as it is in all parts of the UK. Burnham spoke of the workplaces that created a way of life, the social infrastructure taken for granted, the working men’s clubs, the sports teams, the choirs and the trade unions, adding that people came together and looked out for each other. Elsewhere he said Labour had lost power in Wales after elections earlier this year, that the party may have lost sight of the principles that drove devolution, and that for the first time in its history Labour is not leading the Welsh Government.

A No 10 spokesperson said the PM writes most of his own speeches and that an aide sought feedback on a speech draft that had already been written. The Express reported the spokesperson saying the PM writes most of his own speeches and this one was no exception. Reform UK chairman Lee Anderson told the Mail on Sunday that it must be thirsty work writing speeches for Burnham. Anderson said his bubbly-drinking socialists have no plan to tackle the cost-of-living crisis and that AI Andy’s man-of-the-people act has been exposed as a sham. He added that Burnham is an artificial prime minister who does not have the faintest clue what he believes or what he is doing.

The use of ChatGPT and other AI chatbots by politicians and their aides has drawn plenty of attention since the tech first emerged earlier this decade. Addressing the House of Commons last year, Conservative MP Tom Tugendhat blasted colleagues for supposedly using AI to write their own speeches, saying the phrase I rise to speak is a giveaway. Tugendhat said all they were hearing was the ChatGPT generated press releases. He said ChatGPT knows you’re there, but that is an Americanism we don’t use, and told colleagues to keep using it because it makes clear the place has become absurd. The Express reported that the AI tool suggested using an emotive passage describing working men’s clubs, choirs and other social infrastructure lost as Britain moved away from its industrial base.

The photographs were taken on Friday as Burnham and his team travelled to the Welsh Labour conference, and the speech was delivered on Saturday. The Mail on Sunday published the pictures of the aide’s phone screen showing ChatGPT’s feedback on the Thatcher passage. The articles do not say whether the aide faced any disciplinary action or whether Downing Street investigated the matter further. They do not name the speechwriter or say how the photographs were obtained. They also do not say whether Burnham commented on the photographs himself.

stories.Headline: Character.ai files for bankruptcy as Ollie and Sora shut down
stories.Summary:
Character.ai filed for bankruptcy in October 2026, while the privacy assistant Ollie ceased operations a few weeks before that date. Many other projects failed, including the video platform Sora, which shut down in March 2026 due to high costs. The workflow tool Relay closed in August 2026, and Notion Mail is scheduled to shut down on September 22. Humane closed its AI Pin business in February 2025, and the browser ChatGPT Atlas ended on August 9.

The Character.ai sale to Disney involves a bid of 20 million dollars for certain intellectual property rights. Apple paid a 250 million dollar settlement after delaying the Siri AI upgrade, which finally appeared in iOS 27. Humane raised 230 million dollars before HP acquired most of its assets for 116 million dollars in February 2025. Character.ai previously raised 150 million dollars in 2023 and received 2.7 billion dollars from Google for technology licensing. The Rabbit R1 device debuted at CES in January 2024 and reportedly sold 100,000 units shortly after launch.

S&P Global Market Intelligence reports that 42 percent of AI projects fail because of funding or weak user demand. CEO Bill Lennon stated that Ollie would shut down on November 6 due to slow growth and funding issues. OpenAI rolled back a July 9 redesign of ChatGPT after users called the new interface confusing and cluttered. Microsoft delayed its Recall feature for nearly a year to reassess security safeguards after receiving strong privacy backlash. Apple cited engineering issues and bugs as the reasons for the repeated delays of its upgraded Siri AI.

Users of ChatGPT criticized the super app redesign, and families sued Character.ai over teen suicides and self-harm. Disney issued cease and desist letters to Character.ai, and customers were warned that Humane charging cases might catch fire. Cybersecurity researchers affected Microsoft by creating a tool that could extract sensitive data captured by the Recall photographic memory. Notion Mail users were already using standalone AI agents, which made the dedicated email product unnecessary for the market. Rabbit R1 users found the device to be unfinished and unstable according to early reviews of the hardware.

S&P Global notes that technical challenges, intense competition, and scaling difficulties contribute to the growing cemetery of failed AI projects. Character.ai was founded in 2021 by former Google researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas to create customizable bots. Ollie launched in June 2026 as a family assistant and was among the first mainstream apps with SOC 2. Relay operated for five years as a Zapier alternative before major platforms integrated similar automation features into their tools. Microsoft introduced Recall at the 2024 Build developer conference to allow users to search their digital history via screenshots.

The Character.ai transaction with Disney is expected to be completed by late November or early December of the year 2026. Siri AI is currently being rolled out to English users, with support for additional languages expected to follow soon. CFT regulations may influence the future viability of AI projects, though the articles do not specify the exact rules. The articles leave open whether Microsoft has truly fixed the underlying security issues regarding the controversial Recall memory feature. It remains unclear if the Rabbit R1 will be updated to fix the unstable performance noted by early reviewers.

stories.Headline: Microsoft removes WordPad from Windows 11 as users restore it manually
stories.Summary:
The author copied WordPad from a fresh Windows 10 installation to a Windows 11 26H2 PC, as reported by Windows Latest on November 15, 2026. Microsoft had removed WordPad from Windows 11 version 24H2, and the app is still missing in 26H2. The author said he recently updated his father's PC to Windows 11 26H2, and his father asked whether it had WordPad. When told Microsoft had deprecated it, his father sighed and said it was enough for him. The author saw someone on X complain about the new Notepad a few days earlier, and most replies favored the post.

Microsoft deprecated WordPad in September 2023, saying it was no longer being updated and would be removed in a future release of Windows. In March 2024, the company confirmed WordPad would be gone from all editions of Windows 11 24H2 and Windows Server 2025. Three files were removed: wordpad.exe, wordpadfilter.dll and write.exe, and Windows no longer has a built-in RTF reader. Microsoft recommends Word for rich-text documents like .rtf and .doc, and Notepad for .txt files. WordPad arrived with Windows 95 in August 1995, replacing Microsoft Write, and the Windows 95 Reviewer's Guide admitted it was not a full-blown word processor.

Microsoft's developer documentation mentions the three removed files, and Microsoft's old Knowledge Base article Q135079 lists tables, borders, shading and columns among the Word formatting that disappears in WordPad, calling it a design limitation of WordPad. Microsoft's support page says Notepad's Writing Tools are powered by GPT, which means users must sign in with a Microsoft account to use them. Microsoft's old WordPad help page warned that headers, footers or comments opened in WordPad and saved would be lost. Microsoft did test Office banner ads inside WordPad in a January 2020 Windows 10 Insider build, but they were hidden behind a feature flag. Microsoft never formally announced a change of plans about the Ignite features, but they seem no longer under development.

The author said the Copilot branding is gone from Notepad, the Writing Tools can be switched off, and formatting or tables isn't hurting anyone. He said he doesn't mind the new features and sometimes uses them, but WordPad has no account prompt or AI button and won't get any updates. He said a missing spell check hurts the most, especially when the new Notepad has it, and that for a resume or a document with tracked changes, Word or the free Word for the web is still the right tool. Notepad got a Create a table option for everyone in January 2026, but those tables, along with bold, italics, headings and lists, are stored as Markdown in a plain-text file. PCMag's Chris Hoffman wrote that Microsoft unveiled several major Windows features at Ignite last year, such as a way for AI agents to access Windows desktop apps, but many never made it out of Insider builds.

WordPad sat between Notepad and Word for almost three decades, and its Office-style ribbon came with Windows 7. The Home tab has fonts and sizes, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, subscript and superscript, text highlighting and font colors, plus alignment, indentation, line spacing and bulleted lists. The Insert group lets you add pictures, date and time, and objects from other apps, and a ruler lets you drag paragraph margins. WordPad documents save as RTF by default, but it can also save .docx, .odt and plain text files. At Build earlier this year, Microsoft announced experimental tools including Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) to safely sandbox OpenClaw agents, and at Ignite last year it debuted an on-device MCP server registry for Windows and a File Explorer MCP connector.

The author's archive has wordpad.exe, WordpadFilter.dll and an en-US folder with wordpad.exe.mui, and users copy them into C:\Program Files\Windows NT\Accessories and approve the administrator prompt. WordPad won't appear in Start menu search this way, so users pin it to the taskbar and set it as the default app for .rtf files from Open with > Choose another app. WordPad doesn't get security fixes anymore, so the author advises avoiding RTF or DOCX files from people you don't trust. Ignite runs from Nov. 17 to 20 at the Moscone Center in San Francisco, and CEO Satya Nadella will kick off the enterprise-focused event with a keynote. The keynote starts at 10 p.m. in Dubai, 9 p.m. in Riyadh and 8 p.m. in Cairo, and the free digital pass is open to anyone, wherever they live.

stories.Headline: Physicist Nathaniel Craig and GPT-6 Astra propose a lattice definition of the Standard Model
stories.Summary:
Physicist Nathaniel Craig, a visiting scientist at OpenAI, worked with GPT-6 Astra on a candidate lattice definition of the Standard Model, as described in a guest post on OpenAI's science blog dated November 15, 2026. Craig leads the particle theory group at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics. In an October preprint prepared with the aid of GPT-6 Astra, Craig proposed a candidate definition on a lattice, a grid representing spacetime. Craig had a strategy for tackling the problem but had not been able to prove it worked in all the cases it needed to cover. Astra helped turn that strategy into a construction and took the lead in developing the detailed proof.

The Standard Model describes the known elementary particles and three of the four fundamental forces: the strong force, the weak force, and electromagnetism. Its success rests on agreement between theoretical calculations and experiments across eighteen orders of magnitude, from the low energies of hydrogen's 21-centimeter radio emission to the high energies of collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. For more than fifty years a foundational problem has remained: how to give the full theory a nonperturbative definition that does not treat its interactions as small corrections. Perturbation theory has let physicists predict the strength of the electron's magnetism to within a few parts in a trillion. For the full Standard Model in continuous spacetime, there is no nonperturbative definition, or even an understanding of whether the interacting theory is mathematically well defined.

Craig wrote that a promising alternative is to discretize spacetime into a grid of points known as a lattice, whose spacing defines the shortest distance the theory can resolve. Studying a finite grid allows a rigorous nonperturbative definition of the theory at a given spacing and enables calculations on a computer without perturbation theory. This approach, lattice field theory, has led to remarkable progress in understanding the strong force, including a quantitative understanding of the proton's mass from first principles. Craig explained that the Standard Model is a chiral theory, meaning it looks different under reflection in space, because the weak force treats left- and right-handed fermions differently. He wrote that putting chiral theories on a lattice is profoundly challenging, since the most natural rules give a left-handed fermion a right-handed partner you never asked for, a problem called doubling.

Craig described an analogy with light, in which a box with ordinary mirrors turns left-circular light into right-circular light, much as doublers appear when a left-handed fermion is put on the lattice. He wrote that chiral mirrors made of special films whose molecules line up in layers can send left-handed light back left-handed and let right-handed light pass through. Such chiral mirrors have been around for more than a decade, and the phenomenon even occurs in nature, in the shiny shells of some scarab beetles. Decades ago, Paul Ginsparg and Nobel laureate Ken Wilson worked out the lattice rules analogous to the requirement that chiral mirrors reverse the rotation of the electric field upon reflection. Rajamani Narayanan and Herbert Neuberger built the analog of the chiral mirrors by finding the necessary definition of fundamental particles on the lattice, known as overlap fermions.

Martin Lüscher showed how to tell the difference between left-handed and right-handed overlap fermions on the lattice, while Yoshio Kikukawa and collaborators explored how this might be used to describe weak interactions in the Standard Model. Craig wrote that one piece was still missing, which he identified as getting the phase right. He explained the optical phase by imagining water waves rolling past the pilings of a dock, and the relative phase of two waves determining how much they add or cancel at the same point. In a box with chiral mirrors, left-circular light bounces back and forth, and after a lap the returning light meets fresh light from the laser going in the same direction. If their electric fields are in step, the light builds up inside the box, and if the fields are half a cycle apart, the returning light cancels some of the fresh light.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Stanford review finds most AI education tools do not improve student learning
stories.Summary:
The AI Hub for Education, part of Stanford University’s SCALE Initiative, released a review of 52 studies on artificial intelligence in educational settings on Tuesday, November 13, 2026, Chalkbeat reported. The review found that most AI tools do not help students learn and that education-specific AI tools are not necessarily better than general purpose chatbots. It also found that even tools that help teachers save time can have unintended consequences for students. The report’s authors said they are not throwing in the towel on AI in education. The review is the AI Hub’s second AI research review and incorporates 32 new studies.

The included studies were selected from hundreds in the field and are either randomized controlled trials or have a quasi-experimental design providing strong causal evidence. The goal is eventually to have a robust research repository that teachers and districts can use to inform decisions about whether and how to use AI. The review is a synthesis of findings from high-quality studies, not a meta-analysis. AI in education is not just one thing, with too many different tools used in too many different ways to pile studies together and reach strong conclusions. Many of the studies come from other countries or involve college students, and there is still very little research on AI in K-12 settings in the United States.

Susanna Loeb, faculty director at the SCALE Initiative and an author of the report, said AI tools can be quite powerful to differentiate lessons for students at different levels or support students learning a new language. She said you just have to use them thoughtfully and track how they are doing and whether they are really benefiting students. Loeb said that if a district does not want to think about it and does not want to design its classwork, homework and school day to leverage these tools well, she would not use them. She said that on their own without thought, the tools have some negative effects on learning. She said teachers and district leaders need to proceed thoughtfully and that if they do not have the capacity to do so, it is better not to use AI at all.

Collectively, the studies suggest students do not learn much when they use AI to produce essays or solve problems, and when those students later do work without AI, they do worse than other students. AI shows more promise when students use it to explain concepts and help them practice, but even then the results are mixed or do not show much benefit over traditional study methods. AI tools that provide interactive formats and adaptive practice questions may improve student learning more than static digital textbooks, and students sometimes experience AI-generated feedback as clearer and more motivating than feedback from teachers, but even where students reported positive experiences the evidence of learning gains was mixed. Teachers who used an AI tool to do the first pass on grading assignments provided more and more detailed feedback in one study, and teachers who used AI progress-tracking tools saw students complete more assignments, though students’ grades on those assignments were not necessarily better.

Studies found teachers could save time using AI to generate lesson plans without reducing the quality of those lessons, but students who believed a lesson was AI-generated reported being less motivated, and in one study from Turkey students did worse when teachers who already were lower-performing used AI to generate lesson plans. The review comes as school districts are navigating competing pressures to adopt AI rapidly and to limit technology in the classroom. Google caused an uproar this month when it said that school districts that ban AI will not be able to use Google Search. The American Federation of Teachers has embraced training teachers to use AI while pressing major tech companies to agree to guardrails.

A forensic audit found serious flaws in a number of previous meta-analyses that found positive outcomes for AI in education, such as hallucinated references and statistics that did not make sense, according to The Hechinger Report. Another challenge with studying AI in education, particularly with younger students, is that they often do not want to use the tools. The report’s authors said the technology has potential to provide personalized assistance for students and remove some of the tedium from teachers’ jobs, and Loeb said that potential is worth developing. The articles do not say what specific steps districts or the AI Hub will take next.

The articles do not say how the 52 studies break down by country or age group. The articles do not name the other authors of the report. The articles do not say when the AI Hub’s research repository will be complete. The articles do not say how Google’s statement will affect districts that ban AI.

stories.Headline: Bogdan Pătrăucean releases Wintoys 3.0 with an option to disable Windows 11 AI services
stories.Summary:
Wintoys 3.0, build 3.0.10.0, was released by developer Bogdan Pătrăucean and announced on Reddit, adding an AI components option under the Optimizations tab. The free tool is distributed through the Microsoft Store and runs on Windows 10 and Windows 11 through a WinUI 3 interface. The option disables background services such as WorkloadsSessionHost.exe, which hold machine-learning models in memory for features like Windows Recall and semantic search. Pătrăucean said those services can use 2GB to more than 8GB of RAM, including while the related features sit idle. On his 16GB Surface Pro 12, he reported that switching them off cut memory use from 11GB to about 5GB.

The option is limited to Copilot+ PCs with a neural processing unit, and on conventional desktops the entry is not expected to appear at all. Wintoys 3.0 also adds a separate Artificial Intelligence section for managing Recall, Click to Do, Notepad's writing tools and agentic search, with toggles depending on installed hardware and Windows features. Profiles exports and restores a Windows setup as a JSON file and requires the paid Wintoys+ add-on, a one-time purchase with lifetime access, while earlier functions remain free. A new Configuration mode applies settings as preferences or policies where the operating system supports it, improving synchronization with the Windows Group Policy Editor. The build also brings extra privacy controls, File Explorer preloading options, a reworked storage cleaner, clearer restart prompts and bug fixes.

Pătrăucean described the memory figures as individual observations rather than controlled benchmarks, and said actual savings will vary with hardware, software configuration and which AI workloads are active. He pointed to a Microsoft Q&A thread from July 2026 in which a different user described recovering about 5GB by halting the Windows AI Fabric service and its associated workload processes. He said the AI components option targets WorkloadsSessionHost.exe, which can run in multiple instances to keep models ready. He pitched Profiles at people setting up a fresh install or provisioning several machines. He said Configuration mode matters because policy refreshes can otherwise revert changes made by third-party tweakers.

The articles say disabling AI services can break the features that depend on them, and that users on work or organization-managed computers are advised to weigh the implications of each tweak because some changes may conflict with corporate configuration. The articles say Copilot+ machines ship with the AI stack enabled by default, and on 16GB configurations the resident models can consume a meaningful share of system memory. The articles say IT administrators may find the Group Policy synchronization the more consequential addition, since managed machines often have settings locked down by policy. The articles say the tool comes from an unverified third-party source rather than Microsoft's own settings app. The articles say Wintoys has been free since its launch and Profiles marks one of the first capabilities reserved for paying supporters.

The articles say Microsoft has worked to trim Windows 11's memory footprint, an effort the company has discussed publicly in recent months. The articles say Wintoys takes a more granular route by exposing individual components rather than waiting for Microsoft to retune them. The articles say the release lands as that Microsoft effort continues. The articles say Wintoys lets users manage system settings, uninstall applications, optimize performance and control privacy features. The articles say the update was detailed by the developer.

The articles say Wintoys 3.0 can be downloaded at no charge from the Microsoft Store. The articles say whether users who came for the memory savings will follow into the paid tier is an open question. The articles leave open the actual savings on other machines, since the figures are individual observations rather than controlled benchmarks. The articles leave open which toggles appear, since that depends on installed hardware and Windows features present on the system. The articles say users should review the implications of individual tweaks before applying them.

stories.Headline: Pedro Pascal says filming Behemoth! gives him hope amid the AI boom
stories.Summary:
Tony Gilroy wrote and directed the Searchlight film Behemoth!, which stars Pedro Pascal and premieres in theaters on December 4. The movie focuses on a fight for humanity and explores if artificial intelligence can replace the humanizing element of cinema. Pascal plays Alex Serian, a former child prodigy cellist who returns home to Los Angeles to compose film scores. This story also follows the main character as he attempts to reconnect with his family through his musical work. The production serves as a lyrical love letter to the music of the movies according to a review.

The film features a cast including Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Will Arnett, Hank Azaria, Margarita Levieva, and Matthew Lillard. It requires a focus on organic storytelling to push back against the current boom of artificial intelligence in art. The plot centers on the city of Los Angeles where the protagonist returns to pursue his professional composing career. Searchlight Pictures is the studio responsible for releasing the movie on the specific date of December 4. Every department involved in the film worked with a purity of love despite not making money on the project.

Pedro Pascal told Vanity Fair that the experience of shooting the movie injected him with a tremendous amount of hope. He noted that the most expensive people were involved because of their talent and experience rather than for profit. Pascal believes there is a thrilling pushback occurring this year through movies that fight for humanity and storytelling. He stated that people want to be connected, tell each other's stories, and look after one another as humans. The actor was surprised that Gilroy made the film so intimate and healing instead of being mean.

Tony Gilroy stated that there is a clear natural resistance to the robot takeover in the music and film industries. He believes that people want humans and noted that the music scene has been dying for fifteen years. Gilroy suggested that people should blow up AI centers at the voting box by going and voting against them. He admitted that an algorithm could probably replace the emotional amplitude of movies, but this specific film is organic. The director is a two time Oscar nominee who champions the humanity of art over an over-reliance on AI.

The articles explain that the music scene has been struggling for fifteen years but is now grooving a little bit. This background sets the stage for a film that emphasizes organic human connection over the efficiency of artificial intelligence. The production involved highly experienced talent who worked together in a contagious environment of love for the creative process. The film was screened at the New York Film Festival where it received a positive lyrical review. These elements combine to create a project that resists the current trend of using AI in the arts.

The movie will officially premiere in theaters on December 4 to bring its message of humanity to the general public. Future developments regarding the fight for creativity and politics in cinema remain open as the AI boom continues growing. It is unclear what will happen next in the industry or what specific elements of cinema will return. The articles leave open whether the pushback against AI will successfully protect the humanizing elements of the movie business. The long term impact of this organic approach to filmmaking remains to be seen after the premiere.

stories.Headline: MegaETH cuts about 20 percent of staff while it develops an AI marketplace
stories.Summary:
MegaETH, an Ethereum scaling project, has reportedly reduced its workforce by about 20 percent while it develops a new artificial-intelligence business, according to reporting cited by TradingView News on November 15, 2026. The same reporting described plans to direct roughly $30 million from treasury resources toward an AI-related marketplace scheduled for December. The articles do not name the executives who made the decision or give the exact date the cuts took effect. They also do not say how many employees were affected in absolute numbers.

The reported figures include value locked in the MegaETH ecosystem at about $8.8 million, down from an earlier period above $240 million. The articles note that total value locked can move for many reasons, including token prices, rewards programmes and the exit of a few large liquidity providers, so it is not a complete measure of adoption or revenue. Reporting also referenced a planned decentralisation milestone in March 2027, which the articles say matters because it speaks to who controls upgrades and critical infrastructure. The articles stress that the $30 million allocation and the December marketplace are plans, not proof of an operating product or revenue.

The articles do not quote MegaETH executives directly and do not attribute specific statements to named company officials. They frame the open questions instead: whether applications are attracting repeat users without incentives, whether the network delivers the promised speed and reliability, and whether independent developers can ship products people want. On the AI marketplace, the articles say it would need to answer ordinary product questions about customers, the service being sold, the business model and why this particular blockchain improves the experience. They add that a broad trend toward blockchain and AI connections is not a commercial plan in itself.

The articles place the situation against difficult market conditions for Ethereum, including ETF outflows covered in a separate NewsBTC report, and describe MegaETH's case as a company-specific test on top of that. They say the next meaningful update will be evidence of both product execution and the original network commitments, rather than a new roadmap graphic. The articles do not say what MegaETH has announced about next steps beyond the December marketplace plan and the March 2027 milestone.

stories.Headline: AC Milan appoints Rúben Amorim as head coach as AI posts falsely claim Paolo Maldini returns
stories.Summary:
Recent national headlines warned that New Orleans was replacing 911 professionals with AI, and the reports were wrong, but the misinformation spread quickly amid the firestorm surrounding this new technology. The U.S. is not handing its emergency response system over to computers, and AI is making emergency communications faster and more resilient while trained 911 professionals remain in charge. Viral posts on Instagram and Threads claimed that AC Milan legend Paolo Maldini had returned to the club as head coach of its men's first team. The posts were designed to resemble genuine football transfer and appointment announcements, complete with the familiar excitement of a "Here we go!" update.

The creators included a disclaimer reading "CONCEPT ART • AI | FICTIONAL SCENARIO," indicating that the announcement is an AI-generated concept rather than an actual development. AI can identify and translate other languages almost instantly, whereas bringing a human translator on the line takes precious minutes, and it can support realistic training simulations that better equip new hires for the demands of the job. It can analyze far more calls for quality assurance than supervisors could review manually, helping ensure call-takers perform at their best. AI can also help relieve the burden of routine, non-emergency calls coming to 911 centers, roughly two-thirds of all calls handled by 911 centers according to the 2025 Pulse of 911 survey, freeing telecommunicators to focus on calls where lives are on the line. The Enhancing First Response Act (S. 725) would correct the longstanding federal misclassification of 911 telecommunicators as secretarial and administrative personnel rather than the protective service professionals they truly are.

Having passed the Senate unanimously, the legislation now awaits action in the House, and Congress should encourage responsible innovation by passing bipartisan funding legislation to support the nationwide transition to an all-digital Next Generation 911 system. John Provenzano is CEO of NENA: The 9-1-1 Association, a nonprofit professional organization representing tens of thousands of 9-1-1 first responders across the U.S. He wrote that emergency calls are not ordinary customer-service transactions and that 911 has always depended on a direct personal connection. He said someone reporting a heart attack, hiding from an attacker, or helping an injured child may need calm reassurance, lifesaving instructions, or sound judgment amid confusion and changing facts. He wrote that human intuition and empathy are essential features of 911 that AI cannot replace, and that AI will not change the fundamental social contract that has existed since the beginning: when a citizen calls for help, 911 will answer. He called on Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.)

to bring the bill up for consideration during the lame-duck session under suspension of the rules. Provenzano wrote that the question is not whether AI is categorically "dangerous" or "safe" but whether we can harness its potential while ensuring the safety, reliability, privacy and public trust that underpin emergency response. He wrote that realizing that promise will require thoughtful implementation, clear standards and continued investment in both people and infrastructure. The football article said that with realistic-looking graphics and the emotional appeal of a legendary football figure returning home, such posts can easily confuse fans who come across them while scrolling through their feeds.

It said that for supporters who are emotionally invested in their clubs, the prospect of a beloved former player returning to the dugout can be particularly tempting to believe. It said that a quick check of official club announcements and credible sports publications can save fans from falling for an elaborate digital prank. Provenzano wrote that the 911 system Americans rely on today has come a long way since the first call made nearly 60 years ago. He wrote that over the decades 911 has repeatedly adopted new technologies to better serve the public, from mobile phones and text messages to digital data-sharing and streaming video, and that the system has evolved alongside Americans' technology preferences.

He wrote that AI is the next step in this evolution and that the industry's experience in safely implementing previous technologies will guide it now. AC Milan officially appointed Portuguese manager Rúben Amorim as head coach of its men's first team on June 16, 2026, following the departure of Massimiliano Allegri. The former Manchester United and Sporting CP manager was welcomed by the Italian club as part of its plans to rebuild the team. Paolo Maldini has never pursued a coaching career, and after hanging up his boots he remained associated with AC Milan in an administrative capacity, serving as the club's technical director until June 2023.

He also briefly took up the role of technical director at the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) in July 2026, but resigned after just 16 days. The football article said that AI-generated content is increasingly blurring the lines between football news and digital fiction, and that fabricated stories can acquire the appearance of genuine breaking news. It said that while AI can recreate the excitement of a dream managerial appointment, it cannot make that appointment real. It said that Maldini's return to AC Milan might make for a wonderful fictional football story, but Amorim is the man in the hot seat.

stories.Headline: Kovind urges lawyers to verify AI-generated citations as AI reshapes legal work
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence has moved into courtrooms, law offices and legal research departments across the country, according to TechSpective on November 14, 2026. The article says the technology is no longer confined to science fiction or Silicon Valley boardrooms. It describes the rise of AI as both an opportunity and a genuine shift in how legal work gets done. It says attorneys, paralegals and clients alike face this change. It adds that understanding these changes is essential for anyone navigating today’s legal landscape.

AI-driven platforms scan thousands of case files, statutes and legal precedents in minutes, work that once took junior associates hours or full days. The tools retrieve information and also analyze patterns and surface insights a human researcher might overlook under time pressure. AI tools help lawyers identify problematic clauses, inconsistencies and missing provisions faster than manual review, and can be trained to flag language deviating from standard agreements or posing legal risks. Predictive analytics tools evaluate how courts have ruled on similar cases, and AI-driven e-discovery platforms streamline document review during discovery. A probate litigation attorney in California may use AI-assisted research and case analysis in complex matters like estate disputes involving contested wills or trust administration.

Former President Ram Nath Kovind said human judgment and oversight must remain indispensable to protect the credibility of courts and the rights of litigants, the Deccan Chronicle reported on November 14, 2026. Speaking at the Justice K. Ramaswamy Endowment Lecture at Dr B.R. Ambedkar College of Law, Andhra University, in Visakhapatnam on Saturday, he cautioned young advocates against blindly relying on AI-generated case laws and judicial precedents. He said, in the article’s words, that professional credibility cannot be transferred to a software provider. He urged advocates to personally verify legal assertions from authentic sources, including original judgments, rather than rely on software to validate its own output. He said technology should democratise access to justice instead of widening the gap between metropolitan law firms and lawyers practising in district courts.

Kovind cited the US case of Mata vs Avianca Inc., in which lawyers were penalised for submitting fictitious case citations generated by AI. He also referred to the Supreme Court case of Pooja Ramesh Singh v. Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd., where orders based on fabricated citations were set aside. He noted that more than 83,000 Supreme Court judgments were available in 18 Indian languages and said AI could accelerate translations while human supervision preserved the nuances and precision of legal terminology.

He urged law schools to adapt teaching methods to the digital era by emphasising critical thinking, legal research and oral advocacy, and to train future lawyers to examine electronic evidence and identify deepfakes. He said the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam and the Bharatiya Nararik Suraksha Sanhita showed India’s legal framework had recognised the growing importance of electronic records and digital proceedings. TechSpective says questions around data privacy, attorney-client privilege and the accuracy of AI-generated outputs are at the forefront of ongoing legal and ethical debates. It says bar associations and regulatory bodies are actively working to establish guidelines keeping AI use within appropriate ethical boundaries.

It warns that over-reliance on automated tools could lead to critical errors if attorneys accept AI outputs without proper scrutiny, and that the most effective approach treats AI as a powerful assistant rather than a substitute for genuine professional legal judgment. It says legal fees may decrease as efficiency improves and turnaround times on documents and case updates can be significantly faster, while AI-powered client portals and chatbots make basic legal information easier to access and let people communicate with legal teams outside traditional office hours. It says the overall client experience is becoming more transparent, more responsive and far more service-oriented. Kovind paid tribute to Justice K. Ramaswamy, recalling his contribution to the landmark S.R. Bommai judgment and the constitutional principle of secularism.

He concluded by urging young lawyers to combine technological skills with constitutional values and a commitment to justice, saying technology provides powerful tools but will never possess a conscience. TechSpective says the human element of law, including empathy, ethical reasoning and nuanced judgment, remains irreplaceable, and that attorneys who thrive will embrace AI as a tool while prioritising the personal and professional skills that define excellent legal practice. It says the future of law is both human and machine working together toward better outcomes. The articles leave open which guidelines bar associations and regulatory bodies will adopt and when.

stories.Headline: Rajnath Singh urges AI and robotics integration in defence testing for self-reliance
stories.Summary:
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh urged greater use of artificial intelligence, machine learning and robotics in Non-Destructive Testing, TechGig reported on November 15, 2026. He spoke virtually at a three-day conference organised by the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing in Hyderabad. The TechGig report was published on November 15, 2026 at 09:54 PM IST. Singh called for integrating these technologies to boost India's defence capabilities and strategic self-reliance. He said technological innovation is crucial for strengthening the nation's defence ecosystem.

Singh addressed the joint inauguration of the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation and Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace. More than 2,000 industry leaders, researchers and professionals gathered in Hyderabad for the event, Pragativadi reported on November 15, 2026. Singh said India must move from being a mere consumer of advanced technologies to becoming a global developer, innovator and leader in critical domains. He called for rapid domestic development in specialised sensors, evaluation equipment and associated software to secure critical supply chains. He said there can be zero compromise on the integrity of testing results in strategic applications.

Singh said India's pursuit of Aatmanirbharta in defence is not merely an economic objective but also a strategic necessity. He warned that hidden defects can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce service life and jeopardise mission success. He said the sector needs to move beyond merely identifying defects towards preventing them by embedding quality at every stage of manufacturing. He praised government catalysts such as Innovations for Defence Excellence and the Technology Development Fund. He called for a whole-of-government and whole-of-ecosystem approach uniting public sector undertakings, private manufacturers, start-ups, MSMEs, academia and research laboratories.

Singh said AI, ML, robotics, advanced sensors, digital twins and predictive analytics are expanding the possibilities of inspection and structural health monitoring. He said these technologies can improve inspection speed and consistency, facilitate complex data analysis and help identify defects conventional methods might miss. He urged NDT professionals to continuously upgrade their skills and embrace innovation in line with emerging technologies and evolving security requirements. He advocated greater indigenous innovation, urging India to develop solutions tailored to its strategic and industrial needs rather than merely adopting emerging technologies. He said investment in research, advanced equipment, software and skilled manpower would strengthen domestic capabilities and help Indian technologies access international markets.

Singh used a medical analogy, explaining that just as X-rays and ultrasounds examine the human body without surgery, NDT allows engineers to inspect vital defence hardware without dismantling or damaging it. He said this hardware includes missiles, naval vessels and spacecraft. He noted that India's indigenous arsenal is growing more sophisticated, exemplified by milestones like the aircraft carrier INS Vikrant and advancements in radar and missile systems. He said testing protocols must evolve as a result. The three-day conference in Hyderabad continues to serve as a hub for technical deliberation, fostering partnerships aimed at future-proofing India's aerospace and defence manufacturing sectors.

The articles do not state what specific policy changes, funding commitments or timelines, if any, follow from Singh's remarks. They do not say whether the government will mandate AI, ML or robotics in defence NDT or set targets for indigenous adoption. They do not name the specific officials, PSUs, start-ups or institutions that would take part in the proposed whole-of-ecosystem approach. They do not give the conference's closing date or any outcomes expected from it. They do not say how Indian testing technologies would access international markets or what barriers currently exist.

stories.Headline: Stanford AI Index reports global corporate AI investment tops $1 trillion in 2026
stories.Summary:
Global corporate investment in artificial intelligence has surpassed $1 trillion so far in 2026, already exceeding the entire 2025 total by 46 percent, according to new findings from the Stanford AI Index. The figures were released in a Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence article published on November 15, 2026, and written by AI Index editor Sha Sajadieh. The article says the money underscores an economic ambition of extraordinary scale, committed to a technology whose consequences are still being learned how to measure. The findings also describe effects unfolding in real time, from shifts in talent migration to emerging evidence in labor markets and expanding physical infrastructure that communities are being asked to accommodate.

The article reports that in every country surveyed, more people expect AI to eliminate jobs than to create them. In the United States, 60 percent of adults say they would feel uncomfortable with a new data center in their area, including majorities in both political parties, while globally a majority of survey respondents still believe AI's benefits outweigh its drawbacks. Data from the Stanford HAI Digital Economy Lab's AI Economic Indicators show that employment declines among younger workers in AI-exposed occupations have continued into 2026, particularly in customer service. A new finding broadens the concern, because declines have deepened even in occupations where AI supports rather than replaces human work, including roles such as marketing and IT managers. The article states that these patterns do not establish causality but raise important questions about how AI's economic effects may differ across the workforce.

Sajadieh is responsible for the article as the AI Index editor, and the Index describes its mission as providing unbiased, rigorously vetted, and globally sourced data for policymakers, researchers, journalists, executives, and the general public. The article says the findings come as the 2027 AI Index report is being prepared, with annual and year-to-date datasets refreshed periodically, and it recalls that last year's report documented a widening gap between capability, deployment, and readiness. It also asks whether the future being financed is the same future people expect, experience, or want for themselves, noting that public sentiment is turning out to be just as jagged as AI's technical frontier. The next AI Index will be released in April 2027.

stories.Headline: University of Michigan researchers find generative AI consumes more energy for non-English text
stories.Summary:
Researchers from University of Michigan Engineering discovered that generative AI consumes significantly more energy when processing non-English text. This study was presented at the Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing conference of the Association for Computational Linguistics. The team analyzed three open-source models, including Meta's Llama 3.1, Google's Gemma 3, and Alibaba's Qwen 3. They found that these models often produce lower-quality output while using more power.

The energy cost for non-English text ranges from 1.4 to 180 times that of English. Bengali requires 15.3 times more energy, while Hindi needs 7.9 times more. Most Western European languages use twice as much energy or less. These disparities affect roughly 5.2 billion people who must pay more or switch languages. This occurs because non-Latin scripts require more tokens, which consumes more memory and power.

Naihao Deng, a doctoral student and first author, stated that the most energy-intensive languages often have lower accuracy. He warned that this double penalty could price some people out of using AI. Rada Mihalcea, the U-M AI Lab director, urged developers to create more resources for these languages. She suggested using crowdsourced native speakers to improve training data and efficiency.

The research was partially funded by the National Science Foundation and DARPA, with support from OpenAI and Ford. To fix these issues, the team recommends that companies use translation pipelines or models tailored to specific languages. They also suggest routing queries to specialized models to reduce costs. These changes would help prevent global inequalities in AI access.

stories.Headline: Gustavo Espinosa of NTT DATA says agentic AI requires governance of unstructured enterprise data
stories.Summary:
Gustavo Espinosa, Head of Data & AI at NTT DATA International Clients USA, NTT DATA, Inc., published an article on November 10, 2026, titled Unstructured Data Governance: A missing foundation for agentic AI at scale. The article appeared on nttdata.com and was also dated 10 November 2026 in a second version. It says generative AI and now agentic AI are pushing organizations beyond databases and analytical datasets into unstructured enterprise data and content. That content includes documents, presentations, emails, contracts, policies, conversations, images, audio and video. The article says most of this content was never created or managed with AI consumption in mind.

The article says enterprise data governance has focused for years on structured data such as tables, fields, models, lineage, quality rules, access controls and ownership. It says the principles remain but the capabilities must evolve, and that organizations still need ownership, metadata, quality, lineage, security, retention and accountability. It says a customer table has fields, while a contract has clauses, dates, entities and obligations that first need to be extracted and understood. It says an AI pipeline may convert a document into text, divide it into chunks, create embeddings and place those representations into a retrieval index, requiring controls to propagate across every derived representation. It says an audio recording may need transcription and speaker identification before its meaning becomes machine-usable.

The article says traditional cataloging evolves into repository discovery and content inventory, and data profiling expands into OCR, transcription, parsing and multimodal inspection. It says classification expands into topic, entity and sensitivity detection, and lineage extends beyond systems and datasets into documents, chunks, embeddings and AI responses. It says data quality expands beyond completeness and validity into readability, structural integrity, semantic consistency, extraction accuracy and relevance to the intended AI use case. It says the goal is to transform fragmented enterprise content into information assets that are discoverable, understandable, trusted, protected and reusable. It says governance must answer not only whether information can be accessed but whether it should be used, for what purpose, by whom or by what agent, and under what conditions.

The article describes a continuous operating model with visibility, understanding, control and qualification, and activation. It says visibility covers what content exists, where it resides and who owns it, and understanding covers parsing, transcribing, segmenting and enriching content. It says control and qualification apply metadata, classification, quality rules, retention, access controls and AI-use criteria, and activation makes governed content available through search, analytics, RAG, assistants and agents. It says policies need to be executable and continuously enforced rather than documented separately and applied manually after the fact. It says governance becomes embedded in the flow of information itself.

The article says enterprises moving toward AI agents need a persistent enterprise context layer called the Company Brain, which is not simply an enterprise search engine or a collection of documents connected to an LLM. It says outdated documents lead agents to reason over outdated context, and conflicting versions without clear authority may lead agents to select the wrong source. It says permissions not carried into AI retrieval may let an agent expose information the user could never access directly, and missing semantics may let an agent retrieve the right words while misunderstanding their meaning. It says absent provenance leaves organizations unable to explain which information influenced a response or action. It says unstructured data governance is one component of a broader enterprise context governance discipline ensuring knowledge is current, understandable, traceable, protected and accountable.

The article says a chatbot that retrieves an incorrect policy may produce an incorrect answer, while an agent may use that same policy to initiate a workflow, modify a system or recommend an action. It says NTT DATA has been working with assets and accelerators that evaluate unstructured content across semantic quality, visual and structural quality, and compliance and risk, producing a quantitative assessment and a disposition that acts as an AI-readiness gate. It says a policy may say sensitive customer information must be protected, a standard defines that content as restricted, a machine-readable rule applies that classification, a control masks the content and prevents unauthorized retrieval, and evidence records what was detected and enforced. It says organizations that succeed with agentic AI will be those that turn enterprise information into trusted, governed and machine-usable context. It directs readers to read more about NTT DATA's AI services to learn how to operationalize AI throughout their organization.
