stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer of Nvidia on November 14, 2026, according to a report by Nathan Lambert. This sudden departure is described as a decapitation that creates a major setback for the American open model ecosystem. Lambert notes that the timing of the announcement followed a midterm political swing in the United States. The resignation removes a powerful champion who had supported open source AI for about two years. This event leaves the open model movement without its most influential advocate and protector.

Nvidia must now stabilize its operations and deliver to customers over the next 24 months to prevent a total implosion. The company faces challenges including potential chip smuggling investigations and the loss of talent to poaching sharks. The open model economy is currently in its nascency and requires established revenue flows and clear use cases. Some Western models like Inkling 2 Small from Thinking Machines are far behind Kimi K3.1 Pro. Meanwhile, Mira is reportedly seeking a new funding round at a valuation of 40 billion dollars.

Nathan Lambert says that Jensen Huang was more than a cheerleader because he used his power to prevent crises. He argues that the open model economy has correctly focused on enterprise post training and the ownership of intelligence. Lambert believes that the movement is regressing in operational capability just as attacks and stakes are destined to rise. He suggests that open model believers must now engage in soul searching and build a new coalition. The author claims that the shoes Huang emptied will never be fully refilled.

Dylan Patel, the CEO of SemiAnalysis, says that talent is a bigger problem than money for the open model ecosystem. He notes that the most talented people work at OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind, and Meta, leaving others split across startups. Inference startups are struggling to get chips because OpenAI and Anthropic are buying up most of the available capacity. Chris Hughes warns that blunt federal and state regulations could create a costly moat for the largest players. These regulatory changes would only benefit the biggest companies that can afford to navigate the complex rules.

The articles state that Nvidia's business operations are extremely dependent on Jensen Huang as an operator and a founder. Huang had flooded the open model zone with funding, but this financial support is very likely to dry up. The open model ecosystem has faced pressure from the AI safety community and Democratic government funding for regulation. There is a recurring concern that a popular Chinese open weight model could trigger a cybersecurity crisis. The media often drives narratives based on harm and risk rather than the availability of exact information.

The open model movement may now turn to hyperscalers like Satya Nadella, Andy Jassy, or Mark Zuckerberg for support. The industry must determine if a truly frontier open model player can be incubated within the United States. It remains unclear if Thinking Machines or other small labs can overcome their deficits in compute and deployment. The articles leave open whether the open model economy can become a meaningful engine without Huang's protection. Future success depends on whether the ecosystem can survive sloppy state level and national regulations.

stories.Headline: Adobe and Google integrate AI models into creative and productivity tools
stories.Summary:
Adobe and Google expanded their strategic AI partnership on November 14, 2026, to integrate advanced models into creative tools. This collaboration brings Google AI models into Adobe software and extends Adobe tools across the Google productivity ecosystem. Adobe also unveiled new AI agents and features at the Adobe MAX 2026 conference in Miami. This annual creative event opened on October 10 and showcased the evolution of the Firefly generative app. The updates aim to turn Firefly into a comprehensive AI creative studio for all digital creators.

Google Gemini models will power Acrobat, allowing users to edit PDFs via conversational prompts through Google Workspace, Drive, and Gmail. Adobe Firefly, Photoshop, Premiere, and Express will integrate Google image and video models, including Gemini Omni, Veo, and Nano Banana. Firefly now supports 36 models, including ByteDance's Dreamina and Seedance 2.5, Runway's Gen-4.5, Kuaishou's Kling 4.0, and OpenAI's GPT. Adobe also partnered with Disney for custom Firefly Foundry models and Microsoft for Arm-based Windows PCs and Microsoft Photos. New tools include Firefly Design in beta, Firefly Builder in private beta, and the CX Enterprise Coworker in GenStudio.

Forrest Key, vice president for Firefly and agentic AI, stated the company wants to help everyone create digital content. He described Firefly as the best platform for both new creators and professionals to build their digital work. Deepa Subramaniam, vice president of product marketing for Creative Cloud, said updates provide professionals with precision, control, and flexibility. She noted that these new tools allow professionals to focus on the decisions that shape their own creative work. The companies are also exploring custom Google image models for Photoshop to enable near-real-time editing through text prompts.

Users of Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, and Lightroom are affected by these updates, including new lighting and color tools. Premiere mobile users gain natural-language editing and licensed music from UMG and WMG for personal, non-commercial video projects. Designers can use Firefly Design to combine illustration, animation, and 3D tools on a single canvas for efficiency. Marketing teams can now use the Ideation Space in Workfront to build campaign strategies and briefs using AI. Business users can coordinate agents and workflows across planning and activation using the new CX Enterprise Coworker interface.

Adobe's multi-model strategy allows users to work with different AI models alongside professional editing tools in the Creative Cloud. Firefly was developed as a generative AI app offering image and video generation, editing, and now agent-based workflow tools. The company introduced a plan mode for reviewing agent plans and a model picker for selecting specific AI models. Always-on agents are being previewed to handle repetitive background tasks like organizing assets and checking content quality. Adobe also developed Firefly Graph in beta for users who want to build repeatable and efficient creative workflows.

Next, Adobe will expand integrations with Gemini and Gemini Enterprise to bring Acrobat and creative tools into those platforms. The company is rolling out beta features like Generative Remove in Premiere and real-time co-editing in InDesign. Local MCP integrations are being previewed to allow third-party agents to edit native project files while keeping layers editable. Adobe continues to test Firefly Builder for turning spoken descriptions into prototypes for websites and mobile apps without coding. The articles leave open how the custom Google models for Photoshop will perform in real-time text-to-image editing.

stories.Headline: Nvidia board removes CEO Jensen Huang following reports of extramarital affairs
stories.Summary:
The board of Nvidia prepared to remove CEO Jensen Huang around November 11, 2026, following several serious personal allegations. Huang eventually resigned as president, CEO, and board member after reports of affairs with two different women emerged. One woman is suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence, while the other is a senior executive at Nvidia. These events created the most serious leadership crisis in the history of the world's largest AI semiconductor company. The board considered meeting as early as November 11 to determine the future of the company's founder.

The board's decision followed allegations involving Alice Huang of Megaspeed in Singapore and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare. Powell joined the company in 2008 and reported directly to Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 with two engineers. Huang owns about 3.6 percent of the company, which lacks a dual-class share structure for enhanced founder voting rights. The board will now adopt a full chairmanship structure, and Colette Kress will serve as the interim CEO. Kress will also keep her current roles as the company's chief financial officer and executive vice president.

Independent directors hired attorney Joon Kim and his firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, to lead an independent investigation. Huang wrote a letter to employees on November 8 admitting he was unfaithful to his wife and apologizing. He initially expressed his intention to remain in his position before the allegations regarding Kimberly Powell became public knowledge. When the New York Times contacted him about the reports, Huang told the reporter not to reach out directly. Neither Kimberly Powell nor the company issued an official response to the reports regarding the alleged extramarital relationship.

Investors fear a leadership vacuum because Huang personally managed over 60 direct reports and led all major company decisions. The FBI and U.S. intelligence officials are investigating whether Huang shared national security secrets with Alice Huang of Megaspeed. China's Foreign Ministry denied the spy allegations and told the United States to stop fabricating narratives for technology blockades. Market reactions were sharp, with shares dropping 8.1 percent to 159.59 dollars, erasing 340 billion dollars in market value. Analysts like Stacy Rasgon noted that the transition would be difficult because Huang and Nvidia were essentially one.

Huang transformed Nvidia from a gaming chip maker into an AI leader, introducing the GeForce 256 GPU in 1999. In 2006, he developed CUDA, and he later secured early support from Sega and cooperation with TSMC founder Morris Chang. He built strong ties with Samsung Chairman Lee Jae-yong, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, and firms like Microsoft and Google. Huang also persuaded President Donald Trump to ease export restrictions and committed 90 billion dollars to various partnership deals. Despite these successes, the New York Times reported that Huang had rejected internal succession planning for several years.

The board is now searching for a permanent successor to replace the founder who led the company for 33 years. Potential candidates mentioned by media include Apple's Johny Srouji, Arm CEO Rene Haas, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and Lori Huang. Other unlikely candidates include AMD CEO Lisa Su and Intel's Lip-Bu Tan, while the U.S. Congress tightens export controls. The investigation will now examine internal controls and compliance with the company's code of conduct regarding the reported affairs. It remains open whether the leadership change will ripple across the broader AI ecosystem and affect global capital flows.

stories.Headline: Chinese AI firms use restricted Nvidia Blackwell chips despite US sanctions
stories.Summary:
A Radio Free Asia investigation revealed that sanctioned Chinese entities obtained restricted Nvidia AI chips despite strict United States export controls. This discovery occurred as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation on Thursday following a scandal involving an alleged extramarital affair. The U.S. government is investigating Huang's ties to Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former Megaspeed executive. She is suspected of collecting intelligence for Beijing and helping Chinese clients acquire restricted chips through her connections. This situation has been described as an AI industry earthquake that has attracted intense attention from outside observers.

The National Supercomputing Center Jinan, also called Shandong Computing Center, won a bid for RTX 5090 and DGX Spark products. On June 17, 2026, the China Government Procurement Network announced Qiyuan Jiasu (Tianjin) Technology Co., Ltd. won the bid. The winning bid price was RMB 148,500, which is approximately 22,000 US dollars, for one batch of AI equipment. The RTX 5090 uses Blackwell architecture with 32GB GDDR7 memory, while the DGX Spark uses the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip. These products were solicited by the Jinan center as of June 2026 despite its status on the entity list.

The U.S. Department of Commerce is responsible for the entity list and stated that Jinan supported Chinese military modernization. Chris Tseng of the Research Institute for Democracy, Society and Emerging Technology said controls rely heavily on corporate self-compliance. He noted that licenses are required to transfer regulated items to controlled entities even through legitimate third-country distributors. Sylvia Chen of DSET stated that third-party enterprises bear legal liability if they illegally transfer controlled products within China. She explained that the Bureau of Industry and Security has only fifteen export control officers worldwide to verify end-users.

DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group are affected because their models show evidence of using restricted Blackwell GPUs. Unemployment Labs, led by Will Depue, found that these firms used B200, B300, GB200, and GB300 chips for training. The report analyzed six systems released since April, including DeepSeek V4-Flash, V4-Pro, Kimi K3, K3.1-Pro, MiniMax M3, and Ling-3.1-Flash. These companies may have skirted controls by renting compute in Southeast Asia or using smuggled chips via workaround routes. The report estimates that 12,000 Blackwell GPUs were deployed, with costs reaching roughly 500 million US dollars.

The Shandong Computing Center was established in 1976 and is affiliated with the Qilu University of Technology in China. The U.S. Department of Commerce placed the center on the entity list in April 2021 for national security reasons. Broad export restrictions on advanced computing chips to China began in 2022, following the initial listing of the center. Sitonholy (Tianjin) Technology was an Nvidia Elite Partner until it was sanctioned by the U.S. on April 11, 2024. The Trump administration allowed limited exports of H200 chips but did not approve exports of Blackwell or Rubin chips.

Nvidia must now investigate the sales and ultimate flow of products if Qiyuan Jiasu inherited Sitonholy's original business operations. The U.S. government continues to investigate the role of Alice Huang in smuggling advanced AI chips into China. It remains open whether the RTX 5090 cards purchased were the original version or the China special edition. Researchers cautioned that they did not verify the physical location of the chips or prove specific export law violations. The articles leave open whether Qiyuan Jiasu is simply a shell company used to bypass the Entity List.

stories.Headline: Singapore probes Super Micro over potential false declarations regarding server purchases
stories.Summary:
The Ministry of Home Affairs identified Super Micro Computer as part of a larger probe into potential false declarations regarding server purchases. This investigation began in February 2025 and involves the US-based server supplier, which has known links to the chipmaker Nvidia. Singapore authorities stated on November 12 that the firm has provided limited cooperation during the ongoing inquiry. The government also noted that the US Department of Justice and the Federal Bureau of Investigation provided limited assistance despite repeated requests since September 2025.

The probe involves Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed and alleged Chinese spy, who was barred from re-entering Singapore in February. US authorities are investigating whether entities linked to Huang attempted to smuggle Super Micro products into China. Separately, co-founder Yih-Shyan Wally Liaw and two other men were charged in the US for conspiring to divert 2.5 billion US dollars of AI technology to China starting around October 2023. Additionally, two Super Micro employees were among nine people indicted in Taiwan for illegally exporting 130 B300 servers to Chinese customers.

Super Micro stated on November 13 that it has been responsive to inquiries and fully cooperated with officials in the US, Taiwan, and Singapore. The company denied that Megaspeed was ever a customer and claimed to maintain a robust compliance programme to protect American innovation. Regarding the US charges, Wally Liaw pleaded not guilty, while former contractor Ting-Wei Willy Sun pleaded guilty to four counts including smuggling and defrauding the country. The firm continues to operate a small office in Singapore located at Metropolis Tower 1 in Buona Vista.

stories.Headline: Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution showcase AI data center battery systems at RE+ 2026
stories.Summary:
Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution will compete at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas starting November 17. These two companies will showcase energy storage systems and backup power solutions for artificial intelligence data centers. They disclosed their participation plans on November 15 for the three day renewable energy trade show. The event draws about 40,000 visitors and 1,300 companies to the largest renewable energy show in North America. Both firms are targeting North American orders by emphasizing their local production capacity for these battery systems.

LG Energy Solution will use a 279 square meter booth to show the JF3 AC LINK with US-made LFP batteries. This product increases energy density by 26 percent and uses AI and digital twin technologies for grid stabilization. Samsung SDI will exhibit the SBB 2.0 using locally produced LFP prismatic cells in a 20-foot container. Samsung will also show the U8A3 prismatic battery using lithium manganese oxide for uninterruptible power supply applications. LG will display the JP6 Rack for UPS and BBU products based on cylindrical 2170 batteries.

Kang Chang-beom of LG Energy Solution said stable power storage and efficient operations are essential for AI industry growth. He stated the company will become an energy platform by combining battery technology with intelligent operations and North American production. Samsung SDI claims the U8A3 is the first to pass all UL Solutions large-scale indoor fire test criteria. An industry official noted that companies now focus on profitability rather than the cutthroat competition seen in the past. This shift follows a trend where the three major battery firms moved toward making profits this year.

The competition affects Big Tech clients like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google who need cooling and power for AI chips. LG Energy Solution is sitting out a 1,180MW South Korean auction, leaving Samsung SDI and SK On to compete. This auction totals about 7.08GWh in storage capacity, which is larger than the first two rounds combined. Samsung SDI has about 15GWh of production capacity in South Korea with roughly 5GWh of remaining supply. SK On has about 3GWh of LFP capacity converted from an EV line in Seosan for deliveries.

Samsung Electronics previously spent 1.5 billion euros to acquire Germany's Flakt Group for data center climate control technologies. The company is now pursuing US cooling maker Modine to gain North American production facilities and customer networks. Modine recently began mass producing 2 to 3 megawatt chillers at a 63,400 square meter plant in Grand Prairie, Texas. Modine's data center revenue reached 439.7 million dollars in the third quarter, which is up 95 percent from last year. Samsung is also building a 240 billion won production line in Gwangju to start operating in early 2028.

Samsung may acquire Modine for 7.5 billion to 8 billion dollars through a merger agreement or a tender offer. The deal requires approval from two-thirds of voting rights, meaning about 35.41 million votes in favor are needed. LG Electronics is also competing by building a chiller plant in Virginia to begin operating in the first half of 2027. Other competitors like Daikin and Vertiv are expanding through acquisitions to win large projects from North American Big Tech firms. The articles leave open whether Samsung shareholders or Modine's board will ultimately agree to the proposed acquisition.

stories.Headline: Samsung breaks ground on HBM packaging plant in Asan and moves opening to June 2028
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics broke ground on a high-bandwidth memory packaging plant on November 12, 2026, to expand the artificial intelligence server supply chain. This new facility is located at the Onyang campus in Asan, South Korea, and focuses on advanced packaging for HBM memory. The company is accelerating the project to meet the rising demand for server memory used in various modern artificial intelligence systems. Construction of the plant is the first project under a regional industrial mega-project program led by the South Korean government. The facility is now scheduled to begin its operations in June 2028, which is one year earlier than previously planned.

The project requires 6 trillion won, or 4.48 billion dollars, for construction and 40 trillion won for advanced equipment installed in stages. Total medium and long term investment for the Onyang expansion is roughly 46 trillion won, including three clean-room floors of 31,000 square meters. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is investing 8 trillion won in package-substrate production for central processing units and graphics processors in the Chungcheong region. Samsung Display is investing 67 trillion won in an 8.6-generation production line for information technology displays within the same South Korean region. Samsung Electro-Mechanics will also spend 4.27 trillion won in South Korea and 2.51 trillion won in Vietnam for flip-chip ball grid array substrates.

The South Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced the groundbreaking and said it would coordinate permits for the new projects. The ministry also stated it would help the company secure necessary transport infrastructure along with essential water and electricity for the site. Samsung said during its third-quarter earnings announcement that it had already completed negotiations over HBM supply volumes for the year 2027. The company noted that customers continued to seek additional supply, which prompted the decision to move the plant opening date forward. Samsung Electro-Mechanics disclosed in September that its substrate expansion for high-performance computing applications will start mass production in September 2028.

Customers seeking more high-bandwidth memory are affected by packaging capacity, which is a separate manufacturing step from producing the memory wafers. Advanced packaging connects stacked memory dies with processors and other components, making it a critical constraint on the finished HBM supply. The expansion at the Onyang campus was prompted because the existing Samsung campus in Cheonan has run short of available space. This makes Onyang a major production base for advanced AI memory to support the needs of various global technology customers. The project is part of a broader investment program across the Chungcheong region to bolster the regional industrial economy.

The South Korean government identified 112 materials, components and equipment suppliers with additional investment plans totaling about 23.6 trillion won around the projects. HBM combines stacked memory dies with high-speed connections for AI accelerators, which are essential for the operation of AI servers. The government is supporting these industrial projects by managing the infrastructure and permits required for the massive scale of the investments. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is focusing its substrate investments on AI servers and other high-performance computing applications to meet the growing market demand. These efforts are part of a strategic move to secure the supply chain for artificial intelligence hardware in Asia.

The investment for the Onyang plant will be deployed over several years, with equipment spending following the initial construction in phases. Samsung has not disclosed the planned output capacity of the new plant or the specific customer commitments for the facility. The company has also kept the expected financial returns from the 46 trillion won investment private at this current stage. It remains open whether the increased capacity will fully satisfy the rising demand for AI server memory by June 2028. The articles do not state the specific names of the customers who are seeking additional high-bandwidth memory supply.

stories.Headline: Malaysia investigates Megaspeed subsidiary over alleged diversion of Nvidia AI chips
stories.Summary:
Malaysian police opened an investigation in April 2025 regarding United States allegations that high-performance artificial intelligence chips were illicitly procured and diverted through the country. The probe focuses on whether Malaysia served as a transit hub for Nvidia chips or if local proxy companies were involved in the scheme. Authorities are specifically investigating Speedmatrix, a subsidiary of the Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, which operates as a tenant at Malaysian data centers. This investigation follows reports that Megaspeed may have steered advanced technology to China in violation of United States export rules.

The investigation is being conducted under the Strategic Trade Act 2010 and involves several regulatory agencies. These include Bank Negara Malaysia, the Inland Revenue Board, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, Customs, and the police. While Speedmatrix can bring chips into Malaysia without a permit, any entity exporting, re-exporting, transshipping, or transiting high-performance US AI chips has required a permit since July 2025. The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry, known as MITI, is the lead agency coordinating with a task force called STAC.

Home Minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail stated that the government is taking these allegations seriously and that the investigation is very complex. He noted that progress is regularly conveyed to MITI so the information can be shared with relevant parties. MITI added that providing false information to customs authorities is a serious offense and confirmed that Speedmatrix has never been cleared of any wrongdoing. The ministry is working closely with authorities in Singapore and the United States to determine if chips were re-exported illegally.

This situation coincides with the immediate resignation of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer, and board member on November 12, 2026. His departure followed a scandal involving Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese spy who was barred from entering Singapore in February. The controversy has reportedly wiped nearly half a trillion dollars off the market capitalization of Nvidia. Malaysia is now considering stronger controls to curb chip smuggling as the artificial intelligence sector faces significant uncertainty.

stories.Headline: Psychologist Eichenberg says AI chatbots bridge therapy waiting times but cannot replace professional care
stories.Summary:
People who struggle to find a therapist or need help faster than a counselling appointment can be set up are turning to general chatbots such as Gemini, Claude or ChatGPT, which seem like understanding listeners, according to an article published by The Star on Sunday, 15 Nov 2026. The article says many of us, especially the young, are using these chatbots as conversation partners for advice and to discuss problems, and it asks why not mental health conditions too. It adds that this comes with limitations and risks, and that psychologists it checked with were clear that AI is no substitute for psychological help from a person. In Germany, anyone looking for a place on a therapy programme has to wait an average of 20 weeks, says Christiane Eichenberg, head of the Institute for Psychosomatics at Sigmund Freud Private University in Vienna. Eichenberg, a psychologist and author of a book about Artificial Intelligence and Psychotherapy, says the gap in care is by no means the sole reason for the popularity of chatbots, which are available round the clock and are non-judgemental.

She says we can communicate with them without having to fear judgement or stigma, and that talking to a computer or phone makes it easier for many people to open up. She says you feel less pressure to put on a brave face and can express feelings such as sadness more intensely. The article says some people turn to general chatbots to discuss their everyday stress, feelings or anxieties, while other AI-based chatbots and applications have been developed specifically with a focus on mental health and are designed to help users reflect on their emotions, overcome fears or manage stress. Eichenberg says some AI-based mental health programmes have been scientifically evaluated and operate based on a clinically validated treatment protocol, and that the effects are comparable to those of psychotherapy when the systems have been used for four to eight weeks according to the research available so far. However, the article says it remains unclear how stable and long-lasting these effects are.

Kevin Hilbert, Professor of Clinical Psychology and Psychotherapy at the Health and Medical University of Erfurt, says an attentive, caring and always-available listener is appealing at first for most of us. The article says initial studies suggest that the use of artificial intelligence for mild psychological distress may be more effective than doing nothing at all, and that the systems may help in such cases by empowering users, helping them organise their thoughts and supporting them in their self-reflection. Hilbert says initial studies have also shown quite good results when it comes to anxiety, high stress or early symptoms of depression, but the article says there is overall not yet enough research to draw definitive conclusions. Eichenberg says specialist therapeutic chatbots may be particularly useful for bridging waiting times or to complement traditional therapy, and that they can support self-management, serve as a training ground for role-play for example, or provide valuable real-time support in acute stressful situations. She underlines that the bots are no substitute for psychotherapy.

stories.Headline: Meta expands AI age estimation on Instagram to apply teen account protections
stories.Summary:
Meta Platforms announced in a statement dated November 9 that it is expanding its AI-powered age-estimation technology to find Instagram users it suspects are teenagers, even when they signed up with an adult birthdate. Accounts flagged this way are automatically moved into Teen Account protections, which Meta says will reach millions more teenagers across the world. The Epoch Times reported the move on November 10, 2026, and Biometric Update covered it the same day. Meta describes the protections as built-in safeguards that limit the content teens see, the time they spend on the app, and who can contact them. The company says some teens misrepresent their age online to reach experiences they are not old enough to use.

Starting this month, parents in the United States on Instagram will receive a notification explaining how Meta applies the age-appropriate protections and how they can help make sure their teen is logged in with the correct age. Teens aged 13 to 15 need parental permission to make some account protections less restrictive. Those aged 16 and 17 have more freedom to change certain settings, but still face restrictions, such as content limits, that cannot be altered without a parent's approval. Meta says it is continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook, and later this year it will begin launching similar measures globally on Threads. The company has also started using Apple's age-range signal in Australia as an additional way to help determine users' ages.

Meta is the company behind the expansion, and it says it uses AI and other signals to estimate a user's age. Larry Magid, CEO of the nonprofit ConnectSafely, explained the method in a November 6 post on Meta's website. He said the signals include profile information, comments, posts, captions and bios, such as references to school grades or birthdays, and that Meta can also analyze visual patterns in photos and videos. Magid stressed that this visual analysis is not facial recognition, because it looks for general characteristics suggesting an underage person in order to estimate an age range, not to identify anyone. He added that Meta deactivates suspected under-13 accounts and requires proof of age to prevent their deletion.

Meta also said it has long supported legislation requiring age verification and parental consent at the app store level. It argues that one verified signal from a person's device, shared consistently with all apps, is far more effective and privacy-preserving than asking every platform to verify age separately. Meta says it uses Apple's signal voluntarily, but that teens will get inconsistent protections across apps while sharing and using the signal stays optional for app stores and developers. It describes its own AI system as a backstop that can correct mistakes and feed them back to the app store for correction across all the apps a teen uses. Meta also says it has set a strong standard for age assurance and is investing in stronger technology to catch accounts that may belong to children under 13.

Biometric Update's Joel R. McConvey criticized the approach, writing that Meta responds to calls for platform accountability by hitting the problem sideways, in a game of misdirectional tennis. He argued that the age inference system is a form of profiling whose methods, accuracy and privacy implications are not subject to the public scrutiny applied to independently evaluated third-party tools. He also said it removes user choice, applying a model that recalls U2 pushing its album onto everyone's iPod. He noted that effective age assurance tools exist and that Meta already works with vendors, notably Yoti for facial age estimation on Instagram, and he said data from Australia shows how unserious the company has been about following laws it dislikes. Teens are the people directly affected, and the Electronic Privacy Information Center, through Megan Iorio, voiced support for California's AB 1709, saying design features that manipulate kids are the problem.

The expansion follows a roughly $18.1 billion settlement Meta reached in August with multiple U.S. jurisdictions over allegations of endangering children. Those lawsuits accused the company of deliberately designing its platforms to be addictive, knowingly exposing children to mental harms, and misleading people about the safety of its products. Meta agreed to pay $17.1 billion to settle suits from 47 states, territories and the District of Columbia, and $1 billion to settle a Texas suit. As part of the deal, Meta agreed to institute age-verification protocols, content controls and time limits for children. Biometric Update reports that the agreement involves 52 bipartisan attorneys general and makes about 30 percent of the payments conditional on TikTok and YouTube adopting comparable measures and making matching payments.

Meta, Google and TikTok filed separate lawsuits on November 4 seeking to stop California from enforcing Assembly Bill 1709, a new state law meant to protect children under 16 from the effects of social media. The law bars platforms from offering underage children features judged psychologically exploitative that could cause compulsive use, including autoplay videos and personal recommendations. Platforms are obligated to delete the accounts of children with such features. The companies allege that the measure violates First Amendment free speech protections. The Epoch Times also notes that Meta recently settled with a teen during a trial over social media addiction claims, which the articles cite without giving details.

In the weeks ahead, U.S. parents on Instagram will begin receiving the notifications, while the technology keeps rolling out on Facebook and reaches Threads later this year. The articles do not say how accurate Meta's age estimation is, how many teens it has identified, or whether the system will face independent evaluation. They also leave open whether Apple's age-range signal will spread beyond Australia, and whether app stores or developers will be required to share and use it. The outcome of the lawsuits from Meta, Google and TikTok against California's AB 1709 is likewise undecided. Biometric Update adds that the company's statements about online safety rest on credibility it may not have.

stories.Headline: FuelCell Energy joins federal StabilityMax program to test fuel cells for AI data centers
stories.Summary:
FuelCell Energy, a fuel cell company headquartered on Great Pasture Road in Danbury near the Bethel border, will take part in a three-year federally funded program to test whether fuel cells can provide electricity to data centers where there are rapid fluctuations in power consumption. The company announced the project in a release dated Nov 13, 2026, reported by staff writer Rob Ryser. The program is known as StabilityMax. Under the project, FuelCell Energy will develop a fuel cell test facility in Danbury, creating a national laboratory-supported testbed for evaluating integrated power solutions for AI data centers. The federal government wants to know whether fuel cells, which already power commercial and industrial facilities, can handle the heavy demands of artificial intelligence data centers.

The project runs three years and is led by the U.S. Department of Energy's National Laboratories of the Rockies. FuelCell Energy reported 425 employees worldwide last year, most of them at the company's Danbury headquarters and its Torrington manufacturing plant. FuelCell planned to keep its staffing levels the same. Details about the StabilityMax grant program, such as how much federal money is involved, were not disclosed. The pairing of fuel cells with data centers made news in October when a developer proposed to reinvigorate a 1.3-million-square-foot office structure in Danbury by bringing in a data center and using fuel cells to power it.

Mayor Roberto Alves said Thursday that FuelCell Energy's participation in the national research effort is a strong example of the innovation and expertise rooted in Danbury. Alves said he was pleased to see a Danbury company working with leading national labs on the challenge and looked forward to learning what the project demonstrates about performance, cost and the effects on the electric grid. Kathleen Blomquist, the company's director of communications, said the project isn't about testing whether fuel cells can power data centers because they can. Blomquist said the question is how to optimize a fuel cell-based power system for the rapidly changing demands of AI infrastructure, including how fuel cells, batteries, power electronics and advanced controls work together as computing loads fluctuate. Zhiwen Ma, a principal investigator at the National Laboratories of the Rockies, said fuel cells combined with data centers provide unique solutions to meet the power demands of AI infrastructure.

Ma said that through the project, NLR will help demonstrate how integrated fuel cell systems can rapidly respond to data center power needs while limiting impacts to the utility grid and ratepayers. Shankar Achanta, chief product and technology officer at FuelCell, said the insights gained through the work will help optimize system designs, validate performance under real-world conditions, and support future deployment of fuel cell-based solutions for digital infrastructure. The company's release said that as AI adoption accelerates, data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and creating rapid fluctuations in power consumption. A data center is an umbrella term for computer processing plants that support all the ways artificial intelligence is used today. Public concern about energy usage by data centers has made headlines across Connecticut and the region.

A fuel cell makes electricity from fuel and air, eliminating the need to burn fuel. The company's headquarters sits on the city's east end. stories.Headline: Majority of Indians prefer instant AI health answers over waiting for doctors in BCG survey
stories.Summary:
A Boston Consulting Group global survey found that 61 percent of Indians prefer instant AI health answers over waiting for doctors. This study was conducted during July and August 2026 and included 9,914 consumers across 10 different countries. The findings were published on November 15, 2026, by Sumit Jha in a report about the consumerisation of health care. This shift shows that more people in India are using digital technology to seek medical information instead of professionals. The report indicates that patients are increasingly seeking greater control over their treatment decisions, convenience, and their healthcare expenditure.

India scored 66 out of 100 on the Healthcare Consumerization Index, ranking second behind China, which scored 72. The United Arab Emirates ranked third at 63, while Brazil followed in fourth place with a score of 62. In India, 60 percent trust digital health information as much as professional advice, which is 19 percentage points above average. Additionally, 78 percent of Indian respondents want more control over treatment choices, and 73 percent want control over costs. Around 68 percent expect retail level convenience, and 58 percent view medicines as common consumer goods.

Chris Meier of BCG stated that consumer patients are reshaping rules to expect more intuitive, responsive, and personalized health care experiences. He is a managing director and senior partner who co authored the report on the consumerisation of the health industry. Sabrina Kristic, also a managing director and senior partner, noted that health care decisions are more complex than cosmetics. She warned that these decisions have potentially serious consequences, even if products blur the line between health and lifestyle categories. Both authors believe that providers must now balance patient choice and convenience with clinical quality and patient outcomes.

Millennials were most likely to prefer instant AI answers at 52 percent, followed by Generation Z at 47 percent. Baby boomers showed the lowest preference for these digital tools, with only 25 percent choosing AI over a doctor. Doctors from Harvard and Johns Hopkins warn that AI mass surveillance can cause chronic anticipatory stress and physical sickness. Vulnerable groups, including undocumented immigrants, may avoid clinics or pharmacies due to a fear of persecution from surveillance tools. These experts argue that AI surveillance is a structural determinant of health that can create avoidable health inequities.

The BCG report explains that digital platforms can improve information access but may also expose users to fragmented services and misinformation. People with limited digital literacy or confidence may be excluded from these new digital first models of health care. Meanwhile, the New England Journal of Medicine highlights how private companies now control the data ecosystems used for surveillance. Traditional surveillance required human oversight, but AI can continuously comb through social media, financial transactions, and geolocation records. This allows private actors to analyze vast amounts of personal data and share it with government agencies.

Next, healthcare providers must find ways to balance transparency and convenience with equity and the overall quality of patient outcomes. Clinicians can help by documenting patient fears about data usage to provide evidence for policymakers and various legal litigators. Some states, including Washington, Nevada, and Connecticut, have passed laws to extend privacy protections to certain consumer health data. More than 20 state attorneys general have sued the federal government for sharing Medicaid data with Palantir and ICE. The articles leave open whether AI will serve population health or become a driver of structural harm.

stories.Headline: Google DeepMind and University of Chicago researchers test AI agents to scale public policy consultation
stories.Summary:
On November 11, 2026, researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Chicago published a preprint on arXiv about pluralistic AI agents. This study evaluated how autonomous software representatives could represent citizens during deliberations regarding artificial intelligence governance to scale public consultation. The team tested these agents to see if they could capture diverse public input while identifying various operational risks. This research aimed to address low civic engagement and technical barriers that often hinder traditional public consultation on AI regulation. The final results were published by the CASRAI Editorial Board on November 15, 2026, as a four minute read.

The system requires three stages starting with an agent interviewing a person or persona to capture qualitative values and core priorities. Next, agents participate in structured multi-agent discussions using anonymized aliases, and finally, a policy-writing agent synthesizes the consensus into rules. The team, including Jacy Reese Anthis, Ken Burke, David Madras, Crystal Qian, Meredith Ringel Morris, Logan Cross, Caroline Pantofaru, and Utsav Prabhu, tested this. They used models like Claude-Opus-5, GPT-5.6-Sol, GLM-5.2, Kimi-K3, Mistral-Large, and Gemini-3.6-Flash across 5,947 deliberations using conjoint analysis. The study also involved 746 verified human participants recruited through Prolific across six different AI safety topics.

The investigators stated that pluralistic agents should function as amplifiers of public engagement rather than autonomous replacements for democratic institutions. They noted that prompt phrasing functions as de facto procedural rulemaking because verbosity and cooperativeness dictate the final policy outcomes. The authors emphasized that institutional researchers must implement safeguards against prompt manipulation and establish clear audit trails for agent interviews. They also argued that human stakeholders must retain ultimate ratification authority over any policies created through algorithmic consensus. The researchers highlighted that without transparent moderation algorithms, consultations risk skewing outcomes toward the most assertive delegates.

Human participants reported concerns regarding personal agency, noting that delegating deliberation prevented them from engaging in direct social learning. These participants felt that using proxies stopped them from updating their own viewpoints during the debate process. The study affected research administrators, ethics boards, and policy researchers by providing empirical benchmarks on how autonomous proxies deliberate. While participants preferred direct personal participation, pluralistic agents recovered 82 percent of the procedural justice gap against a baseline. When choosing between pluralistic agent proxies and direct deliberation with other humans, the participants split evenly at 50-50.

Traditional consultation mechanisms struggle to keep pace with rapid deployment cycles as universities and funding agencies navigate frontier AI safety. Public consultation often fails because institutions cannot disclose confidential technical details to broad audiences and citizens lack specialized engineering jargon. The researchers found that in 1,000 deliberations with 368 personas, agents matched desired priorities in 90 percent of cases. Direct human participation achieved an average attitude shift of 15.4 percentage points, while pluralistic agents produced a 13.9 point shift. This background shows that agents can solicit granular input on technical choices like computational safety thresholds and laboratory boundaries.

Next, university Research Ethics Boards must recognize the ethical nuances of algorithmic proxy representation when reviewing participatory research protocols. Institutions may adopt these multi-agent tools to improve democratic throughput while maintaining human oversight of the final policy decisions. The articles leave open how to standardize prompt calibration to prevent assertive agents from dominating the deliberative process. There is no mentioned solution for the loss of social learning that humans experience when using AI proxies. The text does not specify which specific AI safety topics were used for the 746 human participants.

stories.Headline: LTM adds its AI-QEM error mitigation tool to IBM Quantum Functions Catalog
stories.Summary:
LTM announced on 12 November 2026 that its AI-powered Quantum Error Mitigation capability, known as AI-QEM, had been added to IBM's Quantum Functions Catalog, and the company said it was the first global systems integrator to publish a function in that catalog. The catalog offers partner-built quantum software services that are meant to simplify quantum workflows and make experiments more efficient for researchers and enterprises. AI-QEM is offered as a circuit function, so users with eligible IBM Quantum access plans can apply it directly inside their Qiskit workflows. LTM said it had tested the capability on IBM Quantum computers across circuits of different sizes and complexities, including experiments involving more than 100 qubits.

The capability uses AI models to learn device-specific error patterns and estimate corrections through classical post-processing, according to the company. LTM said this improves result accuracy without additional quantum processing unit time, repeated circuit executions or extra qubits, which some conventional error mitigation techniques require, and that it reduces the cost and complexity of running useful quantum experiments. IBM's listing says AI-QEM uses circuit, backend and observable characteristics to learn correction factors and applies classical inference to mitigate noisy quantum expectation values. LTM did not disclose the accuracy improvements achieved or provide comparisons with other error mitigation methods. Other providers in IBM's catalog offer related tools, including Q-CTRL's AI-driven error suppression, Qedma's QESEM error mitigation function and Algorithmiq's tensor-network-based approach.

Scott Crowder, Vice President of IBM Quantum Adoption and Business Development, said in a statement that the AI-QEM function would allow IBM's users to mitigate errors faster and with fewer resources in their efforts to develop algorithms and applications. LTM said it continues to advance practical quantum applications across industries, including quantum optimisation solutions for a global insurer, hybrid quantum machine learning for critical infrastructure, and quantum-safe security programs for financial services and insurance organisations. The articles also note that LTIMindtree had earlier joined the IBM Quantum Network as its first Indian global systems integrator. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the availability of the function in the catalog.

stories.Headline: Google releases Gemini Decision 1 and takes first place in 7 of 9 tests
stories.Summary:
On 12 November 2026 Google released Gemini Decision 1, its first decision-making model, alongside the Gemini Decisions API, and it took first place in 7 out of 9 tests with a maximum accuracy of 92.2%. Google CEO Sundar Pichai posted on X to introduce the model's core capabilities. The model does not generate text token by token but scores pre-set candidate answers through a single forward propagation pass. Google's internal teams have already started using the technology. The release was reported by 36Kr and by Google's own blog.

The model scores up to 1000 questions in text, image, audio, video and PDF formats in a single processing pass, with an end-to-end latency of 150 to 250 milliseconds. It supports yes/no judgment, multiple choice with 2 to 255 options, and ordered rubric scoring, and the three task types can be mixed in one request. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens with zero cost for output tokens, about one-fifth of Flash-Lite, and nearly 5 times lower than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite via the Interactions API. It supports a maximum multimodal input context of 256K tokens, and each decision returns a confidence level from 0 to 1. In contexts no larger than 16K tokens the median calculation latency stays between 50 and 100 milliseconds, and latency stays basically stable as questions per request rise from 1 to 100.

Pichai said the Gemini Decisions API is launching in Google AI Studio, powered by the new Gemini Decision 1 model. He said the model is designed for decision-making tasks within a closed set of options and can score up to 1000 questions in text, image, audio, video and PDF formats in a single pass. He said it supports yes/no judgment, multiple choice with up to 255 options, and scoring based on grading rubrics. He said the price is only $0.10 per million input tokens with zero cost for output tokens, about one-fifth of Flash-Lite. He said it leads in multiple benchmark evaluations while having the lowest calibration error.

In JevBench, Gemini Decision 1 scored 92.2%, against 90.9% for OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna, 90.0% for TypeSafe Jev 1.14 and 86.6% for Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite. On Amazon ESCI it got a Macro-F1 of 58.7%, 4 percentage points above GPT-6 Luna and 11.5 above Flash-Lite, and on the New Yorker Caption test it scored 79.7% against 68.4% for GPT-6 Luna. It scored 79.8% on PubMedQA against 74.4% for GPT-6 Luna, and 86.0% on Global-MMLU-Lite against 79.6%. TypeSafe Jev 1.14 led the Mind2Web Multimodal test with 86.8% against 86.2%, and the When2Call test with 82.0% against 79.9%. Gemini Decision 1 scored 71.8% on the MMAU audio test and 69.1% on the Video-MME test, both above Flash-Lite, and its Top-1 ECE calibration error was 0.0250 against 0.0721 for GPT-6 Luna, 0.0494 for TypeSafe Jev 1.14 and 0.2104 for Flash-Lite.

Google said Gemini Notebook uses the Decisions API as a real-time model router to pick model tier and reasoning intensity by request complexity, cutting daily query latency by up to 40%. In Google Stitch, the Rapid Canvas experimental feature uses the API to generate interactive product flow wireframes in seconds and respond to voice or click modifications. In Google Labs' CC product the API picks from more than 200 emoji options, and inside Google Search it builds a safety detection layer for MCP tools to identify adversarial behavior and content. Developers previously had to call a generative model and extract results from generated text for tasks such as spam detection or agent assignment. The model targets AI model routing, agent tool selection, product design and safety detection.

Google published a comparison scorecard against GPT-6 Luna, TypeSafe Jev 1.14 and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite rather than comparing general large models together. Google said the model delivers leading performance and the lowest calibration error in benchmarks covering agent routing, reasoning, ranking and multimodal understanding. Google provided an example of uploading a photo of an office pantry countertop with a text description and asking in one request whether liquid has spilled, what cleaning measures to take and the severity level. Google said developers can analyze call recordings with customer profiles, or combine insurance claim documents with on-site photos. The articles leave open the two benchmarks and the total invocation cost where competitors performed better.

The articles do not say what Google plans after the launch, and they leave open how the model performs outside the published benchmarks. They do not give the full list of the 9 benchmark tests beyond those named. They do not state when the Gemini Decisions API becomes generally available beyond its launch in Google AI Studio. They do not give results for the remaining benchmarks beyond the scores reported. They do not say how the internal products will change after the launch.

stories.Headline: LG CNS hosts robotics forum to advance physical AI deployment in industrial settings
stories.Summary:
The global robotics industry is racing to turn artificial intelligence into physical machines that can perceive, reason, and act in the real world. Experts say these advances are transforming manufacturing and other sectors, while LG CNS hosted a forum in Seoul on November 12, 2026. More than 100 researchers and industry professionals met at the Future Robotics Lab in Magok to discuss deploying physical AI in industrial settings. This movement includes a surge in humanoid robot shipments, with over 22,000 units delivered globally during the first half of 2026. These shipments represent a 300 per cent year-on-year increase, and totals are expected to exceed 50,000 units by the end of the year.

Dubai targets deploying 200,000 robots by 2032 through its Robotics and Automation Program, while GITEX World RobotiX occurs December 8 to 11, 2026. This event at the Dubai Exhibition Centre in Expo City Dubai features Unitree, which holds a 31 per cent share of the global market. Other participants include UBTECH, AiMOGA, DEEP Robotics, Micropolis Robotics, Mangobot, Lumos Robotics, Lootah Robotics, Light Origins, and Raydiculous, which debuts its TP01 and DINOBOT. LG CNS introduced its PhysicalWorks Forge learning platform and PhysicalWorks Baton agentic AI platform, while Lumos Robotics showcased the NIX S3 with 21 degrees. The forum in Seoul included faculty and students from the University of Toronto, Sogang University, Chung-Ang University, and Korea University.

Mazen El-Kurdi of Mangobot said visitors should see what working alongside robots feels like, rather than just looking at the machines themselves. Cecile Wei of Lumos Robotics stated that robots must perform useful tasks reliably in real environments instead of just moving for demonstrations. Hazem Ghazal of Lootah Robotics said they are building an integrated robotics ecosystem so organizations can select different robots for different requirements. Tingxiang Fan of Light Origins believes the bunny-shaped robot is ready to enter consumers' homes for hands-on interaction in household scenarios. Lee Jun-ho of LG CNS said engagement with academia will help turn research results into innovation within actual industrial settings.

Professor Lee Chi-geun discussed combining data from different robots and using flow matching and action chunking to help machines produce smoother, continuous movements. His presentation identified that differences in robot movement, latency, and data availability remain significant challenges for deploying robot foundation models in the world. The technology affects consumer services, education, entertainment, and domestic environments, as well as factories, warehouses, and other industrial settings like car factories. Airbus is testing UBTECH robots, while Dubai Police use autonomous patrol robots from Micropolis Robotics and Mitsubishi Electric uses Lumos MOS robots. Participants also discussed how human roles may evolve as robotics advances and what capabilities companies and universities need to develop.

LG CNS draws on more than two decades of experience and has completed over 1,000 smart factory and smart logistics projects in the past. Lumos Robotics reported that its first-generation MOS robots completed over 1,000 hours of failure-free operation performing material handling, quality inspection, and screwdriving tasks. Raydiculous developed the TP01 humanoid for commercial interaction and public services, which can communicate in both English and Arabic and perform movements. The DINOBOT is described as the world's first intelligent bipedal walking bionic dinosaur and will demonstrate realistic movement and interactive capabilities. Embodied AI integrates AI models into physical bodies or hardware systems, allowing robots to interact more naturally with people in various environments.

The industry will continue showcasing advances in embodied AI and robotic workforces featuring multilingual receptionists and wearable exoskeleton technology at the upcoming GITEX event. Companies will further explore robot foundation models, data, hardware, and simulation to overcome the technical challenges of real-world deployment in industrial operations. The articles leave open how exactly human roles will evolve as these robotics technologies advance and integrate further into the global workforce. It remains to be seen if the bunny-shaped robot and other consumer models will successfully enter homes and domestic environments as planned. Future developments depend on whether research from universities can be successfully turned into industrial innovation through continued engagement with the private sector.

stories.Headline: OpenAI and Anthropic back congressional efforts to block China's access to AI chips and tools
stories.Summary:
OpenAI recently backed a bipartisan congressional effort to block China from accessing artificial intelligence chips and chipmaking equipment this November of 2026. This support follows the recent ouster of Jensen Huang as the chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp on Thursday, November 13, 2026. Howard Lutnick, the commerce secretary, is expected to travel on Air Force One to China this week with President Donald Trump. Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and China's leader Xi Jinping. These events occur during the APEC summit as the United States considers new legislation to tighten export controls on high-end technology.

Congress is weighing three proposals, including the AI Overwatch Act, the Match Act, and the Chip Security Act, to be attached to defense legislation. The AI Overwatch Act, pushed by Jim Banks and Elizabeth Warren, seeks to freeze existing Nvidia chip sales rules for 18 months. The Match Act aims to restrict chip tools from ASML Holding NV, while the Chip Security Act requires mechanisms to prevent smuggling. These measures target the diversion of Nvidia processors and the activities of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company under investigation for improper chip smuggling. All three bills must pass before the end of the year to become law, provided President Donald Trump does not veto them.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has pushed for months to blacklist Megaspeed, while he criticized Howard Lutnick for slow-walking the Commerce Department's restrictions. Lutnick is accused of allowing Nvidia to use loopholes to sell advanced chips to China and giving the company unfettered rule-making access. The White House stated it maintains complete confidence in Lutnick, though some sources question how many lives the secretary has left. A senior US official said the Nvidia scandal should not bear on the China trip or figure in conversations with China. Representative John Moolenaar stated that Nvidia must change corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority.

Nvidia allies and trade groups argue that these provisions would harm the ecosystem of companies that are tied to the chipmaker's business. Democratic lawmakers claim the administration has failed to enforce existing export restrictions on AI chips since Donald Trump returned to office last year. The Justice Department is conducting an espionage probe into Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected of being a spy for China. Alice Huang had an affair with Jensen Huang, which led to a board investigation and his eventual resignation from the company. Anthropic PBC has also expressed support for tougher controls on AI chip exports and tightened access to sophisticated chipmaking equipment.

Jensen Huang previously used his influence to kill the Gain AI Act, which required chipmakers to ensure no US customers sought chips. The current push for legislation gains momentum because Huang was a longtime foe of stricter export controls and diminished Nvidia's Capitol Hill clout. Bipartisan support includes House Speaker Mike Johnson, New York Democrat Hakeem Jeffries, and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, though John Thune remains undecided. China's Ministry of Commerce previously vowed to take necessary measures to safeguard interests after the House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced similar bills. China has previously deployed export controls on rare earth minerals to retaliate against the United States for ratcheting up chip controls.

The administration remains wary of new policies that could imperil the delicate trade truce with China, which expires on January 10, 2027. Lawmakers and administration officials continue to negotiate the exact terms of the three bills, meaning the proposals could still be scrapped entirely. It remains open whether the legislation will pass by the end of the year or if Trump will threaten a veto. The outcome of the Justice Department's espionage probe into Alice Huang and Megaspeed may further influence the final legislative language used. The articles leave unclear if Howard Lutnick will regain his footing after clashing with Scott Bessent and other Trump administration officials.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO following a board investigation
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer of Nvidia on Thursday, November 12, 2026, following a board investigation. This sudden departure occurred after reports surfaced regarding two extramarital affairs involving the co-founder of the company. One of these relationships was with a Chinese businesswoman whom United States authorities suspect of spying for the government in Beijing. The news of the resignation caused immediate volatility for the company's stock as investors reacted to the scandal.

The company announced that Colette Kress, the veteran chief financial officer, will now serve as the interim chief executive officer. Nvidia shares experienced a sharp decline, dropping roughly 14 percent from the previous Wednesday closing price to an intraday low of 148.80 dollars per share. By the early afternoon, the stock had recovered some ground but remained down by 4.3 percent at 166.19 dollars. This leadership change comes at a time when the Nasdaq has seen gains or losses greater than 1 percent in seven of the last 10 trading days.

Investment analysts expressed mixed views, though many believe the company remains the clear leader in the artificial intelligence chip market. Bret Kenwell of eToro U.S. stated that Huang was the crown jewel of the AI trade and his exit will increase scrutiny of next week's earnings report. Dan Ives from Yorkville Ives noted that the board can now move into a new chapter despite this dark moment for the organization. He argued that the company is still two to three years ahead of its nearest competitors in GPU technology.

The company continues to follow a strategic roadmap for its next family of chips to power the ongoing artificial intelligence boom. James McCann of Edward Jones warned that the lack of a clear succession plan risks adding to the current market price volatility. He suggested that investors should avoid over-concentration in tech companies and instead maintain a well-diversified portfolio of large and midcap stocks. The firm's future now depends on whether the shift in leadership will materially affect its long-term strategy and execution.

stories.Headline: Kukoon Rugs and Seating Matters adopt AI to scale operations and boost staff productivity
stories.Summary:
Traditional industries in Northern Ireland began adopting artificial intelligence to become more competitive, as reported by Darran Mashall on November 15, 2026. Two specific companies, Kukoon Rugs and Seating Matters, have integrated this modern technology into their daily business operations. These firms use the software to scale their operations and improve the overall productivity of their various staff members. The adoption of these tools allows these traditional businesses to modernize their processes while maintaining their historical roots. This shift is happening across different sectors, including carpet making and the manufacturing of specialist clinical seating.

Kukoon Rugs, a family firm in Newry, County Down, uses AI daily in finance, commercial, marketing, supply chain, and product departments. Seating Matters, located in the Sperrin Mountains outside Limavady, exports clinical seating to healthcare facilities in the US and Australia. The products from Seating Matters have also appeared in television dramas such as Coronation Street and Emmerdale. These companies sell their goods online and through some of the biggest retail chains found across the UK and Ireland. The technology is used to sift through data, such as finding a relevant email from six years ago.

Chief Executive Paul Vallely says AI allows his team to perform more accurate, efficient, faster, and more thoughtful work. He believes the technology removes the most boring tasks from office roles and increases the excitement and engagement of his team. Managing director Martin Tierney states that AI has revolutionised back office functions like accounting, finance, and pulling data from 20 sources. Tierney claims that while AI will not replace jobs, a person who knows how to use AI could replace a worker. He compares the power of artificial intelligence to a calculator on steroids that makes accountants more productive.

Staff members at Seating Matters are affected by the technology, which Tierney says has actually led to new jobs being created. He notes that the technology is poor at customer service but excellent for managing laborious tasks and avoiding filing cabinets. Vallely argues against claims that AI negatively impacts creative industries, stating it releases time for more research and analysis. The employees are encouraged to use the software to solve problems and speed up mundane tasks within specific guardrails. These guardrails ensure that no patient information or financial information is ever put into the AI software.

Northern Ireland has a long manufacturing tradition, becoming world famous for shipbuilding and linen after the Industrial Revolution in the 19th century. Rug making is also an ancient skill that has existed in the Newry area for a very long time. The articles explain that the basic products may not change, but the design, creation, and marketing processes are changing. Tierney mentions that in the 1800s, people feared calculators would replace accountants, but the technology only increased their productivity. This historical context shows a pattern of traditional roles evolving through the introduction of new tools like Excel.

The companies will continue to use AI to handle mundane tasks while ensuring a human always checks the final work. Seating Matters will keep using the software to flesh out ideas through a chat interface without needing an IT degree. The articles leave open whether other traditional industries in Northern Ireland will follow this path to remain competitive. It remains unclear if the cautious approach to patient and financial data will change as the technology evolves further. The long term impact on the creative nature of rug making and clinical seating design is not fully detailed.

stories.Headline: Remy Cointreau uses an AI sales presenter to attract younger Chinese consumers
stories.Summary:
The French spirits maker Remy Cointreau introduced an artificial intelligence sales presenter named Eve about 18 months ago. This virtual host allows the company to recommend cognac and whiskies to Chinese shoppers at any hour, including 3 am. The initiative aims to attract new customers and expand the company's digital reach. It was highlighted during the 9th China International Import Expo in Shanghai.

The strategy involves a mix of presenters, with humans handling 80 percent of livestreaming and AI managing 20 percent. On October 28, the company reported first-half fiscal 2026-27 sales of 510.9 million euros, or 566.7 million dollars, which is an organic increase of 2.9 percent. Asia-Pacific sales rose 14.3 percent, while second-quarter e-commerce sales grew by more than 30 percent and made up about 30 percent of China sales. Chief Financial Officer Luca Marotta noted that cognac sales in China grew at a high-single-digit rate in the first half.

Sophie Phe, the CEO of Remy Cointreau China, stated that there is very little overlap between the audiences reached by AI and human hosts. She explained that the company has spent over ten years developing e-commerce tools, such as flagship stores on JD and Tmall. Phe noted that Chinese consumers are now drinking better rather than more, prioritizing quality over quantity. She observed that traditional big banquets and business dinners are decreasing in favor of small-group or personal enjoyment.

This shift is occurring as the premium spirits market in China moves away from formal business entertaining. Younger consumers are now more interested in individual preferences and exploring different flavors than following old habits. To adapt, Remy Cointreau is broadening the appeal of its portfolio, which includes Louis XIII, Cointreau, Remy Martin, and Scotch whiskies. The company is focusing on a value strategy rather than a volume strategy to reach these new drinkers.

stories.Headline: JPCERT/CC finds about 1,000 servers likely used for AI-driven cyberattacks
stories.Summary:
Around 1,000 servers suspected of serving as bases for advanced artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks have been online since October, a Japanese-led international investigation showed on Nov 14, according to Kyodo News. The probe was carried out by the Japan Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre, known as JPCERT/CC, in cooperation with overseas cybersecurity firms. The investigation found that the servers may have used AI to search for vulnerabilities and to target websites worldwide. Hacking, which previously required time even for those with specialised knowledge, has become easier with the emergence of high-level AI, the reports said.

JPCERT/CC began its investigation in early October and identified AI tools in the discovered servers, and it is tracking 600 to 700 of them. According to the centre, most of the servers hosted AI-powered platforms such as the penetration-testing tool Artex, and they appeared to be searching for system vulnerabilities and attempting to steal configuration files. One server contained traces of a programming support tool created by AI from the US company Anthropic, which suggested that attackers weaponised AI to enhance their hacking capabilities. Some publicly accessible servers contained tools for analysing the internal structure of smartphone applications and programmes for testing system vulnerabilities, and attackers are believed to have analysed apps and attempted unauthorised access through interfaces that exchange information with external systems. Servers hosting the tools can be set up in physical facilities or operated through virtual frameworks, the articles said.

Ken Sajo, an analyst at JPCERT/CC, warned that AI is still in the early stages of being used for cyberattacks and that more sophisticated attacks will increase in the future. The articles did not name any other officials or give further statements from the organisations involved. The reports, published by The Straits Times and The Mainichi on Nov 15, 2026, both credited Kyodo News and carried the same account of the investigation. The articles did not say what happens next beyond the centre's continuing tracking of the servers.
