stories.Headline: Democrats win US midterms, putting data center regulation in focus and GPU rental prices in play
stories.Summary:
The Democratic Party won an overwhelming victory in the US midterm elections, and the elections in multiple constituencies essentially evolved into referendums on AI, according to an article by Bloomberg macro strategist Simon White cited by 36Kr on 2026-11-12. The states where the Democratic Party's vote share increased the most are precisely the regions with the most dense data center layouts. After the midterm elections, data center construction faces the risk of tightened regulation and approval. The market reacted first and fell sharply last week before stabilizing somewhat, though volatility has not subsided. The world's second largest market capitalization company is mired in a spy scandal, and volatility control funds still need to reduce risk exposure to cope with higher volatility.

Energy research institution Modo Energy estimates that about 40% of announced data center projects may be impacted by the suspension order, involving a computing power capacity of up to 256 GW. Modo Energy calculates that by 2035 the net reduced computing power capacity is about 4 GW, while its estimated total planned capacity exceeds 600 GW, and the gap in Texas (ERCOT grid) is expected to be basically filled in other regions. Epoch AI data shows the total capital expenditure of a 1GW data center is about 37 billion US dollars, converted into an annual investment of about 18.5 billion US dollars according to a two-year construction cycle. CoreWeave's current annualized computing power rental revenue is about 40 billion US dollars per GW, and the rental price of NVIDIA H100 chips has risen by more than 50% in the past year. The existing computing power installed capacity in the United States is about 30 GW.

Simon White, a macro strategist at Bloomberg, pointed out that after market sentiment settles investors need to closely track the trend of GPU rental prices, the key indicator to judge whether the supply of computing power is shrinking relative to demand and then measure the evolution direction of AI transactions. He said the core question is whether the rise in GPU rental prices can be high enough to offset the losses caused by shrinking capital expenditure if data center construction is blocked. He noted there has been no obvious change in the upward trend of GPU rental prices after the election, but if new data center projects are suspended or their approvals are delayed, rental prices may accelerate to rise. He also said there has always been a gap between campaign slogans and governing realities, and it remains to be seen to what extent the Democratic Party will tighten approval of related projects.

Modo Energy believes some projects will still be promoted after being delayed, and others will move to regions with more friendly policies, whether in other US states or overseas markets. The article says a 30% price increase for 1.5 GW of existing computing power can cover the capital expenditure loss of 1 GW of new computing power, and if 10% to 20% of US existing capacity can be repriced quickly, the economic logic shifts from building new computing power to monetizing existing computing power. Since the election, the stock prices of hyperscale cloud vendors have rebounded, while the stocks of emerging cloud service providers, power suppliers and semiconductors have generally fallen. The article names NVIDIA, Eaton and Vertiv as among those disadvantaged, along with AI labs, emerging cloud service providers, data center builders, equipment suppliers and power providers. It says Anthropic and OpenAI may postpone their IPOs due to insufficient computing power.

According to Goldman Sachs data, hedge funds, the main force of last week's sell-off, saw overall position size decrease by nearly 9 percentage points in the past week and beta-adjusted risk exposure decrease by nearly 16 percentage points. Morgan Stanley pointed out that the net risk exposure of hedge funds has dropped to a one-year low. The leverage ETF capital flow shows retail selling pressure is not obvious, and on the institutional side the possibility of a full exit before investment committee review is low, with the proportion of institutional holdings in technology stocks still high. Macroeconomic data shows a deep stock market fall of more than 20% usually occurs during a recession, and there are no such signs at present. The article says large-scale cancellation of data center projects would deal a heavy blow to the economy, but this is not the baseline scenario.

The article says the establishment of this logic will drive a structural rotation within AI transactions, from AI labs, emerging cloud service providers and data center construction chains that rely on continuous expansion to hyperscalers with a large amount of existing computing power. It says hyperscale cloud vendors with abundant existing computing power will regain pricing power and premium, while AI labs, emerging cloud service providers and the data center industrial chain that rely on computing power expansion will face pressure. The article states that if capital expenditure and GPU rental prices decline simultaneously, the assertion is wrong, and otherwise the worst outcome of AI transactions may only be an internal structural rotation. It says this rotation will weaken the breadth and vitality of AI transactions but may also continue the transaction in a narrower and more fragile form. The article was written by Zhang Yaqi of Wall Street CN and published with authorization from 36Kr.

stories.Headline: KAIST team led by Yong-man Noh develops lip-reading AI that decodes ambiguous speech using context
stories.Summary:
A research team at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, led by Professor Yong-man Noh of its School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, has developed artificial intelligence technology that can accurately understand what someone is saying from lip movements alone in noisy places, KAIST said on the 15th. The team improved the accuracy of visual speech recognition, which converts speech into text by observing lip movements, by using a diffusion large language model that repeatedly fills in blanks in a sentence to decode ambiguous lip movements using the surrounding context. Existing AI systems generated sentences sequentially from the first word, so an incorrect choice at the beginning could affect the rest of the sentence, and the team changed the approach from reading in order from the beginning to reading the clearest parts first. The system first identifies words with clear lip movements and uses them as clues to decode the remaining parts, gradually resolving ambiguous sections by considering information from both before and after them in the sentence.

The team also divided training into two stages, first teaching the model to connect lip movements in videos with written text and then teaching it sentence length, and when decoding actual speech the model estimates several possible sentence lengths based on video length, compares the results and selects the sentence it considers more reliable. Using the 433-hour lip-reading video dataset LRS3 as training data with reference transcripts, the team recorded a word error rate of 19.4%, the lowest among existing methods that used only LRS3 as training data with reference transcripts. Word error rate measures how often words are incorrectly recognized, omitted or added compared with the reference sentence, and a lower rate indicates better performance. The technology could be used in communication aids that convey lip movements as text in environments where it is difficult to hear, for example in a device that understands workers' speech at industrial sites with loud machinery or in tools that help people with hearing disabilities or hearing loss communicate.

The team plans to continue its research by reducing the size and computational requirements of the AI model so it can be used on a range of devices, with a next step of enabling it to operate in real time without an internet connection on wearable devices or robots. Professor Yong-man Noh said the significance of the research lies in demonstrating that simply flexibly controlling the order in which AI generates words can overcome the fundamental limitations of speech recognition involving visual ambiguity, and that it will lay the foundation for physical AI that can be used with confidence across a range of devices in everyday life and industrial settings. The study was conducted by postdoctoral researcher Jeong-hun Yeo as first author, doctoral researchers Chae-won Kim and Hyeong-seop Ra as co-authors, and Professor Yong-man Noh as corresponding author. The paper received the Outstanding Paper Award at EMNLP 2026, a major international conference in natural language processing, and Yeo and Noh posed for a commemorative photo holding the certificate for the award.

stories.Headline: Blackstone-backed QTS cuts planned private debt sale by about 60 per cent to roughly US$300 million
stories.Summary:
QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone, reduced the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60 per cent on November 14, 2026. The company struggled to attract sufficient demand from investors and refused to offer much higher yields to secure the original amount. It is now raising approximately US$300 million after it had initially targeted a total of roughly US$800 million. This decision follows a period where the company tapped the private placement market several times to fund its growth.

The new financing includes a US$100 million seven-year US private placement that was priced on Friday to yield 2.45 percentage points more than benchmarks. It also consists of a US$200 million five-year bank loan portion that is expected to be priced in the coming weeks. Because the offering is smaller, the existing five-year bank debt that the company intended to refinance will now remain in place. This shift occurs as artificial intelligence firms seek trillions of dollars from various capital markets to finance massive infrastructure investments.

People familiar with the transaction stated that some investors were unhappy with the offered price or faced constraints due to the company's frequent borrowing. Blackstone was reportedly reluctant to increase yields because wider pricing could create a more expensive reference point for its other debt issuers. A representative at Blackstone declined to comment on the specific details of the reduced debt sale. These sources noted that the private placement market is smaller than public markets and is dominated by long term investors like asset managers.

QTS has been aggressive in seeking capital, having raised billions through at least two debt sales over the last 18 months. This includes a US$1.65 billion high-grade bond sale last year and another financing round worth US$800 million. Additionally, the company sold project finance green bonds in April and August for US$4.6 billion and US$3.9 billion respectively. Blackstone originally acquired the data center developer in 2021 for approximately US$10 billion including its existing debt.

stories.Headline: MIT leads a $53 million ARPA-H project using generative AI to design safer herbicides
stories.Summary:
On November 10, 2026, MIT announced that an MIT-led team will receive up to $53 million from the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health to use generative AI to design safer, more effective herbicides. The project is called PLOW, short for Precision Learning for On-target Weed control, and is funded under ARPA-H's STREAM program. MIT is the prime awardee and Christopher Voigt, head of MIT's Department of Biological Engineering, is the principal investigator. STREAM stands for Systems for Tracking and Resilience in Efficient Agricultural-input Management and is run by ARPA-H, the health-research agency inside the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The CASRAI editorial board published its account of the award on November 15, 2026.

The award is worth up to $53 million, a ceiling the announcement does not break down by year or milestone schedule. The team aims to develop herbicides that counter weed resistance to glyphosate and similar chemicals while posing lower risk to human health and ecosystems. The project also targets the reliance of U.S. glyphosate production on imported phosphorus, a key ingredient, and includes work on engineered microbial systems that break down agrochemicals before they reach food, soil or water. The other named organizations are the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, UNC Chapel Hill, the University of Tennessee at Knoxville, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and Robigo. HHS and ARPA-H launched STREAM on August 17, 2026, and the program manager is CAPT James Coburn.

The MIT account describes a loop between computation and the lab in which AI models generate large candidate libraries and a high-throughput screening team tests them. The results feed back to improve the models, and narrowed candidates then move to greenhouse studies under varied agricultural conditions. The models are designed to predict either chemical compounds or small interfering RNA that could disrupt the plant enzymes targeted by glyphosate and other herbicides. Candidates are optimized for low synthesis cost, low resistance risk and low risk to people and the environment. MIT says the first greenhouse tests of initial RNA-interference candidates are expected by the end of the program's first year.

ARPA-H Chief Medical Officer Rafid Fadul said American farmers are locked in an arms race against weeds, which evolve faster than the tools available to fight them, according to MyChesCo on August 24, 2026. Coburn was quoted on the need for better ways to monitor and protect drinking water from unintended agricultural chemical exposure. Welcome.AI's summary of the MIT release notes that more than 1 billion pounds of herbicides are applied annually in the U.S. and paraphrases Voigt's view that herbicide resistance combined with supply-chain vulnerability could jeopardize the availability of essential agrochemicals. The MIT account links herbicide exposure to concerns including cancer and endocrine disorders.

The STREAM announcement frames the program as a way to help farmers control weeds while protecting agricultural workers, consumers and the environment. It names four technical areas: next-generation herbicides and formulations using AI and machine learning; precision and nonchemical weed control such as laser ablation, autonomous weeders and drone application; low-cost, continuous monitoring of herbicides and related chemicals; and methods to degrade herbicides in soil and water and reduce crop residues. PLOW addresses the first technical area, and the ARPA-H page says selected teams are listed in a STREAM awardee directory. The solicitation ARPA-H-SOL-24-105, "Scalable Solutions," used a two-step process with a Solution Summary deadline of September 14, 2026 and a full-proposal deadline of December 10, 2026. The program page now says the opportunity is closed to new applicants, and awards are expected through Other Transactions Agreements with final decisions dependent on proposal quality.

STREAM supports an HHS, USDA and EPA commitment to invest more than $1 billion in farm modernization and long-term food security, according to the same announcement, and the pages give no dollar figure for STREAM itself. The next milestone MIT names is completion of the first greenhouse tests of initial RNAi candidates by the end of the first program year. The ARPA-H program page remains the place to watch for further teams and any later solicitations. The agreement terms are not public, and the sources do not state the subaward arrangements for the partner institutions. The announcement does not give a year-by-year breakdown or milestone schedule for drawing down the funding.

stories.Headline: Chinese firms showcase AI robots and flying cars at the Web Summit in Lisbon
stories.Summary:
Chinese robotics company Galbot exhibited its G1 robot during the four-day Web Summit 2026 in Lisbon on November 11. This specific machine uses artificial intelligence to understand its surroundings and perform various physical tasks. The robot features a wheeled base and two arms to help it operate in factories, pharmacies, and convenience stores. These exhibits highlight how advances in manufacturing and AI are opening up new applications for physical machines.

The G1 robot requires a combination of AI and a mobile base to function in commercial settings. This technology changes how people might work in retail or industrial environments by automating physical labor. Other Chinese firms also displayed innovations, such as the Land Aircraft Carrier from XPENG ARIDGE, which includes a six-wheeled ground vehicle and a detachable electric aircraft. This system is designed to make aircraft easier to store, recharge, and transport across different locations.

Zhao Deli, the founder of XPENG ARIDGE, stated that the global flying-car industry will likely enter a period of rapid development over the next decade. He explained that these vehicles could first serve emergency rescue and recreational flying before expanding to point-to-point transportation. Zhao also noted that China's electric vehicle supply chain could reduce production costs to make these flying cars more affordable. His company is currently pursuing international cooperation to support the development of low-altitude aviation.

stories.Headline: Downing Street says Andy Burnham writes most of his own speeches after aide is photographed using ChatGPT on a train
stories.Summary:
Downing Street said on Nov 15 that Prime Minister Andy Burnham writes most of his own speeches, after the Mail on Sunday published photos that appeared to show one of his aides using AI to prepare a speech. The Mail on Sunday said the aide, with a glass of prosecco in hand, used ChatGPT to rework a speech for the Labour leader while on board a train. The images were said to have been taken on Nov 13 by a fellow passenger before Burnham gave a speech to the Welsh Labour party conference in Cardiff. The newspaper said the aide used the AI app to ask how to make the speech more emotive.

A Downing Street spokesperson said an aide sought feedback on a speech draft that had already been written, and the spokesperson insisted that the PM writes most of his own speeches. The Press Association news agency reported that the suggestions from ChatGPT did not make it into the final speech. The government said the AI suggestions were not used in the final speech. The Mail on Sunday said the aide used AI to make a draft more emotive before Burnham’s speech to Welsh Labour in Cardiff.

The story concerns Andy Burnham, the British Prime Minister and Labour leader, and an unnamed aide who was photographed on a train on Nov 13. Downing Street played down the photos published in the Sunday newspaper, with a spokesperson quoted by the domestic Press Association news agency. The newspaper posted the snap of the aide using ChatGPT to rework a speech of the Labour leader while on board a train. The images were said to have been taken before Burnham gave a speech to the Welsh Labour party conference in Cardiff.

stories.Headline: AI-generated short dramas transform the Chinese entertainment market with lower costs and massive viewership
stories.Summary:
A massive surge in AI-generated short dramas has transformed the Chinese entertainment market throughout 2026. One breakout hit, Armed into the Song Dynasty, premiered on August 22 and has already reached 1,000 episodes with over 4 billion views. This series was created by a small grassroots team including Zhang Hansheng, a 54-year-old who taught himself AI video generation last March. Other titles like the sci-fi series Guixu launched in May and reached 100 million views with a modest investment of 200,000 yuan.

The technology drastically reduces costs, with premium AI dramas costing about one-tenth as much as live-action versions in early 2026. A 100-episode series can now be completed in three days, while a single minute of runtime for Guixu cost 2,000 yuan in computing power. The market exceeded 22 billion yuan in the first five months of the year and is forecast to reach 40 billion yuan. Cao Shumin of the National Radio and Television Administration reported that 550,000 micro and short dramas were released in the first ten months of the year, with over 94 percent being AI-made.

Major tech firms like Tencent, ByteDance, and Kuaishou are competing for market share by providing production and distribution platforms. Hao Cheng of Mango TV noted that AI simplifies localization, which will accelerate the expansion of Chinese dramas into overseas markets. Despite the growth, DataEye reports that only 1.3 percent of these dramas turn a profit, while 98.7 percent operate at a loss. The National Radio and Television Administration launched a two-month campaign in November to target vulgar or formulaic content.

The industry faces significant quality bottlenecks, including inconsistent facial rendering and unnatural movements that break viewer immersion. While the first AI theatrical feature, Sanxingdui: Future Past, released on October 23, grossed only 1.8 million yuan, BONA Film Group views it as an experiment. Regulators now require explicit consent for using faces or voices, alongside human reviews and traceable records for all AI content. Developers continue to push the technology from short clips toward long-form narratives and full-length feature films.

stories.Headline: World Media Summit participants discuss balancing AI efficiency with journalistic ethics
stories.Summary:
The World Media Summit took place in Beijing from November 5 to 9, providing a global platform for professional exchanges. This event was jointly organized by the Beijing municipal government and the Xinhua News Agency to foster trust among international media organizations. Vugar Aliyev, who serves as the chairman of the Board of Azerbaijan State News Agency AZERTAC, participated in the summit to discuss the role of journalism. He emphasized that such gatherings allow newsrooms to establish direct contacts and launch joint projects to overcome common stereotypes.

The summit operated under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action" to address the rapid development of artificial intelligence. Approximately 500 representatives from nearly 330 media organizations, government bodies, think tanks, and international organizations across 112 countries and regions attended the event. Participants explored how to harness AI for better news production while avoiding ethical pitfalls that could undermine public trust. The goal was to balance the speed of AI data processing with the necessity of maintaining high editorial standards.

Vugar Aliyev stated that while AI can overcome language barriers and analyze large volumes of data, it also introduces risks like misinformation and manipulation. He argued that technology should assist journalists rather than replace their professional responsibility to the public. According to Aliyev, quality journalism must remain rooted in source transparency, rigorous fact-checking, and strong editorial oversight. He believes that strengthening direct ties between media organizations will contribute to a better mutual understanding between the peoples of Azerbaijan and China.

The summit also served as a way for international attendees to experience the modern development and rich cultural heritage of China. Aliyev noted that AZERTAC focuses its coverage on Chinese technological achievements, the digital economy, and major infrastructure projects. He believes that reporting on both major events and everyday people helps global audiences gain a more comprehensive picture of Chinese society. By sharing professional experiences with Chinese colleagues, Aliyev hopes to identify new areas for cooperation in the political and economic fields.

stories.Headline: Chinese creators earn revenue from viral AI-generated pet videos
stories.Summary:
Chinese content creators are using artificial intelligence to produce viral pet videos that have attracted millions of viewers across various social media platforms. Maoziqi, a former real estate planner, now creates full-time videos featuring two AI cats that have earned over 670,000 followers on Bilibili. Other creators, including a graphic designer who makes videos of a cat named Yunmi and another artist who features a pig named Juju, have also found success. These creators utilize tools like ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 model, which was released in February, to build elaborate animal worlds.

This shift requires significant human effort in scriptwriting and repeated generation to refine visual segments, as AI storylines often lack dramatic tension. The trend is part of a larger boom where China released nearly 550,000 micro-dramas between January and October, which is nearly 17 times the total for 2025. AI productions accounted for more than 94 percent of these series, and DataEye projects the market for AI-made dramas will reach 40 billion yuan this year. This represents a 138 percent increase from 2025, with over 500,000 practitioners active in the first half of 2026.

The creators earn substantial income through brand partnerships, with Maoziqi featuring products from Peet's Coffee and Prada. The creator of Juju reports that each branded collaboration brings in at least 10,000 yuan, while Yunmi's creator earns more from advertising than from her day job. Cao Long of Migu Digital Media stated that emotional resonance and rounded characters are what sustain viewership beyond initial novelty. Meanwhile, Wang Xiaoliang of the National Radio and Television Administration noted that while AI improves efficiency, it creates new challenges for content quality and rights protection.

The popularity of these videos stems from a strong appetite among young viewers for pet-themed content that overcomes the physical limitations of filming real animals. Li Tianyu of the Beijing Film Academy explained that AI allows creators to give animals human-like roles and complex actions. Despite the success, creators face issues with unauthorized reposting on platforms like Instagram, where some copies attract more traffic than the originals. Maoziqi admitted that widespread fame has brought personal anxiety regarding public perception, though he remains focused on his own creative process.

stories.Headline: US and Chinese filmmakers meet in Los Angeles to discuss AI integration and co-productions
stories.Summary:
American and Chinese filmmakers, scholars, and industry representatives gathered in Los Angeles during the week of November 11, 2026. These professionals met at the historic TCL Chinese Theatre to participate in the 22nd Annual Chinese American Film Festival and the Chinese American Television Festival. The group focused on exploring new ways to collaborate on animation, film distribution, and short-form mobile dramas. They also discussed the integration of artificial intelligence and the potential for future co-productions.

This cooperation requires a two-way exchange where American companies help Chinese stories reach global audiences while Chinese platforms provide new production capabilities to Hollywood. The scale of this partnership is significant because the United States and China represent the two largest movie markets in the world. Comscore reported that the combined U.S. and Canada market reached 8.87 billion U.S. dollars in 2025 ticket sales. Meanwhile, the China Film Administration recorded 2025 box office sales of 51.83 billion yuan, which is approximately 7.37 billion dollars.

Academy Award winner Richard L. Anderson praised the talent and hard work of Chinese crews, stating there are no technical differences between them and American teams. Producer Arthur Sarkissian noted that the most difficult part of co-production is creating a story that appeals to both Chinese and American viewers. Former studio executive Michael Fisk described artificial intelligence as a useful tool that will lead to a massive explosion of content. Bob Underwood of the Writers Guild of America West emphasized that working with China can enhance the ability of real people to tell stories.

The participants discussed how artificial intelligence can help the industry overcome language barriers and facilitate more efficient collaboration across the Pacific. The appeal of the Chinese market was highlighted by the success of Zootopia 2, which earned over 630 million dollars in China. This specific film accounted for about 35 percent of its total worldwide earnings and received the Most Popular U.S. Film in China Award. The filmmakers believe that mutual cooperation will allow both nations to better navigate the rapid technological changes currently affecting the global film industry.

Articles.Title: American, Chinese filmmakers gather in Los Angeles to explore cooperation in AI era - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Chinese manufacturer Qingdao Ruilijie Metal uses AI to program precision mold machines and cut costs
stories.Summary:
Qingdao Ruilijie Metal Co., Ltd. implemented an artificial intelligence programming system in July 2026 to write instructions for precision mold machines. This technology helps the factory produce parts like washing machine front panels while reducing costly waste caused by design deviations. The transition required an 80-person team to spend one full year collecting and standardizing technical drawings to create a usable dataset. After engineers added an automatic verification function to fix early sizing errors, the system began expanding to other moldmakers.

The new system shortened development cycles for new orders by approximately one week and saved the company over 3 million yuan, or about 447,000 U.S. dollars, annually. This project is part of a broader AI Plus initiative launched by the government in 2024 to develop tools for mining, ports, and logistics. Official figures from October indicate that over one-third of larger manufacturing enterprises have adopted AI in key application scenarios. Developers now aim to bring these tools to 100 small and medium-sized firms by the end of the year.

Factory director Guo Weiwei stated that the AI system reduced defects and significantly lowered annual costs for the company. Yu Tao from the State Grid Tai'an power supply company noted that AI drone inspections of electricity lines around Mount Tai are six times more efficient. Miao Yanliang, the chief economist at China International Capital Corporation, suggested that China's comprehensive industrial base and vast market provide a competitive edge. These leaders believe that directing AI toward wider practical applications will continue to drive industrial efficiency.

China is applying these technologies across various sectors, including healthcare systems at West China Hospital of Sichuan University and lung cancer research in Guangzhou. A September study by the International Labour Organization found that some Chinese manufacturers saw production efficiency gains between 20 and 30 percent. AI is also being used to analyze digital pathology images and manage patient follow-ups across 43 clinical departments. The government continues to encourage the integration of these tools to refine specific industrial and medical tasks.

Articles.Title: China has a job for AI - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Tmall integrates AI token services into its e-commerce platform for Singles Day sales
stories.Summary:
Tmall integrated AI token services into its e-commerce platform for the annual Singles Day shopping festival. A livestreaming star sold 100,000 QwenWork monthly membership cards in thirty minutes. These subscriptions were sold at a promotional price of 0.01 yuan each. The total allowance for these memberships was about 2 trillion tokens. This event occurred during the sales campaign that began on October 20.

Tmall launched its token recharge center on September 3 to host various AI service providers. These providers include Alibaba Cloud, DeepSeek, Zhipu AI, Kimi, QwenWork, and StepFun. MiniMax opened its first official flagship store on the platform during this period. Transaction values in the token category rose 450 percent month on month. Tokens are basic units used to measure large language model inference for billing.

A Tmall representative said the main customers are individuals and small businesses with clear AI needs. These buyers include households, one-person businesses, and people using AI for learning and research. Fan Yubo said providers are making services easier to understand by packaging them into subscriptions. He noted that nominal prices encourage first time users to try these AI services. Fan added that AI is becoming a productive tool rather than just a novelty.

Zhang Ji, an office worker in Shandong Province, used Qwen for work and trip planning. Su Guoqing from Qinghai Province bought tokens to improve his short video scene creation. Wang Daoxing of a Chongqing company bought a year of Qwen memberships for software development. A Tencent Research Institute survey in May found only 9.8 percent of users paid for tools. Most users, over 90 percent, still rely on free AI services.

Tokens were previously billed through providers' own systems, which left users with little price information. This new e-commerce model allows consumers to compare prices and purchase tokens in one place. Tokens represent AI generated output involving costs for electricity, equipment depreciation, and graphics processing units. Ding Ding noted that token services cannot follow the low marginal cost model of mobile data. Overselling these services can lead to throttling and queues for the users.

Industry insiders say challenges remain in security controls, compliance, pricing mechanisms, and accounting. Ma Shenglong noted that token consumption for the same text varies by 20 to 50 percent. Wang Jiandong suggested establishing unified standards for token measurement and introducing third party verification. Consumers want clearer rules for purchase disputes and handling unused quotas through after sales services. It remains open whether users will renew subscriptions after using their initial promotional packages.

stories.Headline: Ni Yueju proposes a framework for AI cooperation among Northeast Asian economies
stories.Summary:
Ni Yueju, a research fellow at the Institute of World Economics and Politics within the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, discussed artificial intelligence cooperation on October 30. She shared these insights during a symposium that was co-organized by the China Daily Opinion Channel and the International Business School of Beijing Foreign Studies University. The event took place in Beijing to explore how Northeast Asian economies could utilize their complementary strengths for practical gains. This gathering focused on turning theoretical potential into actual regional partnerships through strategic technological alignment. The proposed framework requires a step-by-step approach to building regional trust through specific practical applications.

Ni Yueju suggested that cooperation should begin with smart manufacturing and the implementation of in-vehicle artificial intelligence systems. She further outlined significant opportunities in the fields of green computing, the sharing of public data, and the exchange of professional talent. Additionally, the strategy emphasizes the need for increased supply-chain resilience to ensure the stability of regional technological growth. Ni Yueju is responsible for these recommendations and believes that regional trust must be established gradually.

She argued that focusing on concrete applications first would allow these economies to bridge gaps more effectively. By prioritizing shared interests in manufacturing and data, the nations can create a foundation for broader collaboration. Her perspective emphasizes that practical successes are the most reliable way to foster long-term diplomatic and economic ties. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Xinxiang First People's Hospital uses AI to screen diabetic patients for retinopathy
stories.Summary:
Since September, the Xinxiang First People's Hospital in Henan province has utilized artificial intelligence to screen diabetic patients for retinopathy. This specific medical complication can gradually destroy a person's eyesight if it is not detected and treated early. The charity-backed pilot program aims to provide free screenings to local residents to prevent permanent vision loss. Organizers hope that this successful model can be copied in other cities across the country.

The program runs until December and is managed by the Chinese Foundation for Lifeline Express alongside other medical institutions in Xinxiang. These efforts were reviewed at a hospital meeting held before World Diabetes Day on November 14, which marks the twentieth anniversary of the United Nations recognizing the day. The International Diabetes Federation's Diabetes Atlas reported that China had approximately 148 million adults with diabetes in 2024. This number continues to rise as the general population ages and daily lifestyles change.

Guo Wei, the secretary-general of the foundation, stated that Lifeline Express began screening for retinopathy in 2014. The foundation is best known for a hospital train that provided free cataract surgery to over 250,000 people since 1997. Guo Wei noted that more than 310,000 diabetic patients have been screened, with about 23 percent having the condition. Nearly 3 percent of those screened were found to have severe cases of the disease.

The foundation cited studies showing that retinopathy affects about 19 percent of patients who have had diabetes for less than five years. This risk increases significantly over time, affecting more than 70 percent of patients who have lived with the disease for over 15 years. One patient, 46-year-old Li Jikun, has managed his diabetes with insulin injections and medication for more than a decade. He experienced the severity of the condition when he woke up one morning unable to see properly.

stories.Headline: South Korean chip firms eye China as US political shifts threaten AI infrastructure demand
stories.Summary:
The Financial Times published a report on Thursday warning that Democratic victories in the US midterm elections could halt the construction boom of data centers. This political shift creates significant uncertainty for South Korean semiconductor firms that rely heavily on the American market for their high bandwidth memory and server DRAM. These specific memory products are primarily used in artificial intelligence servers, meaning any slowdown in US infrastructure development directly threatens the demand underpinning South Korean exports. Consequently, these chipmakers now face a situation where their growth prospects in the United States may stall or decline due to these new political headwinds.

The impact of this shift is evident when looking at the Bank of Korea data from July regarding shipments in 2025. The United States ranked as the fourth largest destination for South Korean semiconductor exports, with shipments totaling 19.02 billion dollars compared to 13.626 billion dollars three years prior. This growth saw the US share of total exports rise from 9.6 percent to 10.3 percent, while the Chinese mainland remained the largest market. China took shipments worth 74.46 billion dollars in 2025, which represented 40.3 percent of the total semiconductor exports from South Korea. These figures highlight why South Korean firms may now prioritize diversifying their markets toward China to sustain their growth.

The Yonhap News Agency reported in September that South Korea intends to double its semiconductor production capacity within the next five years. To maintain their presence in China, South Korean firms must offer their most advanced products, though US restrictions on high bandwidth memory exports make this difficult. This challenge is compounded by the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which has led to fresh calls in Washington for even tighter restrictions on Chinese chip access. South Korean chipmakers must navigate these pressures while competing against Chinese domestic producers who are making rapid technological progress. These domestic firms possess extensive industrial supply chains that could allow them to scale up production quickly once technical hurdles are overcome.

The Global Times suggests that South Korea should assert its own economic interests because semiconductors are vital to the national economy. The publication argues that chipmakers have every reason to press for more room to sell advanced products in the Chinese market. Following US priorities alone risks undermining South Korean industrial interests, especially as Washington attracts investment while simultaneously imposing restrictive trade barriers. The situation remains complex as memory chip prices stay high, indicating strong underlying demand that South Korean suppliers cannot afford to ignore. Future success will likely depend on whether these firms can overcome American restrictions to serve their largest customer in China.

stories.Headline: Chinese university student earns 2 million yuan from AI animated series
stories.Summary:
Xiao Tianle, a third-year student majoring in mechanical and electronic engineering at Soochow University, created an AI-powered animated series from his dormitory in Suzhou. This ambitious project drew more than 1.5 billion views and generated up to 2 million yuan in revenue for the young creator. Working with a dedicated team, he managed to produce hundreds of AI-generated animated productions in less than one year. The collective efforts of his team resulted in a total revenue exceeding 3 million yuan during that same period.

The production process requires a human touch because AI scripts are often too flat and lack necessary conflict. Xiao and his team must analyze these scripts and break them down into individual shots to ensure a compelling narrative. They also have to refine the AI-generated footage to correct physical errors and awkward facial expressions before the final release. To manage his growing business, Xiao registered a start-up company in Suzhou during August of this year. He now balances his university classes and project work with frequent online meetings and discussions with potential investors.

Xiao told the Yangtse Evening Post that he developed a fascination with making short films while he was still in high school. He spent his spare time carrying a camera to learn about camera positioning, storytelling techniques, and building emotional resonance. After entering university, he taught himself video editing and completed an apprenticeship at a company specializing in training newcomers. This experience allowed him to progress from adjusting simple prompts to overseeing entire productions for real short drama projects. He expressed his desire to eventually create a feature film with a story that truly stays with the audience.

Following his graduation, Xiao plans to remain in the city of Suzhou to further his professional education. He intends to study the arts of directing and screenwriting to improve the quality of his future cinematic works. His long-term goal involves recruiting new talent to lead a professional team producing television dramas and films using AI technology. By combining technical engineering skills with creative storytelling, he hopes to push the boundaries of modern digital animation.

Articles.Title: Undergraduate generates 2 million yuan with AI-powered animated series - Global Times

stories.Headline: Adaspace Technology lists on Hong Kong Stock Exchange to fund space-based AI computing
stories.Summary:
The Chengdu-based artificial intelligence satellite maker Adaspace Technology Co Ltd began trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on Friday, November 13, 2026. This debut marks a significant step for the commercialization of orbital AI infrastructure and space-based computing. The company offered 30.121 million H shares at HK$24.90 each, which raised gross proceeds of approximately HK$750 million. After costs, the net proceeds totaled about HK$652 million, and the shares closed at HK$24.02 on the first day.

The company plans to use these funds to build a satellite research and testing center and advance in-orbit computing technologies. It will also pursue industrial acquisitions, supplement working capital, repay borrowings, and support its Star-Compute project. This project aims to deploy a constellation of 2,800 AI-enabled satellites by 2035 to provide computing power for millions of silicon-based agents. As of October 28, 2026, the firm had developed six AI payloads, four application satellites, and 26 computing satellites across 15 missions.

Li Chang'an, a professor at the University of International Business and Economics, stated that the listing reflects strong investor interest in China's commercial space economy. He noted that innovative mainland firms are using Hong Kong as a platform to raise funds and expand their international presence. Li further explained that the listing provides the company with the necessary funding to accelerate its space-based AI computing development. He highlighted a shift toward value-added services like orbital data processing rather than simple satellite manufacturing.

The company reported 2025 revenue of about 703 million yuan, which was a 27.0 percent increase over the previous year. By October 2026, Adaspace had secured orders for 114 AI satellites with a total contract value of approximately 3.475 billion yuan. This growth occurs as China integrates computing power into satellite networks to enhance orbital systems. Preliminary estimates suggest that China's space-based computing power industry could exceed 250 billion yuan by 2030.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA publishes an IDC InfoBrief on sovereign AI for insurance
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA published an IDC InfoBrief on sovereign AI for insurance, dated 14 November 2026, with a second version dated 12 November 2026. The company also held a webinar on 3 November 2026 about the research. The InfoBrief looks at how insurers can deploy AI securely and at scale. It covers underwriting, claims, fraud detection and compliance.

The InfoBrief sets out several goals for insurers using sovereign and private AI. It says they should move AI from pilot to production while protecting sensitive data and keeping governance, explainability and regulatory compliance. It also lists ways to transform underwriting and claims, strengthen fraud detection while protecting sensitive data, and build trust through explainability and auditability. NTT DATA's AI Factory is described as helping organizations move from isolated AI pilots to secure, governed AI at scale with measurable business outcomes. The pages invite readers to get the InfoBrief, read a data sheet and explore a chapter for their industry.

NTT DATA presents the research as showing how insurers scale AI with trust and control. The company says its AI Factory helps organizations move from isolated pilots to governed AI at scale. The pages describe the aim as building trusted, resilient AI for insurance. They also offer a form asking for contact details such as name, email, job title, country, phone number and company.

The pages link to related material, including a blog from 14 October 2026 on agentic AI as the biggest shift in insurance since digital transformation. They also link to a 2026 Global AI Report for Insurance dated 9 June 2026 and a report on fast-tracking the future of insurance dated 3 September 2026. The InfoBrief is presented as guidance on sovereign AI for insurance, with a chapter for each industry. The pages do not say what happens after readers request the InfoBrief.

stories.Headline: Kopin moves headquarters staff to free floor space for microLED manufacturing
stories.Summary:
Kopin is moving its headquarters staff from 125 North Drive in Westborough, Massachusetts, to 75 North Drive because it needs the old building's floor space for manufacturing. Optics.org reported the plan in its November 12 business round-up. The expansion could add up to 80 jobs over five years. The state is backing it with an Investment Tax Credit of about $1.46 million under the Economic Development Incentive Program and an $800,000 grant from the Massachusetts Manufacturing Innovation Initiative.

The microLEDs made there will go to color microdisplays for next-generation soldier and pilot systems and to Neural I/o, a Kopin interconnect that sends data between AI processors as light. Photonics Spectra's November editorial names Avicena, ams OSRAM, Credo, Ennostar and Kopin, working with partner Fabric.AI, among companies pushing microLEDs into optical communications. Q.ANT, based in Stuttgart, and IONOS, a cloud provider for small and mid-sized businesses, opened a pilot putting Q.ANT's second-generation Native Processing Unit on a bare metal server in a German IONOS data center. Applicants approved through the IONOS website can run their own workloads there with their own data and software.

Kopin CEO Michael Murray described the plan in terms of engineering talent, equipment and domestic production capacity. Q.ANT founder and CEO Michael Förtsch said the AI conversation is turning from what models can do to what they cost to run. IONOS CEO Achim Weiss said the processor runs under German jurisdiction and that the pilot's results will show which applications benefit most and shape the companies' next development work. Q.ANT says its processor computes complex nonlinear functions directly in light, so developers can build smaller models that run faster.

Sajan Saini, education director at MIT's Initiative for Knowledge and Innovation in Manufacturing, told Optics & Photonics News that some experts estimate bringing optics right up to the chip can cut a data center's power use by 30%, and possibly by as much as 50%. Saini was describing co-packaged optics in general, not microLED links in particular. Writer Stewart Wills reports in the same OPN feature that the biggest US shortage is in technicians and other middle-skilled workers. He cites a November 2023 study in Applied Optics that estimated demand for 42,000 new middle-skilled photonics workers by 2030, and at current graduation rates meeting that demand would take about 100 more community college programs.

On November 3, Optics.org reported that PsiQuantum launched an optical circuit switch built on the silicon photonics platform it has spent nearly a decade developing for quantum computers. The first unit is an 8×8 demonstration switch, and PsiQuantum is sending samples to selected prospective customers. According to PsiQuantum, lab results of 1.2 dB typical insertion loss with no amplification needed, 40 dB crosstalk and under 3 ms reconfiguration time all beat the targets it set for the device. The barium titanate technology behind its 64×64 quantum switch isn't needed for this demonstration unit or for the first products, so the company keeps it in reserve for faster future products. Commercial products are due to be announced in the coming months.

Opdo, an AI-native optical engineering startup in Los Angeles, raised $2.3 million in pre-seed funding from investors including Angular Ventures. Co-founder and CEO Stephan Kuehr's pitch is that hardware teams have optics problems waiting in line and too few engineers to work on them. RadianX, previously called California Perovskite Technology, raised $9 million in combined venture and project financing, co-led by SOSV and Twynam. Pacific Union Technology Precision Manufacturing is separately funding a dedicated production line in its facility, and CEO Vivian Qu describes that line, RadianX's first automated 6 MW line, as a design the company can repeat at larger scale elsewhere. SPIE Photonics West runs from January 30 to February 4, 2027, at the Moscone Center in San Francisco, and PsiQuantum's Pete Shadbolt is on the list of plenary and Hot Topics speakers.

stories.Headline: Digantara raises $50m led by Reliance Industries to expand space situational awareness
stories.Summary:
Bengaluru-based spacetech startup Digantara has secured USD 50 million in a funding round led by Reliance Industries, according to a report published on February 2, 2026, which values the company at approximately USD 200 million. The round also included participation from 360 One Asset, Tokyo-based SBI Holdings, and entrepreneur Ronnie Screwvala, while existing investors Peak XV Partners and Kalaari Capital took part as well. The funding follows Digantara's announcement in December 2025 that it had completed a USD 50 million Series B round. The company was founded in December 2020 by Anirudh Sharma and specializes in space situational awareness and intelligence.

The fresh capital will fuel Digantara's global expansion, with a significant focus on the United States market, and will scale its production and satellite manufacturing capabilities. The company currently provides services to defense markets in India, the United States, the United Kingdom, Singapore, Australia, and Japan, and it plans to extend into Europe by mid-2026. Digantara's selection to participate in the Golden Dome missile system program, described as a multi-layered defense effort integrating ground, sea, air, and space-based systems, further supports its US push. Its proprietary space camera can monitor objects at a resolution of up to five centimeters, surpassing the industry standard of around ten centimeters. Digantara has three satellites operational in orbit, with the first two focused on space weather and the most recent dedicated to space object tracking.

The company operates an integrated platform named AIRA that combines sensing hardware, data processing, and analytics across space and terrestrial systems. Its infrastructure includes the SCOT constellation for space surveillance, the ALBATROSS series for missile warning and tracking, and SKYGATE, a network of ground-based sensors, with phased deployment scheduled throughout 2026 and 2027. The spacetech sector has seen a notable increase in venture capital interest over the past year, highlighted by Agnikul Cosmos raising USD 17 million in November 2025 at a valuation of USD 500 million and reusable rocket maker EtherealX securing USD 20.5 million earlier this month in a round co-led by TDK Ventures and BIG Capital. The articles do not name the investors' representatives or include direct statements from them about the funding.

Articles.Title: digantara secures 50m led by reliance industries for space situational awareness expansion

stories.headline_source: digantara secures 50m led by reliance industries for space situational awareness expansion

stories.Headline: NTT Data is placed in the Leaders Category of IDC MarketScape for cloud services in the AI era
stories.Summary:
NTT DATA announced on 12 November 2026 that it had been placed in the Leaders Category of the IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Cloud Professional Services in the AI Era 2026 Vendor Assessment. The assessment was published by IDC in September 2026 under the number US54117426 and was written by Jennifer Thomson and Eren Eser. The vendor assessment examines the providers that help organizations build the data, governance and operating foundations required for AI at scale. NTT DATA shared the result in an insights post on its website dated 12 November 2026. The assessment frames cloud as no longer simply a destination for modernization but as the platform that enables AI-driven business outcomes.

It covers the role cloud must play in an AI strategy and treats AI-model and hyperscaler ecosystem access as a selection factor. It also addresses AI governance, FinOps and agentic operating models, along with sovereign cloud and data residency capabilities. The post says readers can learn why NTT DATA was recognized as a Leader and offers a download of the assessment. IDC MarketScape uses a rigorous scoring methodology based on both qualitative and quantitative criteria, which results in a single graphical illustration of each supplier's position within a given market. The framework lets technology buyers compare the product and service offerings, capabilities and strategies, and current and future market success factors of suppliers.

IDC describes the model as providing a 360-degree assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of current and prospective suppliers. The post attributes the Leaders placement to the independent assessment rather than to NTT DATA's own evaluation. The post presents cloud as the foundation for AI at scale and lists the topics the assessment covers for organizations weighing cloud providers. It does not state how many vendors were assessed, what scores NTT DATA received or where other providers were placed. The articles give no information on what happens next beyond the availability of the download and the related insights link.

Articles.Title: Cloud Is the Foundation for AI at Scale - NTT Data

stories.headline_source: Cloud Is the Foundation for AI at Scale

stories.Headline: Manas AI reduces early cancer drug discovery time from eight years to three months
stories.Summary:
Dr. Siddhartha Mukherjee, an oncologist and CEO of Manas AI, announced on Saturday at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026 that artificial intelligence is accelerating early cancer drug discovery. He explained that the time required for this initial phase has dropped from nearly eight years to just three or four months. This American startup uses machine learning combined with physics and chemistry to build new drug molecules from atoms to block disease proteins. For example, identifying a target spot on a pancreatic cancer protein now takes two hours instead of a decade.

The company pairs molecular design with robotic lab testing to complete design and test cycles every three weeks. These efforts produce experimental cancer candidates that are up to 200 times stronger than current competitor drugs. Dr. Mukherjee also co-founded Immuneel Therapeutics with Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw in Bengaluru to create customized blood cancer treatments. These treatments cost roughly 35,000 dollars in India, which is significantly lower than the 500,000 dollars charged in the United States.

Dr. Mukherjee stated that while AI saves time and money early on, it does not yet reduce the cost of clinical trials or regulatory timelines. He urged India and China to implement technological and regulatory reforms to streamline testing rules without compromising safety. He noted that cancer cannot be cured all at once because every type of cancer is biologically distinct. While progress is strong for leukemia, lymphoma, and breast cancer, stomach and pancreatic cancers remain very difficult challenges.

The World Health Organization and its research agency reported in 2026 that there are 20.6 million new cancer cases and 10 million deaths globally each year. In India, that report estimates 1.56 million new cases and over 900,000 annual deaths, with 3.32 million people living with the disease. Additionally, the Indian Council of Medical Research projected 1.57 million cases for 2025 and noted that one in nine Indians faces a lifetime risk of cancer.

Articles.Title: AI cuts early cancer drug discovery from 8 years to 3 months: Dr Siddhartha Mukherjee

stories.headline_source: AI cuts early cancer drug discovery from 8 years to 3 months: Dr Siddhartha Mukherjee

stories.Headline: CoreWeave results and Anthropic IPO roadshow lift AI stocks on Wednesday
stories.Summary:
AI stocks rallied on Wednesday, boosted by results from neocloud company CoreWeave and upbeat feedback from Anthropic's ongoing campaign to sell its blockbuster IPO to Wall Street, according to Investor's Business Daily. The report said the AI trade was propped up as Anthropic's roadshow went well. Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, told Investor's Business Daily that shares were up because the Anthropic roadshow was going well. The article also pointed to Nvidia earnings and the Anthropic IPO as events that loomed over the market. The report gave no specific figures for the rally and named no dates beyond Wednesday, while the article was dated November 11, 2026.

It described CoreWeave's results as a factor behind the move and said Anthropic's IPO was a blockbuster offering still being sold to investors. The same article listed related coverage on the stock market falling while the Nasdaq held a key level, and on Dow Jones futures as Bitcoin tumbled with the market rally shaky. It also referenced a separate piece titled "Anthropic's Blockbuster IPO Is Near. Here's What Analysts Are Saying." Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, was the only person the article quoted on the rally, and he credited Anthropic's roadshow for lifting shares.

The article did not say who at CoreWeave or Anthropic commented, and it gave no statement from Nvidia. Responsibility for the reported moves was attributed to the market reaction to CoreWeave's results and to feedback from Anthropic's IPO campaign. The context the article gave was a market in which Nvidia earnings and the Anthropic IPO were both approaching, and it noted related headlines about a shaky rally and tumbling Bitcoin. It did not say what happens next beyond those looming events, and it offered no further detail on timing or numbers.

Articles.Title: Are AI Bulls Back? Looks Like It Thanks To Anthropic, CoreWeave, Nvidia - Investor's Business Daily

stories.Headline: ModelOp and Coralogix each report being named Market Shapers in a Gartner AI FinOps quadrant
stories.Summary:
ModelOp announced on November 12, 2026 that it was positioned as a Market Shaper in the Gartner Emerging Market Quadrant for AI FinOps Tools - Startup Vendors, published October 28, 2026. The announcement came from Park City, Utah, where ModelOp is based. ModelOp is one of four vendors positioned in the Market Shapers quadrant among 18 vendors recognized in the report. Coralogix announced on November 12, 2026 that it was recognized as a Market Shaper in the same Gartner Emerging Market Quadrant for AI FinOps Tools - Startup Vendors. Coralogix made its announcement from Boston.

Gartner's Emerging Market Quadrant examines vendors in rapidly evolving technology markets, assessing Potential for Market Disruption and Potential to Execute. Gartner defines AI FinOps tools as solutions that measure, attribute, forecast, control and optimize AI costs. The report characterizes Market Shapers as vendors with strong cost optimization insights and automation pursuing end-to-end proactive AI cost management. The report was authored by Ray Collins, Adam Ronthal, Marco Meinardi and Nitish Tyagi and published October 28, 2026. In June 2026, ModelOp was named a Visionary in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Governance Platforms, and in the accompanying Critical Capabilities for AI Governance Platforms report it received the highest score for the AI Agent Governance use case.

Dave Trier, CEO of ModelOp, said enterprise AI is facing a financial accountability crisis, with companies deploying more AI models and autonomous agents than ever before. He said counting tokens and tracking invoices does not tell a CEO or CFO how they impact specific business use cases or whether those investments are paying off. He said the real question is not how much AI is consumed but what business value comes from specific use cases. He said ModelOp connects AI costs directly to the use case, the business owner and the expected outcome. He said AI FinOps has to be part of how enterprises govern and operate AI, not another dashboard added after the fact.

Ariel Assaraf, CEO and co-founder of Coralogix, said AI is fundamentally changing the economics of running modern software. He said that as organizations deploy more autonomous agents, understanding what those systems are doing, how they are performing and what they are costing becomes increasingly important. He said AI spending cannot be effectively managed without visibility into the systems and workflows driving it. He said Coralogix believes its recognition reflects the growing importance of connecting AI observability with the financial accountability enterprises need. He added that the next phase of AI cost management will require organizations to understand the economics of their AI systems at a much deeper level.

Gartner said the emerging market is increasingly shifting beyond cost reporting toward AI economics management. Gartner also said organizations must connect token consumption, compute and other costs to measurable business outcomes. ModelOp's platform serves Fortune 500 and Global 2000 organizations and links AI consumption to business ownership, governance and operational intelligence. Coralogix's capabilities include budget controls, consumption forecasting and automated safeguards against unexpected spending. In one customer deployment, a global professional services firm uses Coralogix to monitor approximately 19,500 coding-agent users.

ModelOp has been building its enterprise AI delivery and governance foundation since 2018, with capabilities spanning AI lifecycle automation, risk management, policy enforcement, operational monitoring and AI FinOps. ModelOp's AI FinOps capabilities are delivered through its Enterprise AI Command Center and powered by the ModelOp AI Delivery Engine (MADE). ModelOp integrates with technologies including Microsoft Agent 365, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Quick, OpenAI and Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based tools. Coralogix is built on a streaming-first architecture and brings together logs, metrics, traces and AI observability capabilities. Coralogix's platform includes Olly, its built-in AI investigator, along with MCP and CLI interfaces for agent-based workflows.

ModelOp's placement follows two earlier Gartner research recognitions in 2026, and ModelOp said it believes these inclusions reflect its vision that governance, use case delivery and financial accountability should operate together. Coralogix said it continues to invest in AI-native observability, real-time data infrastructure and autonomous investigation capabilities. The full Coralogix report is available for download at coralogix.com. ModelOp directed readers to modelop.com for information about its AI FinOps capabilities and to its blog. The articles leave open which of the 18 recognized vendors occupy the other quadrants and how the four Market Shapers compare with one another.

stories.Headline: Software engineer Hugo Venturini says humans stay accountable for AI-written code
stories.Summary:
Hugo Venturini, a software engineer, spoke to Shane Hastie of InfoQ about accountability when AI writes code, in a podcast published on 13 November 2026. Venturini said he defended his PhD on the debugging of optimized code in 2008 and later worked as a manager at Meta, where he was accountable for the type checker and compiler of the Hack language. He said he was later CTO of Qwant, the search engine, with 90 people from network engineers to AI researchers, and now works at a startup that deals with tooling for AI. He said AI is a powerful tool but humans remain accountable for the decisions it makes possible and the code it produces. He said he still has wow moments several times a week, but if the tool fails, the person conducting it is accountable.

Venturini said pull requests have been growing for years and AI did not create the review-scale problem. He described stories of 2000-line pull requests and a senior engineer with a backlog of over 300 pull requests, each hundreds of lines long, waiting to be reviewed. He said teams should apply the same trust-based judgement about what needs reviewing that worked before AI, and his own team does not review everything. He said he worked with Microsoft in 2014 when it merged the software engineer branch with the testers branch, which raised quality by making engineers accountable for the whole product. He said AI risks reversing that gain if people blame the tool instead of owning outcomes.

Venturini said humans are in charge and should be accountable, and that AI is just another tool. He said doing the right thing means solving the problem to a user, and at every step doing the right thing of that step. He said code has to be right to the colon, the semi-colon and the character, and that proper tooling can tell the AI how to loop and give the right feedback. He said cultures of transparency, honest no-blame Q&As, anonymous questions and naming solutions rather than people let people dare to take accountability. He said this can start at any level of the organisation, not just the top.

Hastie said studies point to pull requests getting bigger and bigger. Venturini said some people play a game of the wow effect, claiming to have rewritten an entire big product in only one diff, which he called just for the show. He said at his group of engineers, anyone doing this was told to help others review the code. He said he has no good answer on how to review for the number of diffs and is eager for anyone to tell him how. He said AI collapses traditional role boundaries of product manager, architect and tester, pushing engineers to ask better questions, a skill that defines seniority and that organisations need to deliberately teach.

Venturini said the size of pull requests was already a problem before AI. He said boilerplate could already be automated before AI, and if code compiles, passes the tests and behaves as wanted, you may not need to review it. He said he lived in an organisation where people did not need a signature on every diff, trusting senior people to merge and be accountable for fixing anything that went wrong. He said the heart of the product needs review for quality and for sharing knowledge, while boilerplate can be merged. He said he has seen software lacking quality over the last month and read in the press that those people are massively using AI.

Venturini said he would like to know what feedback he can give to get those people back on quality. He said the difference today is that roles are merging again but quality is not rising yet, because people still blame the AI and do not feel accountable for what the tooling does. He said this is something leaders, managers, colleagues and users need to work on. Hastie said the question of how others handle review volume would be left open for the audience to respond. Hastie also asked about the architect as roles collapse, and the articles give no answer from Venturini to that question.

stories.Headline: Apple releases Siri AI developer preview to let apps integrate with the assistant
stories.Summary:
Apple released the Siri AI Developer Preview in the 27.3 beta releases of its operating systems, which lets developers and apps integrate with the assistant and hand off actions to it. During the preview, access to Siri AI is restricted to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers. Apple describes Siri AI as an entirely new version of its assistant that is profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal. The preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, which makes it easier for all apps to tap into the newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, and natural language.

These capabilities let users make natural language requests and have Siri AI carry out any custom action the app supports. The framework also supports complex requests through Skills, a new feature that lets developers teach Siri AI how to combine several actions into a single experience. If a request does not name an app, it is automatically routed to the app currently in the foreground, the app associated with an active Live Activity, or the app previously mentioned in the ongoing conversation. An app running in the background receives only requests that explicitly mention its name, and requests can also include actions across apps, such as finding content in one app, sending it to another, and performing an action there.

Apple says all Apple Intelligence features, including Siri AI, may be subject to usage limits, with extended, premium access planned for the future. Developers based in the EU should be aware that Siri AI is currently unavailable in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS. One user who tested the preview said that with a good description on the intent and parameters, Siri can figure it out, and called it what Siri should have been all along. Another user said doing it via App Intents was the right move, comparing it to Google's AppFunctions and noting that Google instead made a separate agent skills SDK that developers have to implement.

stories.Headline: Australia’s seat belt mandate shows how built-in safeguards cut road deaths and can guide AI security
stories.Summary:
Australia's experience with road safety shows how engineered protections can work alongside human accountability, according to an article published by IT Brief Australia on 13 November 2026. By 1970 faster vehicle speeds had pushed the annual road toll in Victoria alone to 1061, a level that public education and traffic rules could not address. In 1970 Victoria became the first jurisdiction in the world to make wearing seat belts mandatory. Seat belts were later supplemented with airbags, crumple zones and other safety features built directly into every car. That combination of engineered controls and driver training saw Victoria's annual road toll decline by more than 70 per cent over the next three decades.

The article argues that managing AI security risks now requires a similar shift from rules governing how technology is used to protections built into the technology itself. Regulatory guidelines set necessary boundaries, but they cannot stop an attack that tricks an AI system into following malicious instructions or halt a breach already in progress. The challenge grows when AI systems can act autonomously across multiple government systems, and the article says Australia is seeing rapid evolution of software that acts autonomously and with authority. The fundamental governance question for Australian leaders is no longer about controlling what software can see but about governing what software is authorised to do. The article says the Australian Federal Government parliamentary inquiry into Artificial Intelligence has made clear that acknowledging the risks of autonomous, rogue AI agents after a breach is not sufficient.

The article says organisations must rethink security practices, because autonomous AI agents can be tricked into revealing sensitive information, impersonating legitimate users or taking actions they were never authorised to perform. Traditional cybersecurity tools were not designed to manage these threats, and manual approvals and periodic audits cannot keep pace as adversaries use AI to compress attack timelines from days down to minutes. Modern AI applications are rarely built from scratch and are assembled from models, data and software components developed by numerous third parties, each of which can introduce its own security risks. The article says AI models and the tools they use must be checked before deployment, with their behaviour continuously monitored as systems evolve. It adds that under expert human supervision, advanced AI systems can help cybersecurity teams discover weaknesses, understand how attackers might exploit them and rapidly put protections in place.

The article says government policy must facilitate early, managed access to cutting-edge frontier models for national defenders, security researchers and critical infrastructure operators before those models are broadly deployed. It says Australia's AI Safety Institute has an important role in evaluating emerging risks, and that its role should extend to helping government agencies, security researchers and critical infrastructure operators safely access advanced AI capabilities for defensive purposes. The article draws a parallel with the mandated use of seat belts, which it says saw Australia lead the world in vehicular safety half a century ago, and says the country now has the opportunity to set a global standard for secure AI adoption. It says Australia can achieve the same balance between innovation and safety by building security into AI systems from the outset, adopting continuous technical safeguards, giving defenders timely access to advanced AI capabilities and ensuring those protecting critical systems can respond as quickly as attackers. The article says the recommendations from Parliament's inquiry provide an opportunity to ensure governance frameworks and technical defences keep pace with the technology itself.

Articles.Title: Built-in Protection: How Australia's Public Safety History Can Guide the AI Era - IT Brief Australia
